causes: Common causative organisms include Bartonella species (especially B. henselae), Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Escherichia coli. Predisposing factors include pre-existing valvular disease, immunosuppression (e.g., FIV/FeLV infection), dental disease, and chronic infections that serve as sources of bacteremia. Invasive procedures such as surgery or catheterization may also introduce bacteria into the bloodstream.

name: Cardiovascular Fungal Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms (commonly Aspergillus, Cryptococcus, or Histoplasma species) disseminate hematogenously and colonize the cardiovascular system, including the endocardium, myocardium, and great vessels. This leads to fungal endocarditis, myocarditis, or vasculitis with formation of vegetative lesions, thromboembolism, and progressive cardiac dysfunction. The resulting inflammatory response and tissue destruction can cause valvular insufficiency, arrhythmias, and systemic embolization to other organs.
pathophysiology_ja: 真菌（主にアスペルギルス、クリプトコッカス、ヒストプラズマなど）が血行性に播種し、心内膜、心筋、大血管などの心血管系に定着します。これにより真菌性心内膜炎、心筋炎、または血管炎が生じ、疣贅性病変の形成、血栓塞栓症、進行性の心機能障害を引き起こします。炎症反応と組織破壊により弁膜不全、不整脈、全身性塞栓症が生じる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include systemic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Cryptococcus neoformans, Histoplasma capsulatum, Blastomyces dermatitidis, or Coccidioides immitis that disseminate to the cardiovascular system. Secondary causes and risk factors include immunosuppression (FIV, FeLV infection, prolonged corticosteroid use), chronic debilitating diseases, and pre-existing cardiac valve damage that facilitates fungal colonization.

name: Cardiovascular Infection (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular infections in cats involve microbial colonization of the heart valves (endocarditis), myocardium (myocarditis), or pericardium (pericarditis), leading to valvular dysfunction, cardiac inflammation, and potential septic embolization to distant organs. Bacterial agents such as Bartonella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Staphylococcus spp. are common causative organisms that adhere to damaged or inflamed endothelial surfaces, forming vegetative lesions. This results in progressive cardiac dysfunction, thromboembolic events, and systemic inflammatory response.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管感染症は、心臓弁（心内膜炎）、心筋（心筋炎）、または心膜（心膜炎）への微生物の定着により、弁機能不全、心臓の炎症、および遠隔臓器への敗血症性塞栓を引き起こす。Bartonella属、Streptococcus属、Staphylococcus属などの細菌が損傷または炎症を起こした内皮表面に付着し、疣贅性病変を形成する。これにより進行性の心機能障害、血栓塞栓症、および全身性炎症反応が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (Bartonella henselae, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., E. coli), with Bartonella being the most common agent in feline endocarditis. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include pre-existing valvular disease, immunosuppression (e.g., FIV or FeLV infection), dental disease, chronic infections, and invasive medical procedures such as intravenous catheterization. Fungal agents are rare but may occur in immunocompromised cats.

name: Cardiovascular Inflammation (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular inflammation in cats involves inflammatory infiltration of the heart and/or blood vessel walls (myocarditis, endocarditis, pericarditis, or vasculitis), leading to impaired cardiac function, valvular damage, arrhythmias, and potentially thromboembolic events. Inflammatory mediators cause tissue edema, necrosis, and fibrosis, resulting in reduced cardiac output, congestive heart failure, or vascular compromise. Immune-mediated mechanisms or direct pathogen invasion disrupt normal myocardial and endothelial cell function.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管炎症は、心筋炎、心内膜炎、心膜炎、または血管炎として心臓や血管壁への炎症性細胞浸潤を伴い、心機能障害、弁膜損傷、不整脈、血栓塞栓症を引き起こす。炎症性メディエーターが組織の浮腫、壊死、線維化を引き起こし、心拍出量の低下やうっ血性心不全につながる。免疫介在性機序または病原体の直接侵入により正常な心筋および内皮細胞機能が障害される。
causes: Primary causes include infectious agents such as Bartonella henselae, feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) coronavirus, Toxoplasma gondii, and bacterial septicemia leading to endocarditis. Secondary causes include immune-mediated diseases, chronic kidney disease-associated inflammation, and extension of systemic inflammatory conditions. Idiopathic myocarditis and endomyocarditis of unknown etiology are also recognized in cats.

name: Cardiovascular Neoplasia (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular neoplasia in cats involves abnormal proliferation of cells within the heart, great vessels, or pericardium. The most common types include lymphoma, hemangiosarcoma, and chemodectoma, which can cause pericardial effusion, cardiac tamponade, arrhythmias, and impaired cardiac output. Tumor growth may obstruct blood flow, invade myocardium, or metastasize to other organs, leading to progressive cardiovascular compromise.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管系腫瘍は、心臓、大血管、または心膜内の細胞の異常増殖を伴う。最も一般的な腫瘍にはリンパ腫、血管肉腫、化学受容器腫瘍があり、心嚢液貯留、心タンポナーデ、不整脈、心拍出量低下を引き起こす。腫瘍の成長は血流を阻害し、心筋に浸潤し、他の臓器に転移することで進行性の心血管機能障害をもたらす。
causes: The exact etiology is often unknown, but lymphoma (the most common cardiac tumor in cats) may be associated with feline leukemia virus (FeLV) infection. Genetic predisposition and chronic immune dysregulation may also contribute. Other tumor types such as hemangiosarcoma and mesothelioma arise spontaneously without clearly identified risk factors.

name: Cardiovascular Metabolic Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular metabolic disease in cats involves the interplay between metabolic derangements (such as obesity, diabetes mellitus, hyperthyroidism, or dyslipidemia) and cardiovascular dysfunction. Metabolic disturbances lead to myocardial remodeling, systemic hypertension, increased cardiac workload, and endothelial dysfunction, ultimately resulting in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, congestive heart failure, or thromboembolic events. Chronic metabolic stress promotes oxidative damage, inflammation, and fibrosis within the myocardium.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管代謝疾患は、肥満、糖尿病、甲状腺機能亢進症、脂質異常症などの代謝異常と心血管機能障害の相互作用により発症します。代謝障害は心筋リモデリング、全身性高血圧、心臓負荷の増大、血管内皮機能障害を引き起こし、最終的に肥大型心筋症、うっ血性心不全、血栓塞栓症に至ります。慢性的な代謝ストレスは心筋における酸化障害、炎症、線維化を促進します。
causes: Primary causes include hyperthyroidism (most common endocrine cause of secondary cardiac disease in cats), obesity, diabetes mellitus, and systemic hypertension. Secondary causes include chronic kidney disease leading to hypertension and cardiac remodeling, hyperaldosteronism, and nutritional deficiencies such as taurine deficiency causing dilated cardiomyopathy.

name: Cardiovascular Nutritional Deficiency (Cat)
pathophysiology: Deficiency of essential nutrients, primarily taurine, leads to impaired myocardial function in cats. Taurine is critical for calcium channel regulation, antioxidant defense, and maintenance of cardiac muscle contractility. Prolonged deficiency results in dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) with progressive ventricular dilation, reduced systolic function, and potential congestive heart failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 必須栄養素、特にタウリンの欠乏により、猫の心筋機能が障害されます。タウリンはカルシウムチャネルの調節、抗酸化防御、および心筋収縮力の維持に不可欠です。長期的な欠乏は拡張型心筋症（DCM）を引き起こし、心室拡大、収縮機能低下、およびうっ血性心不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is dietary taurine deficiency, as cats cannot synthesize sufficient taurine endogenously and require it from their diet. Secondary causes include feeding improperly formulated commercial diets, exclusive home-cooked or vegetarian diets lacking taurine supplementation, and malabsorptive gastrointestinal conditions that impair taurine absorption. Other nutritional deficiencies such as carnitine, selenium, or vitamin E may also contribute to cardiovascular dysfunction.

name: Cardiovascular Genetic Disorder (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular genetic disorders in cats most commonly manifest as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), involving mutations in genes encoding sarcomeric proteins (e.g., MYBPC3), leading to myocardial hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, and impaired ventricular filling. Progressive fibrosis and myocardial disarray result in congestive heart failure, arterial thromboembolism, or sudden cardiac death. Other genetic cardiovascular conditions include dilated cardiomyopathy and arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, though these are less common.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管遺伝性疾患は、最も一般的に肥大型心筋症（HCM）として発現し、サルコメアタンパク質をコードする遺伝子（例：MYBPC3）の変異により心筋肥大、拡張機能障害、心室充満障害を引き起こす。進行性の線維化と心筋錯綜配列により、うっ血性心不全、動脈血栓塞栓症、または突然死に至る。拡張型心筋症や不整脈源性右室心筋症などの他の遺伝性心血管疾患も存在するが、頻度は低い。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, most notably autosomal dominant mutations in the MYBPC3 gene identified in Maine Coon and Ragdoll breeds. Other breeds such as British Shorthair, Sphynx, Persian, and Bengal cats also have breed-specific genetic predispositions. Polygenic inheritance and gene-environment interactions may modify disease expression and severity.

name: Cardiovascular Autoimmune Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: The immune system erroneously targets cardiac tissues, including myocardial cells, endocardium, or vascular endothelium, leading to inflammation, fibrosis, and progressive cardiac dysfunction. Autoantibodies and autoreactive T-cells mediate damage to the heart muscle and blood vessels, potentially resulting in myocarditis, pericarditis, or vasculitis. Chronic immune-mediated inflammation can lead to dilated cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, and congestive heart failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が心筋細胞、心内膜、または血管内皮を誤って攻撃し、炎症、線維化、および進行性の心機能障害を引き起こします。自己抗体および自己反応性T細胞が心筋や血管に損傷を与え、心筋炎、心膜炎、または血管炎を引き起こす可能性があります。慢性的な免疫介在性炎症は拡張型心筋症、不整脈、およびうっ血性心不全に至ることがあります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against cardiac antigens, potentially triggered by viral infections (such as feline coronavirus or parvovirus), molecular mimicry, or genetic predisposition. Secondary factors include chronic inflammatory conditions, concurrent autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus), and environmental stressors that may exacerbate immune-mediated cardiac damage.

name: Cardiovascular Degenerative Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular degenerative disease in cats involves progressive structural deterioration of cardiac valves (most commonly the mitral and aortic valves) and/or myocardial tissue due to age-related fibrosis, myxomatous degeneration, and collagen breakdown. This leads to valvular insufficiency, impaired cardiac output, volume overload, and eventual congestive heart failure. Secondary changes include atrial dilation, myocardial remodeling, and potential thromboembolic complications due to blood stasis.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管変性疾患は、加齢に伴う線維化、粘液腫様変性、コラーゲン分解により心臓弁（主に僧帽弁および大動脈弁）や心筋組織が進行性に構造的劣化を起こす疾患です。これにより弁閉鎖不全、心拍出量の低下、容量負荷が生じ、最終的にうっ血性心不全に至ります。二次的変化として心房拡大、心筋リモデリング、血液うっ滞による血栓塞栓症のリスクが増大します。
causes: The primary cause is age-related degenerative changes in cardiac valves and myocardium, with increased prevalence in geriatric cats. Secondary contributing factors include chronic hypertension (often associated with chronic kidney disease or hyperthyroidism), obesity, chronic taurine deficiency, and genetic predisposition in certain breeds.

name: Cardiovascular Traumatic Injury (Cat)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the thorax causes direct damage to the heart, great vessels, or pericardium. This can result in myocardial contusion, cardiac tamponade from hemopericardium, traumatic arrhythmias, or vascular rupture leading to hemorrhagic shock. Secondary inflammation and reperfusion injury may further compromise cardiac function in the hours following the initial insult.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性の胸部外傷により、心臓、大血管、または心膜に直接的な損傷が生じます。これにより心筋挫傷、心嚢血腫による心タンポナーデ、外傷性不整脈、または血管破裂による出血性ショックが引き起こされます。二次的な炎症や再灌流障害が、初期損傷後数時間にわたり心機能をさらに悪化させる可能性があります。
causes: The most common causes include high-rise syndrome (falls from height), motor vehicle trauma, and bite wounds from other animals. Less frequent causes include penetrating injuries from foreign objects, iatrogenic injury during thoracic procedures, and blunt force impacts. Underlying coagulopathies or pre-existing cardiac disease may exacerbate the severity of injury.
causes_ja: 最も一般的な原因は高所落下症候群（高所からの転落）、交通事故、および他の動物による咬傷です。稀な原因として異物による穿通性損傷、胸部処置中の医原性損傷、鈍的衝撃があります。基礎疾患としての凝固障害や既存の心疾患が損傷の重症度を悪化させることがあります。

name: Cardiovascular Behavioral Disorder (Cat)
pathophysiology: Stress-induced sympathetic nervous system activation leads to excessive catecholamine release, causing tachycardia, hypertension, and arrhythmias in cats. Chronic behavioral stress (fear, anxiety, territorial conflict) triggers sustained cardiovascular responses including myocardial remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, and potential stress cardiomyopathy. This neurohumoral dysregulation creates a cycle where cardiovascular changes further exacerbate behavioral disturbances.
pathophysiology_ja: ストレスによる交感神経系の活性化がカテコラミンの過剰分泌を引き起こし、頻脈、高血圧、不整脈を生じます。慢性的な行動学的ストレス（恐怖、不安、縄張り争い）が持続的な心血管反応を誘発し、心筋リモデリング、内皮機能障害、ストレス性心筋症を引き起こす可能性があります。この神経液性調節の異常が心血管変化と行動障害の悪循環を生み出します。
causes: Primary causes include chronic environmental stress, anxiety disorders, fear-based behavioral conditions, and inadequate socialization. Secondary causes involve inter-cat aggression, confinement stress, sudden environmental changes, and separation anxiety. Predisposing factors include genetic temperament, lack of environmental enrichment, and coexisting medical conditions such as hyperthyroidism.

name: Cardiovascular Infectious Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular infectious diseases in cats involve pathogen invasion of the heart and vascular structures, most commonly causing infective endocarditis (bacterial colonization of heart valves), myocarditis, or pericarditis. Organisms such as Bartonella henselae, streptococci, staphylococci, and less commonly fungi or viruses damage endothelial surfaces, promote thrombus and vegetation formation, and may lead to valvular insufficiency, embolic events, and progressive heart failure. Systemic inflammatory responses and immune-mediated damage further contribute to myocardial dysfunction and vascular compromise.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管感染症は、病原体が心臓や血管構造に侵入し、感染性心内膜炎（心臓弁への細菌定着）、心筋炎、心膜炎を引き起こします。Bartonella henselae、連鎖球菌、ブドウ球菌などの病原体が内皮表面を損傷し、血栓や疣贅の形成を促進し、弁膜不全、塞栓症、進行性心不全を引き起こす可能性があります。全身性の炎症反応と免疫介在性障害が心筋機能障害および血管障害をさらに悪化させます。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (most notably Bartonella henselae, Staphylococcus spp., Streptococcus spp., and E. coli), with Bartonella being a leading cause of feline infective endocarditis. Secondary predisposing factors include pre-existing valvular disease, immunosuppression (e.g., FIV or FeLV co-infection), dental disease causing bacteremia, and indwelling catheters or surgical procedures. Flea infestation is a major risk factor for Bartonella transmission.

name: Cardiovascular Parasitic Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular parasitic disease in cats is most commonly caused by Dirofilaria immitis (heartworm), which resides in the pulmonary arteries and occasionally the right heart. The presence of adult worms and subsequent worm death triggers severe pulmonary vascular inflammation, endothelial damage, villous endarteritis, and thromboembolism. Even a small worm burden (1-3 worms) can cause significant pulmonary hypertension, right-sided heart failure, and potentially fatal acute lung injury (HARD: Heartworm Associated Respiratory Disease) in cats.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管寄生虫疾患は主にDirofilaria immitis（犬糸状虫）によって引き起こされ、成虫は肺動脈および時に右心に寄生します。成虫の存在およびその死滅により、重度の肺血管炎症、内皮障害、絨毛性動脈内膜炎、および血栓塞栓症が誘発されます。猫では少数の虫体（1〜3匹）でも重大な肺高血圧症、右心不全、および致死的な急性肺障害（HARD：フィラリア関連呼吸器疾患）を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is infection with Dirofilaria immitis transmitted via mosquito bite; infective L3 larvae migrate through subcutaneous tissues and eventually reach the pulmonary vasculature. Less commonly, other parasites such as Aelurostrongylus abstrusus (lungworm with cardiovascular involvement) or aberrant migration of other helminths may affect the cardiovascular system. Risk factors include outdoor access, geographic regions with high mosquito prevalence, and lack of preventive medication.

name: Cardiovascular Viral Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as feline parvovirus (FPV) can infect myocardial cells, particularly in neonatal kittens, causing myocarditis, myocardial necrosis, and subsequent cardiac dysfunction. Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) coronavirus can also cause vasculitis and pericardial/myocardial inflammation through immune-mediated mechanisms. These viral insults lead to impaired cardiac contractility, arrhythmias, congestive heart failure, or pericardial effusion.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫パルボウイルス（FPV）は特に新生子猫の心筋細胞に感染し、心筋炎・心筋壊死を引き起こし心機能障害をもたらす。猫伝染性腹膜炎（FIP）コロナウイルスも免疫介在性に血管炎や心膜・心筋の炎症を引き起こす。これらのウイルス障害により心収縮力低下、不整脈、うっ血性心不全、または心嚢水貯留が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include feline parvovirus (panleukopenia virus) causing neonatal myocarditis, and feline coronavirus (FIP) causing myocarditis, pericarditis, and vasculitis. Secondary factors include immunosuppression from feline leukemia virus (FeLV) or feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV), which may predispose to opportunistic viral myocardial damage.

name: Cardiovascular Bacterial Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Bacteria enter the bloodstream through wounds, dental disease, or other infections, leading to bacteremia and potential colonization of cardiac structures such as heart valves (infective endocarditis). Bacterial colonization causes valvular damage, vegetation formation, and inflammatory responses that impair cardiac function. Septic emboli may disseminate to other organs, causing secondary infections and multi-organ dysfunction.
pathophysiology_ja: 細菌が創傷、歯科疾患、またはその他の感染症を通じて血流に侵入し、菌血症および心臓弁などの心血管構造への定着（感染性心内膜炎）を引き起こします。細菌の定着は弁の損傷、疣贅形成、および炎症反応を引き起こし、心機能を障害します。敗血症性塞栓が他の臓器に播種し、二次感染や多臓器不全を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Bartonella henselae (most frequent in cats), Staphylococcus spp., Streptococcus spp., and Escherichia coli. Predisposing factors include pre-existing valvular disease, immunosuppression (e.g., FIV/FeLV infection), chronic dental disease, and indwelling catheters. Flea infestation is a major risk factor for Bartonella-associated endocarditis.

name: Cardiovascular Fungal Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms (commonly Aspergillus, Cryptococcus, or dimorphic fungi such as Histoplasma or Blastomyces) disseminate hematogenously and colonize cardiovascular structures including the myocardium, endocardium, and great vessels. This leads to granulomatous or pyogranulomatous inflammation, vegetative endocarditis, myocardial necrosis, and potential thromboembolic complications. Progressive cardiac dysfunction, valvular insufficiency, and systemic dissemination may result in congestive heart failure or multi-organ involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 真菌（主にアスペルギルス、クリプトコッカス、またはヒストプラズマ・ブラストミセスなどの二形性真菌）が血行性に播種し、心筋、心内膜、大血管などの心血管構造に定着します。これにより肉芽腫性または化膿性肉芽腫性炎症、疣贅性心内膜炎、心筋壊死、血栓塞栓性合併症が生じます。進行すると心機能不全、弁膜症、うっ血性心不全や多臓器障害に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include systemic infection by fungi such as Cryptococcus neoformans, Aspergillus spp., Histoplasma capsulatum, and Blastomyces dermatitidis that disseminate to the cardiovascular system. Secondary causes include immunosuppression due to FIV, FeLV infection, prolonged corticosteroid use, or other debilitating diseases that predispose cats to opportunistic fungal infections.

name: Cardiovascular Infection (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular infections in cats involve microbial colonization of the heart valves (endocarditis), myocardium (myocarditis), or pericardium (pericarditis), leading to valvular destruction, impaired cardiac function, and potential septic embolization to distant organs. Bacterial, viral (such as FIP coronavirus), or rarely fungal organisms trigger inflammatory responses causing tissue damage, valvular insufficiency, and possible congestive heart failure. Immune-mediated mechanisms and thromboembolic complications further contribute to multi-organ dysfunction.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管感染症は、心臓弁（心内膜炎）、心筋（心筋炎）、または心膜（心膜炎）への微生物の定着を伴い、弁の破壊、心機能障害、および遠隔臓器への敗血症性塞栓を引き起こす。細菌、ウイルス（FIPコロナウイルスなど）、まれに真菌が炎症反応を誘発し、組織損傷、弁閉鎖不全、うっ血性心不全を引き起こす。免疫介在性機序および血栓塞栓性合併症が多臓器不全をさらに悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (Bartonella henselae, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., E. coli), viral infections (feline infectious peritonitis virus, feline parvovirus), and rarely fungal organisms. Secondary causes include immunosuppression (FIV, FeLV), pre-existing cardiac disease or valvular abnormalities, dental disease causing bacteremia, and invasive procedures such as IV catheterization.

name: Cardiovascular Inflammation (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular inflammation in cats involves inflammatory infiltration of the heart and/or blood vessels (myocarditis, endocarditis, pericarditis, or vasculitis), leading to impaired cardiac function, valvular dysfunction, or vascular compromise. Inflammatory mediators cause tissue damage, fibrosis, and potential arrhythmias. This can result in decreased cardiac output, thromboembolism, and congestive heart failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管炎症は、心筋炎、心内膜炎、心膜炎、または血管炎として心臓や血管への炎症性細胞浸潤を伴い、心機能障害、弁膜機能不全、または血管障害を引き起こします。炎症性メディエーターが組織損傷や線維化、不整脈を誘発します。その結果、心拍出量の低下、血栓塞栓症、およびうっ血性心不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include infectious agents such as Bartonella henselae, feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) coronavirus, toxoplasmosis, and bacterial endocarditis. Secondary causes include immune-mediated diseases, systemic inflammatory conditions, and drug or toxin-related myocardial injury. Idiopathic myocarditis is also recognized in cats.

name: Cardiovascular Neoplasia (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular neoplasia in cats involves abnormal proliferation of cells within the heart, great vessels, or pericardium. The most common types include lymphoma, hemangiosarcoma, and chemodectoma, which can cause pericardial effusion, cardiac tamponade, arrhythmias, and impaired cardiac output. Tumor growth may obstruct blood flow, invade the myocardium, or metastasize to other organs, leading to progressive cardiovascular compromise.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管系腫瘍は、心臓、大血管、または心膜内の細胞の異常増殖を伴います。最も一般的な腫瘍にはリンパ腫、血管肉腫、化学受容器腫瘍があり、心嚢液貯留、心タンポナーデ、不整脈、心拍出量の低下を引き起こします。腫瘍の増殖は血流を妨げ、心筋に浸潤し、他臓器に転移することで進行性の心血管障害をもたらします。
causes: The exact etiology is often unknown, but lymphoma (the most common cardiac tumor in cats) is frequently associated with feline leukemia virus (FeLV) infection. Genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and environmental carcinogens may also contribute. Other tumor types such as hemangiosarcoma and metastatic carcinomas may arise spontaneously or secondary to systemic neoplastic disease.

name: Cardiovascular Metabolic Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular metabolic disease in cats involves the interplay between metabolic derangements (such as hyperthyroidism, diabetes mellitus, obesity, or chronic kidney disease) and secondary cardiovascular dysfunction, including myocardial hypertrophy, systemic hypertension, and impaired cardiac output. Metabolic disturbances lead to volume overload, increased peripheral vascular resistance, neurohormonal activation, and oxidative stress, which progressively damage the myocardium and vasculature. This results in conditions such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy secondary to hyperthyroidism or hypertensive cardiomyopathy associated with renal disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管代謝疾患は、甲状腺機能亢進症、糖尿病、肥満、慢性腎臓病などの代謝異常と、それに続く心筋肥大、全身性高血圧、心拍出量低下などの心血管機能障害の相互作用を伴います。代謝障害は容量負荷の増大、末梢血管抵抗の上昇、神経体液性因子の活性化、酸化ストレスを引き起こし、心筋および血管を進行性に障害します。これにより甲状腺機能亢進症に続発する肥大型心筋症や腎疾患に関連する高血圧性心筋症などが生じます。
causes: Primary causes include hyperthyroidism (most common in older cats), systemic hypertension secondary to chronic kidney disease, obesity-related metabolic syndrome, and diabetes mellitus causing endothelial dysfunction. Secondary causes include electrolyte imbalances (hypokalemia, hyperphosphatemia), anemia-induced high-output cardiac states, and chronic inflammatory conditions that promote vascular remodeling and myocardial fibrosis.

name: Cardiovascular Nutritional Deficiency (Cat)
pathophysiology: Taurine deficiency is the primary nutritional cause of cardiovascular disease in cats, leading to dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). Taurine is essential for myocardial cell function, calcium regulation, and contractility; its deficiency causes progressive myocardial failure with chamber dilation and reduced systolic function. Secondary effects include congestive heart failure with pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, and potential thromboembolism.
pathophysiology_ja: タウリン欠乏が猫における心血管疾患の主な栄養性原因であり、拡張型心筋症（DCM）を引き起こします。タウリンは心筋細胞の機能、カルシウム調節、および収縮力に不可欠であり、その欠乏は心筋の進行性不全、心腔拡大、および収縮機能低下を引き起こします。二次的な影響として、肺水腫、胸水貯留、および血栓塞栓症を伴ううっ血性心不全が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is dietary taurine deficiency, as cats cannot synthesize sufficient taurine endogenously and require it as an essential amino acid. Secondary causes include feeding taurine-deficient commercial diets (historically common before supplementation standards), exclusive homemade diets lacking taurine, or diets heavily processed with heat that degrades taurine content. Other nutritional deficiencies such as L-carnitine, selenium, or vitamin E may also contribute to myocardial dysfunction.

name: Cardiovascular Genetic Disorder (Cat)
pathophysiology: Genetic mutations affecting cardiac structural proteins (such as myosin-binding protein C in Maine Coons and Ragdolls) lead to abnormal myocardial architecture, resulting in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), or other inherited cardiomyopathies. These mutations cause myocardial fiber disarray, fibrosis, diastolic dysfunction, and progressive ventricular remodeling, ultimately leading to congestive heart failure, thromboembolism, or sudden cardiac death.
pathophysiology_ja: 心筋構造タンパク質に影響を与える遺伝子変異（メインクーンやラグドールにおけるミオシン結合タンパクC変異など）が異常な心筋構造を引き起こし、肥大型心筋症（HCM）、拡張型心筋症（DCM）などの遺伝性心筋症を発症させる。これらの変異は心筋線維の錯綜配列、線維化、拡張機能障害、進行性の心室リモデリングを引き起こし、最終的にうっ血性心不全、血栓塞栓症、または突然死に至る。
causes: Primary causes include autosomal dominant genetic mutations such as MYBPC3 (A31P in Maine Coons, R820W in Ragdolls) causing HCM, and other unidentified mutations in breeds like British Shorthairs, Sphynx, and Persians. Secondary contributing factors include modifier genes, environmental stressors, obesity, and concurrent diseases such as hyperthyroidism or systemic hypertension that can exacerbate the genetic predisposition.

name: Cardiovascular Autoimmune Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: The immune system erroneously targets cardiac tissues, including myocardial cells, endocardium, or vascular endothelium, leading to inflammation, fibrosis, and progressive cardiac dysfunction. Autoantibodies and autoreactive T-cells mediate damage to the myocardium and/or coronary vasculature, resulting in myocarditis, pericarditis, or vasculitis. Chronic immune-mediated inflammation can lead to dilated cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, and congestive heart failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が心筋細胞、心内膜、または血管内皮を誤って攻撃し、炎症、線維化、および進行性の心機能障害を引き起こす。自己抗体および自己反応性T細胞が心筋や冠動脈血管に損傷を与え、心筋炎、心膜炎、または血管炎を引き起こす。慢性的な免疫介在性炎症は拡張型心筋症、不整脈、およびうっ血性心不全に至ることがある。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against cardiac antigens, potentially triggered by viral infections (e.g., feline parvovirus), molecular mimicry, or genetic predisposition. Secondary causes include chronic inflammatory conditions, concurrent autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus), or drug-induced immune reactions. Environmental stressors and co-infections such as FIV or FeLV may also predispose affected cats.

name: Cardiovascular Degenerative Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Progressive degenerative changes occur in the myocardium, cardiac valves, and/or vascular walls due to aging, chronic wear, or metabolic disturbances. Myxomatous degeneration of valve leaflets leads to valvular insufficiency and regurgitation, while myocardial fibrosis and arteriosclerosis reduce cardiac output and vascular compliance. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, resulting in congestive heart failure, arrhythmias, or thromboembolic events.
pathophysiology_ja: 加齢、慢性的な負荷、または代謝異常により、心筋、心臓弁、および/または血管壁に進行性の変性変化が生じる。弁尖の粘液腫様変性は弁閉鎖不全と逆流を引き起こし、心筋線維化や動脈硬化は心拍出量と血管コンプライアンスを低下させる。やがて代償機構が破綻し、うっ血性心不全、不整脈、または血栓塞栓症に至る。
causes: Primary causes include age-related degenerative changes of the myocardium and cardiac valves, chronic hypertension, and genetic predisposition in certain breeds. Secondary causes include chronic kidney disease, hyperthyroidism, diabetes mellitus, obesity, and chronic inflammatory or oxidative stress contributing to accelerated cardiovascular degeneration.
causes_ja: 主な原因として、加齢に伴う心筋および心臓弁の変性変化、慢性高血圧、特定の品種における遺伝的素因がある。二次的原因として、慢性腎臓病、甲状腺機能亢進症、糖尿病、肥満、および慢性炎症や酸化ストレスによる心血管変性の促進が挙げられる。

name: Cardiovascular Traumatic Injury (Cat)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the thorax causes direct damage to the heart, great vessels, or pericardium. This can result in myocardial contusion, cardiac tamponade from hemopericardium, vessel rupture, or traumatic arrhythmias. Secondary effects include decreased cardiac output, hemorrhagic shock, and potentially fatal circulatory collapse.
pathophysiology_ja: 胸部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、心臓、大血管、または心膜に直接的な損傷が生じます。心筋挫傷、心嚢血腫による心タンポナーデ、血管破裂、または外傷性不整脈を引き起こす可能性があります。二次的影響として心拍出量の低下、出血性ショック、致死的な循環不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Common causes include vehicular trauma (hit by car), falls from height (high-rise syndrome), bite wounds from other animals, and penetrating injuries such as impalement or gunshot wounds. Secondary causes include iatrogenic injury during thoracic procedures and blunt force from kicks or crush injuries.
causes_ja: 主な原因は交通事故（自動車との衝突）、高所からの落下（高層症候群）、他の動物による咬傷、刺創や銃創などの穿通性外傷です。二次的原因には胸部手術中の医原性損傷や、蹴りや圧挫損傷による鈍的外力が含まれます。
treatment: Immediate stabilization includes fluid resuscitation, oxygen supplementation, and pain management. Pericardiocentesis is performed for cardiac tamponade, and thoracotomy may be required for active hemorrhage or major vessel damage. Traumatic arrhythmias are managed with antiarrhythmic drugs such as lidocaine, and continuous ECG monitoring is essential during the critical period.

name: Cardiovascular Behavioral Disorder (Cat)
pathophysiology: Stress-induced sympathetic nervous system activation leads to excessive catecholamine release, causing tachycardia, hypertension, and potential myocardial damage in cats. Chronic behavioral stress can result in cardiac remodeling, arrhythmias, and a condition resembling stress cardiomyopathy (similar to Takotsubo-like syndrome). The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation contributes to sustained cardiovascular strain.
pathophysiology_ja: ストレスによる交感神経系の過剰な活性化がカテコラミンの過剰分泌を引き起こし、頻脈、高血圧、心筋障害をもたらします。慢性的な行動学的ストレスにより心臓のリモデリング、不整脈、ストレス性心筋症様の病態が生じることがあります。視床下部-下垂体-副腎軸の調節障害が持続的な心血管系への負荷に寄与します。
causes: Primary causes include chronic environmental stress, fear-based behavioral disorders, inter-cat conflict, and separation anxiety. Secondary causes may involve pre-existing cardiac conditions exacerbated by behavioral stress, confinement stress, and lack of environmental enrichment.
causes_ja: 主な原因は慢性的な環境ストレス、恐怖に基づく行動障害、猫同士の対立、分離不安です。二次的原因として、行動ストレスにより悪化する既存の心疾患、閉じ込めストレス、環境エンリッチメントの不足が挙げられます。

name: Cardiovascular Infectious Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Infectious agents such as bacteria (e.g., Bartonella spp.), viruses (e.g., FeLV, FIV), parasites (e.g., Dirofilaria immitis), and fungi colonize cardiovascular structures including the endocardium, myocardium, and pericardium. This leads to valvular vegetations (infective endocarditis), myocardial inflammation and necrosis, pericardial effusion, or vascular inflammation, resulting in impaired cardiac function, thromboembolic events, and potential systemic dissemination of infection. Progressive cardiac dysfunction may lead to congestive heart failure, arrhythmias, and multi-organ damage from septic emboli or reduced perfusion.
pathophysiology_ja: 細菌（バルトネラ属など）、ウイルス（FeLV、FIVなど）、寄生虫（犬糸状虫など）、真菌などの感染性病原体が心内膜、心筋、心膜などの心血管構造に定着します。これにより弁膜疣贅（感染性心内膜炎）、心筋炎・壊死、心膜液貯留、血管炎が生じ、心機能障害や血栓塞栓症、感染の全身播種を引き起こします。進行すると鬱血性心不全、不整脈、敗血症性塞栓による多臓器障害に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (Bartonella henselae, Staphylococcus spp., Streptococcus spp.), heartworm disease (Dirofilaria immitis), and viral infections (FeLV, FIV, FIP coronavirus). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, pre-existing valvular disease, dental disease providing a source of bacteremia, and indwelling intravenous catheters that facilitate hematogenous spread to the heart.

name: Cardiovascular Parasitic Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular parasitic disease in cats is most commonly caused by Dirofilaria immitis (heartworm), where infective larvae transmitted by mosquitoes migrate through tissues and mature in the pulmonary arteries. The adult worms cause pulmonary arterial inflammation, endothelial damage, villous endarteritis, and thromboembolism, leading to pulmonary hypertension and potential right-sided heart failure. Even small worm burdens (1-3 worms) can cause significant disease in cats due to the small size of their pulmonary vasculature, and worm death can trigger acute lung injury (HARD - Heartworm Associated Respiratory Disease).
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管寄生虫疾患は主にDirofilaria immitis（犬糸状虫）によって引き起こされ、蚊によって伝播された感染幼虫が組織を移行し肺動脈で成熟します。成虫は肺動脈の炎症、内皮損傷、絨毛性動脈内膜炎、血栓塞栓症を引き起こし、肺高血圧症および右心不全を招きます。猫では肺血管が小さいため少数の虫体（1〜3匹）でも重篤な疾患を引き起こし、虫体の死滅により急性肺障害（HARD：犬糸状虫関連呼吸器疾患）を誘発することがあります。
causes: The primary cause is infection with Dirofilaria immitis transmitted by mosquito vectors. Less commonly, other cardiovascular parasites such as Aelurostrongylus abstrusus (which primarily affects the lungs but can impact pulmonary vasculature) may be involved. Risk factors include outdoor exposure to mosquitoes in endemic areas and lack of preventive medication.

name: Cardiovascular Viral Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as feline parvovirus (feline panleukopenia virus) can infect rapidly dividing myocardial cells in neonatal kittens, leading to myocardial necrosis, inflammation, and subsequent dilated cardiomyopathy. Feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) coronavirus can also cause fibrinous or pyogranulomatous pericarditis and myocarditis through immune-mediated vasculitis. These viral infections result in impaired cardiac contractility, arrhythmias, and potential congestive heart failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫パルボウイルス（猫汎白血球減少症ウイルス）は新生子猫の急速に分裂する心筋細胞に感染し、心筋壊死・炎症を引き起こし、拡張型心筋症に至ることがある。猫伝染性腹膜炎（FIP）コロナウイルスも免疫介在性血管炎を通じて線維素性または肉芽腫性の心膜炎・心筋炎を引き起こす。これらのウイルス感染により心収縮力の低下、不整脈、うっ血性心不全が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include feline parvovirus (panleukopenia virus) infection in utero or in neonatal kittens, and feline coronavirus causing FIP-associated myocarditis and pericarditis. Secondary contributing factors include immunosuppression from concurrent FeLV or FIV infection, which may exacerbate viral-induced cardiac damage.

name: Cardiovascular Bacterial Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Bacteria enter the bloodstream through wounds, dental disease, or other infections, leading to bacteremia and potential colonization of cardiac structures such as heart valves (infective endocarditis). Bacterial colonization triggers inflammatory responses, vegetation formation on valves, and progressive valvular damage, which can result in congestive heart failure, thromboembolic events, and sepsis. Secondary organ damage may occur due to septic emboli lodging in kidneys, spleen, brain, or other tissues.
pathophysiology_ja: 細菌が創傷、歯科疾患、またはその他の感染症を介して血流に侵入し、菌血症を引き起こし、心臓弁などの心血管構造に定着します（感染性心内膜炎）。細菌の定着により炎症反応、弁上の疣贅形成、進行性の弁損傷が生じ、うっ血性心不全、血栓塞栓症、敗血症を引き起こす可能性があります。敗血症性塞栓が腎臓、脾臓、脳などの臓器に到達し、二次的な臓器障害が生じることがあります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Bartonella henselae (most frequent in cats), Staphylococcus spp., Streptococcus spp., and Escherichia coli. Predisposing factors include pre-existing valvular disease, immunosuppression (e.g., FIV/FeLV infection), chronic dental disease, and indwelling catheters. Flea infestation is a major risk factor for Bartonella-associated endocarditis.

name: Cardiovascular Fungal Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms (commonly Aspergillus, Cryptococcus, or other systemic mycoses) disseminate hematogenously and colonize the cardiovascular system, including the endocardium, myocardium, and great vessels. This leads to fungal endocarditis, myocarditis, vasculitis, or formation of vegetative lesions that can cause valvular dysfunction, thromboembolic events, and progressive cardiac insufficiency. The inflammatory response and tissue destruction compromise cardiac output and may result in systemic embolization of infected material to other organs.
pathophysiology_ja: 真菌（主にアスペルギルス、クリプトコッカスなどの全身性真菌症）が血行性に播種し、心内膜、心筋、大血管などの心血管系に定着します。これにより真菌性心内膜炎、心筋炎、血管炎、または疣贅性病変が形成され、弁機能不全、血栓塞栓症、進行性の心不全を引き起こします。炎症反応と組織破壊により心拍出量が低下し、感染物質の全身塞栓が生じる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include systemic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Cryptococcus neoformans, Histoplasma capsulatum, Blastomyces dermatitidis, or Coccidioides immitis that disseminate to the cardiovascular system. Secondary factors include immunosuppression (FIV, FeLV, corticosteroid therapy, or concurrent illness), pre-existing cardiac disease or valvular damage that predisposes to fungal colonization, and environmental exposure to high fungal spore burdens.

name: Cardiovascular Infection (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular infections in cats involve colonization of the heart valves, endocardium, or vascular endothelium by bacterial, fungal, or parasitic organisms, leading to vegetative lesions (endocarditis), valvular insufficiency, and potential septic embolization to distant organs. The infection triggers local inflammation, platelet-fibrin deposition, and immune complex formation, which can result in progressive cardiac dysfunction, arrhythmias, and systemic complications including glomerulonephritis and thromboembolic disease. Bacteremia from oral, skin, or urinary infections often seeds the cardiovascular system, particularly when pre-existing endothelial damage is present.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管感染症は、細菌、真菌、または寄生虫が心臓弁膜、心内膜、または血管内皮に定着し、疣贅性病変（心内膜炎）、弁膜不全、および遠隔臓器への敗血症性塞栓を引き起こす。感染により局所的な炎症、血小板フィブリン沈着、免疫複合体形成が起こり、進行性の心機能障害、不整脈、糸球体腎炎や血栓塞栓症などの全身性合併症を引き起こす。口腔、皮膚、尿路感染からの菌血症が、特に既存の内皮障害がある場合に心血管系に播種することが多い。

name: Cardiovascular Inflammation (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular inflammation in cats involves inflammatory infiltration of the myocardium, endocardium, pericardium, or vasculature, leading to impaired cardiac function, arrhythmias, and potential heart failure. Inflammatory mediators cause endothelial damage, increased vascular permeability, and fibrosis, which can result in cardiomyopathy, valvular dysfunction, or pericardial effusion. Chronic inflammation may lead to myocardial remodeling and progressive deterioration of cardiac output.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管炎症は、心筋、心内膜、心膜、または血管壁への炎症細胞浸潤を伴い、心機能障害、不整脈、心不全を引き起こす。炎症性メディエーターが内皮障害、血管透過性亢進、線維化を引き起こし、心筋症、弁膜機能不全、心嚢液貯留につながる。慢性炎症は心筋リモデリングと心拍出量の進行性低下をもたらす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include infectious agents such as feline infectious peritonitis (FIP) coronavirus, Bartonella henselae, toxoplasmosis, and viral myocarditis. Secondary causes include immune-mediated diseases, systemic inflammatory conditions, sepsis, and neoplastic infiltration. Idiopathic myocarditis and endocarditis associated with bacteremia from dental disease or other chronic infections are also recognized causes.

name: Cardiovascular Neoplasia (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular neoplasia in cats involves abnormal proliferation of cells within the heart, great vessels, or pericardium. The most common types include lymphoma, hemangiosarcoma, and chemodectoma, which can cause pericardial effusion, cardiac tamponade, arrhythmias, and impaired cardiac output. Tumor growth may obstruct blood flow, invade myocardium, or metastasize to other organs, leading to progressive cardiovascular compromise.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管系腫瘍は、心臓、大血管、または心膜内の細胞の異常増殖を伴う。最も一般的な種類にはリンパ腫、血管肉腫、化学受容器腫瘍があり、心嚢液貯留、心タンポナーデ、不整脈、心拍出量の低下を引き起こす可能性がある。腫瘍の増殖は血流を阻害し、心筋に浸潤し、他の臓器に転移して、進行性の心血管機能障害をもたらす。
causes: The exact etiology is often unknown, but lymphoma (the most common cardiac tumor in cats) is frequently associated with feline leukemia virus (FeLV) infection. Genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and immune dysregulation may also contribute to tumor development. Other tumor types such as hemangiosarcoma and metastatic carcinomas may arise spontaneously or secondary to primary neoplasia elsewhere in the body.

name: Cardiovascular Metabolic Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular metabolic disease in cats involves the interplay between metabolic derangements (such as obesity, diabetes mellitus, hyperthyroidism, or dyslipidemia) and cardiovascular dysfunction. These metabolic disturbances lead to myocardial remodeling, increased cardiac workload, endothelial dysfunction, and systemic hypertension, ultimately resulting in heart failure, thromboembolism, or arrhythmias. Chronic metabolic stress promotes oxidative damage, fibrosis, and hypertrophy of the myocardium, impairing cardiac output and organ perfusion.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管代謝疾患は、肥満、糖尿病、甲状腺機能亢進症、脂質異常症などの代謝異常と心血管機能障害の相互作用により生じます。これらの代謝障害は心筋リモデリング、心臓負荷の増大、内皮機能障害、全身性高血圧を引き起こし、最終的に心不全、血栓塞栓症、不整脈に至ります。慢性的な代謝ストレスは心筋の酸化的損傷、線維化、肥大を促進し、心拍出量と臓器灌流を障害します。
causes: Primary causes include hyperthyroidism (most common endocrine disease in older cats), diabetes mellitus, obesity, and chronic kidney disease leading to secondary hypertension and cardiac changes. Secondary causes encompass systemic hypertension from renal or endocrine disease, hyperaldosteronism, and dietary factors such as taurine deficiency leading to dilated cardiomyopathy. Genetic predisposition to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy may be exacerbated by concurrent metabolic disorders.

name: Cardiovascular Nutritional Deficiency (Cat)
pathophysiology: Deficiency of essential nutrients, primarily taurine, leads to impaired myocardial contractility and progressive dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in cats. Taurine is critical for calcium regulation in cardiac myocytes, and its depletion results in reduced systolic function, chamber dilation, and eventual congestive heart failure. Secondary deficiencies in L-carnitine, selenium, or vitamin E may also contribute to oxidative damage and impaired myocardial energy metabolism.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にタウリンなどの必須栄養素の欠乏により、心筋収縮力が低下し、猫において進行性の拡張型心筋症（DCM）が発生します。タウリンは心筋細胞のカルシウム調節に不可欠であり、その欠乏は収縮機能の低下、心腔拡大、最終的にはうっ血性心不全を引き起こします。L-カルニチン、セレン、ビタミンEの二次的欠乏も酸化的損傷や心筋エネルギー代謝障害に寄与する可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is dietary taurine deficiency, historically associated with commercial cat foods with insufficient taurine content or improperly formulated homemade diets. Secondary causes include malabsorption disorders reducing taurine uptake, excessive heat processing of food degrading taurine, and deficiencies in other cardioprotective nutrients such as L-carnitine, selenium, and vitamin E.

name: Cardiovascular Genetic Disorder (Cat)
pathophysiology: Genetic mutations affecting cardiac structural proteins (such as myosin-binding protein C in Maine Coons and Ragdolls) lead to abnormal myocardial development, most commonly resulting in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). The thickened ventricular walls impair diastolic filling, increase left atrial pressure, and can progress to congestive heart failure, arterial thromboembolism, or sudden cardiac death. Other inherited cardiomyopathies (dilated, restrictive, arrhythmogenic right ventricular) involve distinct genetic pathways but similarly compromise cardiac output and rhythm.
pathophysiology_ja: 心筋構造タンパク質（メインクーンやラグドールにおけるミオシン結合タンパクCなど）の遺伝子変異により心筋の異常な発達が生じ、最も一般的には肥大型心筋症（HCM）を引き起こします。肥厚した心室壁は拡張期充満を障害し、左房圧を上昇させ、うっ血性心不全、動脈血栓塞栓症、または突然死に進行する可能性があります。その他の遺伝性心筋症（拡張型、拘束型、不整脈源性右室心筋症）も異なる遺伝経路を介して心拍出量やリズムを障害します。
causes: Primary causes are autosomal dominant genetic mutations, most notably the MYBPC3 mutations (A31P in Maine Coon, R820W in Ragdoll) causing hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Breed predispositions exist in Maine Coon, Ragdoll, British Shorthair, Sphynx, Persian, and Bengal cats. Secondary factors such as hyperthyroidism, hypertension, and obesity can exacerbate the underlying genetic cardiac disease.

name: Cardiovascular Autoimmune Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: The immune system erroneously targets cardiac tissues, including myocardial cells, endocardium, or vascular endothelium, leading to inflammation, fibrosis, and impaired cardiac function. Autoantibodies and autoreactive T cells mediate progressive damage to the myocardium and vasculature, potentially resulting in dilated cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, or vasculitis. Chronic immune-mediated inflammation can lead to cardiac remodeling, arrhythmias, and congestive heart failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が心筋細胞、心内膜、または血管内皮を誤って攻撃し、炎症、線維化、および心機能障害を引き起こします。自己抗体および自己反応性T細胞が心筋や血管に進行性の損傷を引き起こし、拡張型心筋症、心筋炎、または血管炎を生じる可能性があります。慢性的な免疫介在性炎症は心臓リモデリング、不整脈、およびうっ血性心不全につながることがあります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against cardiac antigens, potentially triggered by viral infections (such as FCV or FPV), molecular mimicry, or genetic predisposition. Secondary factors include chronic inflammatory conditions, concurrent autoimmune diseases (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndrome), and environmental stressors that may exacerbate the immune response against cardiac tissues.

name: Cardiovascular Degenerative Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Progressive degenerative changes occur in the cardiac valves (most commonly the mitral and aortic valves) and myocardium, leading to valvular insufficiency, impaired cardiac output, and eventual congestive heart failure. Fibrosis, myxomatous degeneration, and calcification of valve leaflets result in regurgitant blood flow and volume overload of cardiac chambers. In cats, concurrent myocardial degeneration may lead to reduced contractility and arrhythmias.
pathophysiology_ja: 心臓弁（主に僧帽弁および大動脈弁）や心筋に進行性の変性変化が生じ、弁閉鎖不全、心拍出量の低下、最終的にはうっ血性心不全に至る。弁尖の線維化、粘液腫様変性、石灰化により逆流が生じ、心腔の容量負荷が増大する。猫では心筋変性が併発し、収縮力低下や不整脈を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include age-related degenerative changes of the cardiac valves and myocardium, often accelerated by chronic hypertension or hyperthyroidism. Secondary causes include chronic kidney disease leading to volume overload and hypertension, nutritional deficiencies (such as taurine deficiency), and chronic inflammatory or metabolic conditions that contribute to progressive cardiac deterioration.

name: Cardiovascular Traumatic Injury (Cat)
pathophysiology: Traumatic injury to the cardiovascular system in cats typically results from blunt or penetrating trauma (e.g., vehicular accidents, falls from heights, bite wounds) causing direct damage to the heart, great vessels, or peripheral vasculature. This can lead to myocardial contusion, cardiac tamponade from hemopericardium, hemorrhagic shock from vascular rupture, or traumatic arrhythmias due to disrupted cardiac conduction. The resulting hemodynamic compromise leads to decreased cardiac output, poor tissue perfusion, and potentially fatal cardiovascular collapse.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管系外傷は、鈍的外傷や穿通性外傷（交通事故、高所からの落下、咬傷など）により心臓、大血管、末梢血管に直接損傷が生じることで起こる。心筋挫傷、心嚢血腫による心タンポナーデ、血管破裂による出血性ショック、心臓伝導系障害による外傷性不整脈が発生しうる。その結果、心拍出量の低下、組織灌流不全、致命的な循環虚脱に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include vehicular trauma (hit by car), high-rise syndrome (falls from elevated heights), bite wounds from other animals, and penetrating injuries such as gunshot or impalement. Secondary causes include iatrogenic injury during thoracic surgery or catheterization, and coagulopathies that exacerbate hemorrhage from minor vascular trauma.

name: Cardiovascular Behavioral Disorder (Cat)
pathophysiology: Stress-induced sympathetic nervous system activation leads to excessive catecholamine release, resulting in tachycardia, hypertension, and potential cardiac remodeling. Chronic behavioral stress (fear, anxiety, territorial aggression) can cause sustained cardiovascular changes including myocardial hypertrophy and arrhythmias. This creates a feedback loop where cardiovascular dysfunction further exacerbates anxiety-related behaviors.
pathophysiology_ja: ストレスによる交感神経系の活性化がカテコラミンの過剰放出を引き起こし、頻脈、高血圧、心臓リモデリングにつながります。慢性的な行動ストレス（恐怖、不安、縄張り攻撃性）は、心筋肥大や不整脈などの持続的な心血管系の変化を引き起こす可能性があります。心血管機能障害が不安関連行動をさらに悪化させるフィードバックループが形成されます。
causes: Primary causes include chronic environmental stress, fear-based anxiety disorders, and inadequate socialization leading to persistent sympathetic overactivation. Secondary causes include confinement stress, inter-cat conflict in multi-cat households, and pre-existing subclinical cardiac conditions exacerbated by behavioral stress.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、慢性的な環境ストレス、恐怖に基づく不安障害、および持続的な交感神経の過活性化につながる不十分な社会化です。二次的原因として、閉じ込めストレス、多頭飼育における猫同士の対立、行動ストレスにより悪化する潜在的な心疾患が含まれます。

name: Cardiovascular Infectious Disease (Cat)
pathophysiology: Cardiovascular infectious diseases in cats involve pathogen invasion (bacterial, viral, parasitic, or fungal) of the heart and/or blood vessels, leading to inflammation of the endocardium (endocarditis), myocardium (myocarditis), or pericardium (pericarditis). Common agents include Bartonella henselae, feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV), feline leukemia virus (FeLV), and Dirofilaria immitis (heartworm), which cause valvular damage, myocardial dysfunction, thromboembolic events, and impaired cardiac output. Systemic inflammatory responses and immune-mediated damage further compromise cardiovascular function, potentially leading to congestive heart failure or septicemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 猫の心血管感染症は、細菌（Bartonella henselaeなど）、ウイルス（FIV、FeLV）、寄生虫（犬糸状虫）、真菌などの病原体が心臓や血管に侵入し、心内膜炎、心筋炎、心膜炎を引き起こす疾患である。弁膜の損傷、心筋機能障害、血栓塞栓症、心拍出量の低下が生じる。全身性炎症反応や免疫介在性障害により心血管機能がさらに悪化し、うっ血性心不全や敗血症に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (Bartonella spp., Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp.), viral infections (FIV, FeLV), and parasitic infections (Dirofilaria immitis heartworm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, pre-existing valvular disease, dental disease providing a source of bacteremia, and indwelling catheters or surgical procedures that introduce pathogens into the bloodstream.

name: Equine Infectious Anemia
pathophysiology: Equine Infectious Anemia virus (EIAV), a lentivirus of the Retroviridae family, infects monocytes and macrophages, integrating into the host genome. The virus causes recurrent episodes of viremia with immune-mediated destruction of erythrocytes and platelets through complement activation and immune complex deposition, leading to hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and vasculitis. Chronic infection results in glomerulonephritis, hepatitis, and bone marrow suppression due to persistent immune stimulation and cytokine dysregulation.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬伝染性貧血ウイルス（EIAV）はレトロウイルス科レンチウイルス属に属し、単球やマクロファージに感染して宿主ゲノムに組み込まれる。ウイルスは反復性のウイルス血症を引き起こし、補体活性化や免疫複合体の沈着により赤血球や血小板の免疫介在性破壊が生じ、溶血性貧血・血小板減少症・血管炎を発症する。慢性感染では持続的な免疫刺激とサイトカイン調節異常により、糸球体腎炎、肝炎、骨髄抑制が生じる。
causes: The primary cause is infection with Equine Infectious Anemia Virus (EIAV), a lentivirus transmitted mechanically by blood-feeding insects, particularly horseflies (Tabanus spp.) and deerflies (Chrysops spp.). Iatrogenic transmission occurs through contaminated needles, surgical instruments, blood transfusions, or other blood-contaminated equipment. Transplacental transmission from infected mares to foals can also occur.
causes_ja: 血液を媒介とした吸血昆虫（主にアブ）による感染が主な感染経路です。また、汚染された注射針や外科器具を通じた直接的血液接触、または感染馬の血液製品の輸血による感染もあります。
treatment_ja: EIAに対して確立された治療方法は存在しません。感染馬はウイルスを終生保有し、治療により回復することはありません。管理としては、感染馬の隔離と症状の緩和療法のみが実施されます。
prevention_ja: EIAウイルスは抗原変異を容易に起こすため、ワクチン開発は実質的に非常に困難です。感染馬を血清検査で検出し、淘汰処分することが感染拡大防止の最重要対策です。定期的な血清検査による陽性馬の早期発見と隔離が予防の中心となります。
prognosis_ja: EIA感染馬の予後は極めて不良です。感染馬は生涯ウイルスを保有し、回復することはありません。多くの場合、慢性的な貧血と全身状態の悪化により、最終的には死亡に至ります。
description_ja: 馬伝染性貧血（EIA）はウイルスの感染によって起こる馬属固有の伝染病です。持続的なウイルス血症、貧血を伴う高熱、慢性的経過での回帰熱を特徴とします。一旦ウイルスに感染した馬は、生涯回復することなく感染状態が続き、予後は非常に不良です。

name: Navicular Disease
pathophysiology: Navicular disease involves chronic degenerative changes of the navicular bone, navicular bursa, and deep digital flexor tendon (DDFT) in the forelimb. Repetitive biomechanical stress leads to vascular compromise, subchondral bone sclerosis, cartilage erosion, and fibrocartilage degeneration on the flexor surface of the navicular bone. Inflammation and remodeling of the navicular bone result in chronic heel pain and progressive lameness, typically affecting both front feet.
pathophysiology_ja: 舟状骨病は、前肢の舟状骨、舟状骨滑液包、および深指屈筋腱（DDFT）の慢性変性疾患である。反復的な生体力学的ストレスにより血管障害、軟骨下骨硬化、軟骨びらん、および舟状骨屈筋面の線維軟骨変性が生じる。舟状骨の炎症とリモデリングにより慢性的な蹄踵部痛と進行性跛行が発生し、通常両前肢に影響する。
causes: The primary cause is repetitive concussive and compressive forces on the navicular apparatus due to conformational predisposition (upright pasterns, small feet, heavy body relative to foot size) and intense athletic work. Secondary contributing factors include poor hoof balance, irregular trimming/shoeing, work on hard surfaces, and genetic predisposition particularly in Quarter Horses, Thoroughbreds, and Warmbloods. Vascular insufficiency to the navicular bone may also play a role in disease initiation and progression.

name: Colic
pathophysiology: Colic refers to abdominal pain resulting from gastrointestinal disturbances including spasm, distension, displacement, torsion, or vascular compromise of the intestinal tract. Disruption of normal intestinal motility leads to gas accumulation, fluid sequestration, impaction, or ischemic necrosis, triggering visceral and somatic pain responses. In severe cases, intestinal compromise leads to endotoxemia, systemic inflammatory response, hypovolemic shock, and potentially death.
pathophysiology_ja: 疝痛は、腸管の痙攣、膨張、変位、捻転、または血行障害などの消化管障害に起因する腹痛を指す。正常な腸管運動の障害により、ガス貯留、液体の隔離、食滞、または虚血性壊死が生じ、内臓痛および体性痛反応を引き起こす。重症例では腸管の障害からエンドトキシン血症、全身性炎症反応、循環血液量減少性ショックを引き起こし、死に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include intestinal impaction (feed, sand, foreign bodies), gas distension, large colon displacement or volvulus, small intestinal strangulation (lipoma, inguinal hernia, epiploic foramen entrapment), intussusception, and enteritis. Secondary or predisposing factors include dietary changes, poor dental health, inadequate water intake, parasitic infestation (especially Strongylus vulgaris causing thromboembolic colic), stress, lack of exercise, and post-operative adhesions.
causes_ja: 疝痛の原因は不適切な飼養管理に起因することが多いです。主な誘因は：（1）濃厚飼料（穀物）の多給、（2）乾草の急激な変更、（3）歯の疾病による咀嚼不全、（4）運動不足による便秘、（5）水分摂取不足、（6）寄生虫感染。また、春先など季節の変わり目に疝痛の発症が増加します。
treatment_ja: 疝痛馬には馬服を着用させ、必要に応じて保温により体温低下を防止します。腹部マッサージを行い、痛みが軽度で曳き運動が可能な場合には10～30分程度の運動を行います。この軽度の運動は腸の蠕動を刺激し、鎮痛効果があります。重度症例では獣医師による診断と手術適応の判断が必要です。鎮痛薬の投与と栄養管理も重要です。
prevention_ja: 疝痛予防には適切な飼養管理が極めて重要です：（1）歯の定期的な検査と咀嚼機能の維持、（2）濃厚飼料の過剰給与を避ける、（3）乾草の急激な変更を避ける、（4）便秘の兆候（糞が小さく硬くなる）が見られたら、芒硝、流動パラフィン、整腸剤を投与する、（5）定期的な適度な運動、（6）十分な水分摂取の確保、（7）獣医師と相談して適切な駆虫プログラムを実施する。
prognosis_ja: 疝痛の予後は重症度と疾患の種類に大きく左右されます。軽度の疝痛は適切な治療で回復しますが、腸変位や腸閉塞などの重度疾患は、手術が必要となり予後が悪くなります。早期の獣医師による診察と迅速な治療介入が予後を大きく改善します。
description_ja: 馬の疝痛は、腹部の疼痛を伴う多くの疾病を含む症候群です。胃や腸などの消化管疾患が主な原因で、馬の腸管の解剖学的特性により、一度疝痛が起こると生命に関わる状況になることが多いです。便秘疝、風気疝、変位疝など複数のタイプがあります。

name: Equine Recurrent Uveitis (ERU)
pathophysiology: ERU is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease of the uveal tract characterized by recurrent episodes of intraocular inflammation. It involves a T-lymphocyte-mediated autoimmune response against ocular antigens, potentially triggered by molecular mimicry with Leptospira spp. antigens. Repeated bouts of inflammation lead to progressive destruction of intraocular structures, including the iris, ciliary body, lens, and retina, ultimately resulting in blindness.
pathophysiology_ja: ERUはブドウ膜の免疫介在性炎症疾患であり、再発性の眼内炎症を特徴とします。レプトスピラ属の抗原との分子擬態により誘発される可能性のある、眼内抗原に対するTリンパ球介在性自己免疫反応が関与しています。炎症の反復により虹彩、毛様体、水晶体、網膜などの眼内構造が進行性に破壊され、最終的に失明に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is an autoimmune response targeting uveal tissues, frequently associated with prior Leptospira interrogans infection (particularly serovars Pomona and Bratislava). Other potential triggers include Onchocerca cervicalis infection, trauma, and bacterial or viral infections. Genetic predisposition exists, with Appaloosas, Warmbloods, and draft breeds being at increased risk.

name: Lameness
pathophysiology: Lameness in horses results from pain, mechanical dysfunction, or neuromuscular deficits affecting one or more limbs. Inflammation, tissue damage, or structural abnormalities in bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, or the hoof alter normal gait biomechanics, leading to asymmetric weight-bearing and compensatory movement patterns. Chronic lameness may involve progressive degenerative changes such as cartilage erosion, fibrosis, and remodeling of affected structures.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の跛行は、疼痛、機械的機能障害、または神経筋障害により一肢以上に影響を及ぼすことで生じる。骨、関節、腱、靱帯、蹄における炎症、組織損傷、構造異常が正常な歩様のバイオメカニクスを変化させ、非対称な荷重負担と代償性の運動パターンを引き起こす。慢性跛行では軟骨びらん、線維化、罹患構造のリモデリングなど進行性の変性変化を伴うことがある。
causes: Primary causes include hoof disorders (laminitis, navicular disease, hoof abscess), joint disease (osteoarthritis, osteochondrosis), and soft tissue injuries (tendinitis, suspensory ligament desmitis, muscle strains). Secondary causes include poor hoof trimming/shoeing, conformational defects, repetitive concussive trauma from hard surfaces, excessive or improper training, and systemic diseases such as equine metabolic syndrome or Cushing's disease predisposing to laminitis.

name: Strangles
pathophysiology: Strangles is caused by Streptococcus equi subspecies equi, which colonizes the pharyngeal and nasal mucosa, invades the lymphoid tissue, and spreads to regional lymph nodes (submandibular and retropharyngeal). The bacteria resist phagocytosis via the hyaluronic acid capsule and antiphagocytic M-protein (SeM), leading to massive abscessation of the lymph nodes. Severely enlarged lymph nodes can compress the upper airway, potentially causing respiratory obstruction ('strangling'), and in some cases the infection disseminates hematogenously to other organs (bastard strangles).
pathophysiology_ja: 腺疫はStreptococcus equi subsp. equiによって引き起こされ、咽頭および鼻粘膜に定着した後、リンパ組織に侵入し、顎下および咽頭後リンパ節に広がります。ヒアルロン酸莢膜および抗貪食M蛋白（SeM）により貪食を回避し、リンパ節の著しい膿瘍化を引き起こします。腫大したリンパ節が上部気道を圧迫し呼吸困難（絞扼）を起こすことがあり、血行性に他臓器へ播種する場合は転移性腺疫（bastard strangles）となります。
causes: The primary cause is infection with Streptococcus equi subspecies equi, a gram-positive, beta-hemolytic, Lancefield group C bacterium. Transmission occurs via direct contact with infected horses or carriers, or indirect contact through contaminated fomites (water troughs, feed buckets, handlers' equipment). Stress, young age, immunocompromised status, and introduction of new horses into a herd are predisposing factors.

name: Equine Herpesvirus (EHV)
pathophysiology: EHV (primarily EHV-1 and EHV-4) infects respiratory epithelial cells, then establishes cell-associated viremia by infecting leukocytes, allowing systemic spread to endothelial cells of the pregnant uterus, CNS, and other organs. EHV-1 causes vasculitis and thrombosis in the endometrium leading to abortion, and in the CNS leading to equine herpesvirus myeloencephalopathy (EHM). The virus establishes lifelong latency in trigeminal ganglia and lymphoid tissues, with periodic reactivation under stress.
pathophysiology_ja: EHV（主にEHV-1およびEHV-4）は呼吸器上皮細胞に感染後、白血球に感染して細胞結合性ウイルス血症を引き起こし、妊娠子宮や中枢神経系の血管内皮細胞へ全身性に拡散する。EHV-1は子宮内膜の血管炎・血栓症による流産、中枢神経系の血管炎によるヘルペス脊髄脳症（EHM）を引き起こす。ウイルスは三叉神経節やリンパ組織に終生潜伏感染し、ストレス下で周期的に再活性化する。
causes: The primary cause is infection with Equine Herpesvirus, most commonly EHV-1 (causing abortion, neonatal disease, respiratory disease, and neurological disease) and EHV-4 (primarily respiratory disease). Transmission occurs via direct contact with nasal secretions, aborted fetuses and placental tissues, or aerosolized droplets, as well as through fomites. Stress, transportation, commingling, immunosuppression, and concurrent illness predispose to reactivation of latent infection and clinical disease outbreaks.

name: Laminitis
pathophysiology: Laminitis involves failure of the lamellar bond between the distal phalanx (P3) and the hoof wall due to enzymatic degradation (matrix metalloproteinases), ischemia, and inflammation of the dermal laminae. This leads to mechanical separation of the laminae, allowing rotation and/or distal displacement (sinking) of the distal phalanx within the hoof capsule. Underlying mechanisms include endocrine dysfunction (insulin dysregulation), sepsis-related inflammatory mediator release, or excessive mechanical overload on the laminae.
pathophysiology_ja: 蹄葉炎は、基質メタロプロテアーゼによる酵素分解、虚血、および真皮葉の炎症により、蹄骨と蹄壁の間の葉状結合が破綻する疾患である。これにより葉状組織の機械的分離が生じ、蹄骨の回転および/または沈下が起こる。基礎的なメカニズムにはインスリン異常症などの内分泌障害、敗血症関連の炎症性メディエーター放出、または蹄への過度な機械的負荷が含まれる。
causes: Primary causes include endocrine disorders (equine metabolic syndrome, pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction/Cushing's disease) with insulin dysregulation, grain overload or excessive intake of non-structural carbohydrates, and systemic inflammatory response (sepsis, endotoxemia from colitis, retained placenta, or pleuropneumonia). Secondary causes include supporting limb laminitis due to contralateral limb injury, corticosteroid administration, black walnut shaving exposure, and excessive concussive forces on hard surfaces.
causes_ja: 蹄葉炎の原因は多様で、複数の分類が存在します：（1）負重性蹄葉炎：下痢や感染症などの全身疾患、穀類過剰摂取による腸内細菌叢変化と内毒素産生、過労、（2）食餌性蹄葉炎：一度に多量の濃厚飼料給餌、（3）内分泌性蹄葉炎：インスリン抵抗性上昇と高インスリン血症がインスリン自体の蹄葉炎誘発作用を引き起こす。
treatment_ja: 蹄葉炎の治療は複雑で、多角的なアプローチが必要です：（1）獣医学的療法：レントゲン検査に基づく診断、鎮痛薬投与、炎症管理、基礎疾患の治療。（2）装蹄療法：蹄の保護対策、蹄角度の調整、蹄底支持具の装着。獣医師と装蹄師の連携が極めて重要です。重度症例では複数回の装蹄が必要な場合があります。
prevention_ja: 蹄葉炎は多くの場合、全身性または他の部位の問題が原因となっています。予防には日頃の適切な飼養管理と基礎疾患の早期治療が重要です。特に、穀類過剰摂取の回避、感染症の早期治療、過労の回避、定期的な蹄の観察と手入れが予防につながります。代謝性疾患（インスリン抵抗性）の馬には特に注意が必要です。
prognosis_ja: 蹄葉炎の予後は発症時期での早期診断と治療の迅速性に大きく左右されます。軽度の急性蹄葉炎は適切な治療で回復の可能性がありますが、重度症例や慢性化した症例では、完全な回復は難しく、生活の質の低下が避けられません。蹄骨沈下が生じた場合、完治は困難で、長期的な管理が必要になります。
description_ja: 馬の蹄葉炎は、蹄部の蹄葉（蹄壁と蹄骨を結合する組織）に起こる急性または慢性の炎症疾患です。蹄葉が破壊されると蹄骨の支持が失われ、蹄骨が沈下・回転し、重度の跛行や蹄変形を引き起こします。有蹄類の疾患の中でも重篤な疾患の一つです。

name: Tendinitis
pathophysiology: Tendinitis in horses involves microtearing and disruption of collagen fibers within the tendon, most commonly the superficial digital flexor tendon (SDFT), due to excessive strain during high-speed exercise. This triggers an inflammatory cascade with edema, hemorrhage, and infiltration of inflammatory cells, followed by disorganized fibroplasia and scar tissue formation. The resulting repair tissue has inferior biomechanical properties compared to normal tendon, predisposing to re-injury.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腱炎は、高速運動時の過度な負荷により腱（最も一般的には浅指屈筋腱）内のコラーゲン線維が微小断裂・破壊されることで発生します。これにより炎症反応が誘発され、浮腫、出血、炎症細胞の浸潤が起こり、その後無秩序な線維増殖と瘢痕組織が形成されます。修復組織は正常な腱と比べて生体力学的特性が劣るため、再発しやすくなります。
causes: Primary causes include overexertion during galloping or jumping, leading to cumulative microdamage exceeding the tendon's repair capacity, as well as acute hyperextension of the metacarpophalangeal joint. Secondary contributing factors include poor footing, inadequate conditioning, fatigue, improper shoeing, and conformational defects such as long toe/low heel.

name: Thrush
pathophysiology: Thrush is a degenerative infection of the frog and adjacent sulci of the horse's hoof, primarily caused by anaerobic bacteria (most notably Fusobacterium necrophorum). The organisms thrive in moist, anaerobic conditions, producing proteolytic enzymes that break down the horn tissue of the frog, leading to necrosis and characteristic black, foul-smelling discharge. In severe cases, the infection can penetrate deeper structures including the sensitive corium, causing lameness and potentially compromising the digital cushion.
pathophysiology_ja: 蹄叉腐爛は、主に嫌気性細菌（特にFusobacterium necrophorum）によって引き起こされる馬の蹄叉およびその周辺溝の変性感染症です。これらの細菌は湿潤で嫌気的な環境下で増殖し、タンパク質分解酵素を産生して蹄叉の角質組織を分解し、壊死と特徴的な黒色で悪臭を伴う排出物を生じます。重症例では感染が敏感な真皮層まで深達し、跛行を引き起こし、蹄球枕を損傷する可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is infection by anaerobic bacteria, particularly Fusobacterium necrophorum, facilitated by prolonged exposure to wet, unsanitary conditions such as standing in mud, manure, or soiled bedding. Secondary contributing factors include poor hoof hygiene, infrequent farrier care, lack of hoof picking, improper hoof conformation (such as contracted heels), and inadequate exercise that reduces natural frog pressure and blood circulation to the hoof.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, triggering inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を介した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害を引き起こし、両側性の場合は腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities of the urinary tract. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infections.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, protein loss, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow and tubular function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal failure if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、タンパク質の喪失、電解質異常、および代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。炎症性細胞浸潤と浮腫が腎血流と尿細管機能を障害し、未治療の場合は線維化から慢性腎不全へ進行する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), toxin ingestion (e.g., heavy metals, oak leaves, red maple), dehydration, septicemia, and chronic systemic diseases.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. Progressive tumor growth leads to renal insufficiency, paraneoplastic syndromes, and space-occupying effects causing abdominal discomfort.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常な細胞増殖を特徴とする。最も一般的に報告される腫瘍は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫であり、正常な腎構造の破壊、濾過・排泄機能の障害、所属リンパ節や肺などへの転移を引き起こしうる。腫瘍の進行に伴い腎不全、腫瘍随伴症候群、腹部の圧迫症状が生じる。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistently identified predisposing factors such as specific toxins, viral agents, or hereditary conditions. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may involve the kidneys as part of multicentric disease. Age-related somatic mutations and potential chronic inflammatory or toxic insults to the kidney may play contributing roles.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction may lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary mineral imbalances affecting bone and soft tissue integrity.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄を調節する腎臓の機能障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、または代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能不全は腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または骨や軟部組織に影響を及ぼす二次的なミネラル不均衡につながる場合がある。
causes: Primary causes include genetic or idiopathic renal tubular dysfunction, chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), and oxalate-containing plant ingestion. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, high-calcium diets (excessive alfalfa), systemic diseases such as pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID), and chronic kidney disease leading to impaired mineral metabolism.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium), can lead to renal tubular dysfunction, nephrocalcinosis, or nephrosis in horses. Imbalances in the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio or excessive oxalate ingestion from certain forages can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tubules, leading to progressive renal damage. Chronic deficiency states may impair renal concentrating ability and glomerular filtration, resulting in renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏は、馬において腎尿細管機能障害、腎石灰化症、またはネフローゼを引き起こす可能性があります。カルシウムとリンの比率の不均衡や、特定の牧草からのシュウ酸の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管にシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の沈着を引き起こし、進行性の腎障害をもたらします。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎濃縮能力および糸球体濾過を損ない、腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), chronic ingestion of high-oxalate plants (e.g., tropical grasses such as Setaria or Buffel grass), and deficiencies of vitamin A or vitamin D. Secondary causes include prolonged grazing on nutrient-poor pastures, inadequate mineral supplementation, and concurrent conditions that impair nutrient absorption from the gastrointestinal tract.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal kidney development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and inflammation ultimately lead to chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異を伴い、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能の障害、および代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成が正常な腎構造を破壊します。進行性の線維化と炎症が最終的に慢性腎不全へと至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting renal development or function, which may follow autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Secondary factors such as dehydration, concurrent infections, or nephrotoxic exposure can accelerate disease progression. Certain breeds may have higher predisposition due to limited genetic diversity.
causes_ja: 主な原因は腎臓の発達や機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異であり、特定の疾患により常染色体劣性または優性の遺伝様式をとります。脱水、併発感染症、腎毒性物質への曝露などの二次的要因が疾患の進行を加速させることがあります。特定の品種では遺伝的多様性の制限により素因が高い場合があります。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitium. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Chronic immune-mediated inflammation leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質に免疫複合体が沈着する。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎を生じる。慢性的な免疫介在性炎症は線維化、ネフロンの喪失、進行性腎不全につながる。
causes: The primary cause is dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoimmune targeting of renal tissues; this may be idiopathic or triggered by chronic infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia, Streptococcus equi), drug reactions, or neoplasia. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune conditions or persistent antigenic stimulation from chronic inflammatory diseases. Genetic predisposition may also play a role in susceptibility.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephrons, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired renal filtration, concentration ability, and waste elimination. Chronic insult results in loss of functional renal mass, accumulation of uremic toxins, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may involve both acute and chronic components, with compensatory hypertrophy of remaining nephrons ultimately failing to maintain adequate renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロンの進行性劣化を伴い、腎濾過機能、濃縮能力、老廃物排泄の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害により機能的腎組織が減少し、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンの代償性肥大が最終的に十分な腎機能を維持できなくなる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, reduced renal perfusion from cardiovascular disease, chronic urinary obstruction, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Infectious causes such as leptospirosis and ascending pyelonephritis can also contribute to progressive renal degeneration.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to renal parenchyma, vasculature, or the renal pelvis. This can result in subcapsular or perirenal hematoma, parenchymal laceration, renal vascular disruption, or urine leakage (uroperitoneum/uroretroperitoneum). The resulting hemorrhage, inflammation, and potential urine contamination can lead to hypovolemic shock, peritonitis, and progressive renal dysfunction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、血管系、または腎盂に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより被膜下血腫や腎周囲血腫、実質裂傷、腎血管損傷、または尿漏出（尿性腹膜炎・後腹膜尿漏出）が発生し得る。その結果生じる出血、炎症、尿汚染により、循環血液量減少性ショック、腹膜炎、進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that are associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal insufficiency can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to characteristic behavioral changes. The disorder reflects the horse's response to discomfort originating from the kidneys or upper urinary tract, which may alter normal posture, appetite, and performance.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能不全に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を気にする、体を伸ばすなど）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石症、または腎機能不全が内臓痛経路を刺激し、特徴的な行動変化を引き起こします。この障害は腎臓や上部尿路に起因する不快感に対する馬の反応を反映し、姿勢、食欲、運動能力に影響を及ぼします。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure leading to visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal cysts, perirenal abscessation, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Toxin exposure (such as aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity or heavy metal ingestion) can also contribute to renal discomfort manifesting as behavioral changes.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to nephritis or pyelonephritis, causing tubular damage, interstitial edema, and potential abscess formation. Progressive infection can impair glomerular filtration, concentrating ability, and ultimately lead to renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が誘発され、腎炎や腎盂腎炎を引き起こし、尿細管障害、間質浮腫、膿瘍形成を伴います。感染が進行すると糸球体濾過率や濃縮能が低下し、未治療の場合は腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, or hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, and structural abnormalities that predispose to bacterial colonization. Leptospira spp. can also cause renal infection in horses through environmental exposure.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or lodge within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. The parasites cause direct tissue destruction, granulomatous inflammation, and fibrosis of the kidney, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through renal arteries (particularly S. vulgaris) can also cause thrombosis, infarction, and ischemic damage to renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis（deletrix）、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発生する。寄生虫は直接的な組織破壊、肉芽腫性炎症、および腎臓の線維化を引き起こし、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。腎動脈を通じた幼虫の移行は血栓症、梗塞、および虚血性腎障害を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through renal vasculature, infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode causing opportunistic granulomatous nephritis), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or compromised health status that may predispose to opportunistic parasitic infections, as well as heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming programs.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to the renal vasculature and glomeruli, leading to glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, and impaired renal function. Immune complex deposition in renal tissues further exacerbates inflammation and compromises filtration capacity, potentially leading to acute or chronic renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルス性病原体が腎血管系および糸球体に血管炎や免疫介在性損傷を引き起こし、糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、腎機能障害をもたらす。腎組織への免疫複合体の沈着がさらに炎症を悪化させ、濾過能力を低下させ、急性または慢性の腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, viral-induced vasculitis, and concurrent dehydration or nephrotoxic drug administration that exacerbate renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue.
