Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, recurrent hemodynamic insults (dehydration, hypotension), oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis can also contribute to progressive renal degeneration.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle. This leads to hemorrhage (subcapsular, perirenal, or intra-abdominal), potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum), inflammation, and if severe, compromised renal perfusion resulting in ischemic necrosis. Secondary complications include hematoma formation, abscessation, hydronephrosis, and in bilateral cases or solitary kidney trauma, acute renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または血管茎に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下、腎周囲、または腹腔内）や尿漏出（尿腹症）、炎症が起こり、重症例では腎灌流障害から虚血性壊死に至る。二次的合併症として血腫形成、膿瘍化、水腎症、および両側性損傷の場合は急性腎不全が生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition (e.g., racing, jumping, cross-country), collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fence posts, or fractured ribs may also damage the kidney. Iatrogenic causes such as percutaneous renal biopsy complications are rare secondary causes.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal neoplasia can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to behavioral changes that mimic colic or musculoskeletal discomfort. Altered renal function may also cause electrolyte imbalances and uremia, further contributing to neurological and behavioral abnormalities.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能不全に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を気にする行動、伸展姿勢など）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石、または腎腫瘍が内臓痛経路を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系の不快感に類似した行動変化を引き起こします。腎機能の変化により電解質異常や尿毒症が生じ、神経学的および行動異常がさらに助長されます。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and chronic interstitial nephritis causing visceral pain that manifests as behavioral abnormalities. Secondary causes include ureterolithiasis, post-renal obstruction, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and referred pain from adjacent organ pathology.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli cause inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in pyelonephritis, fibrosis, and eventual renal insufficiency if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害をもたらす。慢性感染は腎盂腎炎、線維化、最終的には腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (most commonly E. coli), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and nephrolithiasis causing urinary stasis. Secondary contributing factors include urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and concurrent systemic diseases that predispose to bacterial colonization of the kidneys.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or lodge within the renal parenchyma, renal pelvis, or renal vasculature. The parasites cause direct mechanical tissue destruction, granulomatous inflammation, vasculitis, and progressive nephritis, potentially leading to renal insufficiency or failure. Larval migration of Strongylus vulgaris through mesenteric arteries can also cause thromboembolic damage to renal arterial supply.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質、腎盂、または腎血管系に移行・定着することで発生する。寄生虫は直接的な組織破壊、肉芽腫性炎症、血管炎、進行性腎炎を引き起こし、腎不全に至る可能性がある。普通円虫の幼虫移行は腸間膜動脈を経由して腎動脈への血栓塞栓性障害も引き起こしうる。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasitic larvae such as Strongylus vulgaris (large strongyles) through the renal vasculature, infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic tissue invasion), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include inadequate deworming programs, immunosuppression, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water harboring infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can target renal vasculature and tubular epithelium, causing immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, vasculitis, and tubular necrosis. Viral replication within renal endothelial cells leads to inflammation, edema, and compromised renal perfusion, resulting in progressive decline in glomerular filtration rate and renal function. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli further exacerbates tissue damage and can lead to acute or chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や尿細管上皮を標的とし、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、血管炎、尿細管壊死を引き起こします。腎内皮細胞でのウイルス増殖により炎症、浮腫、腎灌流障害が生じ、糸球体濾過率が進行性に低下します。糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着がさらに組織障害を悪化させ、急性または慢性腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that can directly or indirectly damage renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that compound viral-induced renal injury. Immunosuppression and stress may predispose horses to more severe renal involvement.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生する。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こす。主な原因菌には大腸菌、連鎖球菌、ブドウ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどがあり、未治療では腎機能障害に至る。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections from cystitis or urethritis, hematogenous bacterial spread from distant infection sites, and urolithiasis causing urinary stasis. Secondary contributing factors include immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, urinary tract obstruction, nephrolithiasis, and anatomical abnormalities that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction of urine flow, progressive loss of nephron function, and formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) within the renal pelvis. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can result in unilateral or bilateral renal involvement with subsequent renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、尿路の閉塞、ネフロン機能の進行性喪失、腎盂内の真菌塊（ファンガスボール）形成が生じうる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により片側性または両側性の腎障害を来し、腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that gain access to the kidneys via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Secondary predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, chronic debilitating diseases, and corticosteroid administration that alter normal microbial flora and impair immune defenses.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If untreated, chronic infection can result in fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ上行性に細菌が感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、好中球浸潤、尿細管損傷、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を伴う炎症反応を引き起こします。未治療の場合、慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害、さらには敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale, which typically ascend from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infections is less common but possible.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if untreated. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性物質や感染性の侵襲により生じることが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from chronic infections, systemic vasculitis, and hemodynamic insults such as severe dehydration or endotoxemia. Ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) and pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria can also contribute.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. As the tumor expands, it may cause compression of adjacent renal tissue, hematuria, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常かつ制御不能な細胞増殖を伴います。最も多く報告される腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、所属リンパ節や肺などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の拡大に伴い、周囲の腎組織の圧迫、血尿、進行性の腎機能不全が生じます。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, and no specific genetic, environmental, or infectious risk factors have been definitively identified. Sporadic mutations in renal tubular or embryonal cells are thought to drive tumorigenesis. Nephroblastoma is more commonly seen in younger horses, suggesting possible congenital or developmental origins.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves dysfunction of the kidneys' ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired tubular reabsorption and secretion lead to electrolyte imbalances (particularly calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate), accumulation of uremic toxins, and disruption of vitamin D metabolism. Progressive nephron loss results in secondary hyperparathyroidism, renal osteodystrophy, and metabolic acidosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄の腎調節機能の障害を伴う。尿細管の再吸収・分泌障害により電解質異常（特にカルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩）、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積、ビタミンD代謝の破綻が生じる。進行性のネフロン喪失により、二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症、腎性骨異栄養症、代謝性アシドーシスが引き起こされる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, and chronic pyelonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, oxalate-containing plant ingestion, hypercalcemia, and age-related nephron degeneration. Nutritional imbalances such as excessive dietary calcium or phosphorus can also contribute to renal metabolic derangements.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can impair renal tubular function and structural integrity in horses. Chronic imbalances, especially excessive dietary phosphorus relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), lead to renal calcium deposition, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive tubular degeneration. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further contributing to renal mineralization and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 特にビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡は、馬の腎尿細管機能および構造的完全性を損ないます。特にカルシウムに対するリンの過剰摂取（Ca:P比の逆転）は、腎臓へのカルシウム沈着、腎石灰化症、進行性の尿細管変性を引き起こします。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発生し、腎臓の石灰化および線維化をさらに悪化させることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include chronic dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus intake (e.g., high-grain diets), calcium deficiency, and deficiencies of vitamins A or D. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of oxalate-rich forages (e.g., tropical grasses) that bind dietary calcium, leading to chronic hypocalcemia and compensatory renal changes.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Depending on the specific mutation, pathological changes may include renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, or tubular dysfunction, resulting in chronic kidney disease with azotemia and electrolyte imbalances. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional renal parenchyma ultimately lead to renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能および濃縮機能の障害を引き起こす。特定の変異により、腎異形成、多発性嚢胞腎、または尿細管機能障害などの病理変化が生じ、高窒素血症や電解質異常を伴う慢性腎臓病に至る。進行性の線維化と機能的腎実質の喪失により、最終的に腎不全に進行する。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting renal development or function, such as renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease. Certain breeds may have higher predisposition due to limited gene pools. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate disease progression in genetically predisposed individuals.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of nephrons, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, reduced glomerular filtration rate, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の自己抗原に対する自己抗体や自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、ネフロンの進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が発生します。慢性的な炎症は線維化、糸球体濾過率の低下、進行性腎不全へと至ります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation resulting in loss of self-tolerance to renal antigens, potentially triggered by preceding infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), systemic autoimmune conditions, or chronic antigenic stimulation. Secondary causes include drug-induced immune reactions (e.g., NSAIDs), immune complex deposition from equine infectious anemia or other chronic infections, and genetic predisposition in certain individuals.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired filtration, concentration ability, and electrolyte balance, ultimately resulting in chronic renal failure. Accumulation of uremic toxins and loss of endocrine functions (erythropoietin, vitamin D activation) contribute to systemic manifestations.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性悪化を伴います。これにより濾過機能、濃縮能、電解質バランスが障害され、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。尿毒症性毒素の蓄積およびエリスロポエチンやビタミンD活性化などの内分泌機能の喪失が全身症状に寄与します。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), age-related degenerative changes, and idiopathic renal fibrosis. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, prolonged ischemia, systemic diseases (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes disruption of renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, urine leakage, and inflammation. The right kidney in horses is more protected by the ribs, while the left kidney is more mobile and potentially more susceptible to displacement injuries. Secondary complications include perirenal hematoma formation, uroperitoneum, retroperitoneal abscessation, and potential ischemic necrosis of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、被膜、または血管茎が損傷を受け、出血、尿漏出、炎症が生じる。馬では右腎は肋骨に保護されているが、左腎はより可動性があり転位損傷を受けやすい。続発性合併症として腎周囲血腫、尿腹症、後腹膜膿瘍形成、腎組織の虚血性壊死が起こりうる。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects, iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy, and rarely rib fractures with fragment displacement into the kidney.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他の馬からの蹴り、運動中や競技中の転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる腹部・腰部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として、鋭利な物体による穿通創、経皮的腎生検時の医原性損傷、まれに肋骨骨折の骨片による腎損傷がある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as excessive flank watching, stretching, frequent posturing to urinate, or discomfort signs) associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction. Renal pathology such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia can stimulate visceral pain receptors, leading to characteristic behavioral changes. Chronic renal irritation may also alter autonomic nervous system signaling, resulting in persistent behavioral abnormalities even when overt clinical signs of renal failure are minimal.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連した異常行動（過度な側腹部注視、伸展姿勢、頻繁な排尿姿勢、不快感の兆候など）を伴います。腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの腎病変が内臓痛受容体を刺激し、特徴的な行動変化を引き起こします。慢性的な腎刺激は自律神経系のシグナル伝達を変化させ、明らかな腎不全の臨床兆候が最小限であっても持続的な行動異常を引き起こすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), pyelonephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and renal trauma causing visceral pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, chronic urinary tract infections, toxin-induced nephropathy (e.g., aminoglycoside toxicity, NSAID overuse), and referred pain from adjacent structures.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Leptospira spp. induce inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive nephron destruction, leading to impaired renal function. Chronic infection can result in pyelonephritis, interstitial nephritis, fibrosis, and potentially renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、アクチノバチルス・エクーリ、レプトスピラなどの病原体が炎症、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こし、腎機能障害をもたらす。慢性感染は腎盂腎炎、間質性腎炎、線維化を引き起こし、未治療の場合は腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli) from the lower urinary tract, hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and Leptospira spp. infection. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder dysfunction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and nephrolithiasis that promotes bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or establish in the renal parenchyma. The parasites cause granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, tubular necrosis, and fibrosis of the kidney, leading to impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also cause thrombosis, ischemia, and secondary bacterial infections.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫は肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、尿細管壊死、腎臓の線維化を引き起こし、腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、虚血、および二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasitic larvae to the kidneys, most notably Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode causing opportunistic granulomatous nephritis), Strongylus vulgaris larvae (aberrant larval migration via mesenteric arteries), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or heavy parasite burden facilitating aberrant migration, and concurrent bacterial infection of damaged renal tissue.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause immune-mediated or direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelium and glomeruli, leading to vasculitis, interstitial nephritis, and impaired renal function. Immune complex deposition in glomerular basement membranes may further compromise filtration, resulting in proteinuria, azotemia, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV-1）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮や糸球体に直接的な細胞傷害または免疫介在性損傷を引き起こし、血管炎、間質性腎炎、腎機能障害をもたらす。糸球体基底膜への免疫複合体沈着により濾過機能がさらに低下し、蛋白尿、高窒素血症、進行性腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus-1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other equine viral agents that exhibit renal tropism or induce vasculitis. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, dehydration, concurrent bacterial infections, and nephrotoxic drug administration during viral illness.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な原因菌には大腸菌、連鎖球菌、ブドウ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections, urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urinary catheterization, immunosuppression, bladder paralysis, anatomical abnormalities, and conditions causing incomplete bladder emptying.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, causing progressive renal dysfunction, obstruction, and potential formation of fungal concretions (fungal balls). Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can contribute to renal involvement, with immunosuppression being a key predisposing factor.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、進行性の腎機能障害、尿路閉塞、および真菌塊（ファンガスボール）の形成が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染が腎への波及に関与し、免疫抑制が主要な素因となる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade renal tissue. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (due to corticosteroid use, systemic illness, or stress), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary tract obstruction.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を介した上行性細菌感染によって生じ、まれに血行性播種によっても起こります。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害を招き、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Mares may be more predisposed due to shorter urethral length facilitating bacterial ascent.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. Inflammatory infiltrates and edema impair glomerular filtration, tubular reabsorption, and secretion, leading to progressive loss of renal function, azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially renal failure. Chronic inflammation may result in fibrosis and irreversible structural damage to the nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の要因により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に損傷が生じる疾患です。炎症性浸潤や浮腫により糸球体濾過、尿細管再吸収・分泌機能が障害され、高窒素血症、電解質異常、さらには腎不全に至る可能性があります。慢性炎症は線維化を引き起こし、ネフロンに不可逆的な構造的損傷をもたらすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), toxin exposure (e.g., heavy metals, oak toxicosis), dehydration, septicemia, and immune complex deposition associated with chronic infections or systemic disease.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass progressively replaces normal renal parenchyma, impairing kidney function and potentially metastasizing to lungs, liver, and other organs. Local invasion can obstruct the ureter or renal vasculature, leading to hydronephrosis, hematuria, and paraneoplastic syndromes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は腎臓内の細胞が無制御に増殖するもので、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫が最も多い。腫瘍塊が正常な腎実質を進行性に置換し、腎機能を障害するとともに、肺や肝臓などへ転移する可能性がある。局所浸潤により尿管や腎血管が閉塞し、水腎症、血尿、腫瘍随伴症候群を引き起こすことがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though spontaneous neoplastic transformation of renal epithelial or embryonal cells is considered the primary cause. Potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic renal irritation or inflammation, and advancing age. No specific environmental carcinogens or infectious agents have been definitively linked to equine renal tumors.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disruption of electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys lose their ability to properly regulate calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic cases may lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and osteodystrophy (rubber jaw).
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能の障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物の排泄が乱れる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウムまたは低カルシウム血症、高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性例では腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、骨異栄養症（ラバージョー）に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic renal failure from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), chronic nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, and age-related renal degeneration. Secondary causes include prolonged dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, oxalate-containing plant ingestion (e.g., Oxalis species), and vitamin D imbalances. Pre-existing conditions such as equine metabolic syndrome or Cushing's disease may predispose horses to renal metabolic dysfunction.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or tubular degeneration in horses. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios (especially excess phosphorus or oxalate ingestion) promote calcium deposition in renal tissue, causing progressive nephropathy. Chronic deficiency states lead to renal tubular necrosis, interstitial fibrosis, and ultimately compromised renal filtration and concentrating ability.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取により、腎尿細管機能が障害され、腎石灰化や尿細管変性が生じます。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡は腎組織へのカルシウム沈着を促進し、進行性腎症を引き起こします。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎尿細管壊死、間質性線維化を招き、最終的に腎濾過能力と濃縮能力が低下します。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus intake relative to calcium, prolonged feeding of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., tropical grasses, sorrel), and deficiencies of vitamin A or vitamin D. Secondary causes include chronic consumption of poor-quality forage, lack of mineral supplementation, and conditions that impair nutrient absorption such as chronic intestinal disease.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation disrupts normal kidney architecture. Progressive fibrosis and inflammation ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異により、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能の障害、代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。腎形成不全や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な腎発生や嚢胞形成が正常な腎臓構造を破壊します。進行性の線維化と炎症が最終的に慢性腎不全をもたらします。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting genes essential for normal renal development and function. Specific breeds may have higher prevalence due to limited genetic diversity and founder effects. Secondary factors such as dehydration, infection, or nephrotoxin exposure can accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components and tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated attack leads to glomerulonephritis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, and progressive renal damage. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue injury, resulting in impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎抗原に対して自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生する。免疫複合体の沈着や抗体介在性の直接攻撃により糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が引き起こされ、進行性の腎障害をもたらす。補体の活性化と炎症細胞の浸潤がさらに組織障害を悪化させ、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の低下を招く。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions. Secondary causes include persistent immune complex formation from other diseases such as equine purpura hemorrhagica or systemic lupus-like syndromes. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease susceptibility.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic nephron loss triggers compensatory hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, which paradoxically accelerates further damage. This ultimately results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and end-stage renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能が障害される。慢性的なネフロン喪失により残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過が起こり、さらなる損傷が加速される。最終的に高窒素血症、電解質異常、末期腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic pyelonephritis, and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include systemic conditions such as hemodynamic compromise from severe dehydration or shock, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oxalate-containing plants, red maple leaves) can also contribute.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature. This results in hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), disruption of the collecting system with potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum or retroperitoneal urine accumulation), and subsequent inflammation. Severe cases may lead to hypovolemic shock, secondary infection, or progressive loss of renal function in the affected kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 側腹部や腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、被膜、または血管系に直接的損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下または腎周囲血腫）、集合系の破壊による尿漏出（尿腹症または後腹膜への尿貯留）、およびそれに続く炎症が引き起こされる。重症例では循環血液量減少性ショック、二次感染、または患側腎の進行性機能喪失に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collision with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from fencing materials, sharp objects, or fractured ribs lacerating the kidney. Foaling injuries, recumbent horses being stepped on, and iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures are less common causes.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, stretching, flank-watching, or discomfort signs) associated with underlying renal pathology including nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal inflammation. Pain or irritation originating from the kidneys or ureters triggers visceral afferent nerve stimulation, leading to characteristic postural and behavioral changes. Chronic renal dysfunction may also cause electrolyte imbalances and uremia, further contributing to altered mentation and behavior.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、または慢性腎炎などの腎臓病変に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、伸展、側腹部注視、不快感の兆候など）を伴います。腎臓や尿管からの痛みや刺激が内臓求心性神経を刺激し、特徴的な姿勢や行動の変化を引き起こします。慢性腎機能障害は電解質異常や尿毒症も引き起こし、精神状態や行動の変化にさらに寄与します。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic interstitial nephritis. Secondary causes may involve urinary tract infections ascending to the kidneys, toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, pigweed) or drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), and ischemic renal injury due to dehydration or hemodynamic compromise.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus spp. cause inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infections may result in pyelonephritis, fibrosis, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、アクチノバチルス属などの細菌が炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害をもたらす。慢性感染は腎盂腎炎、線維化、最終的に腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis, bladder dysfunction, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, chronic dehydration, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that promote bacterial colonization and stasis.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and potentially renal fibrosis. Larval migration through renal arteries (as with Strongylus vulgaris) can also cause thromboembolism and ischemic damage to the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に侵入・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管の破壊、間質性腎炎、さらに腎線維化が引き起こされる。幼虫が腎動脈を通じて移行する場合は、血栓塞栓症や腎臓の虚血性障害も生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic renal tropism), migrating larvae of Strongylus vulgaris, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor deworming programs, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water that harbors infective larvae or free-living nematodes.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause immune-mediated vasculitis and direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular and glomerular endothelial cells, leading to nephritis and impaired renal function. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli and viral-induced thrombosis of renal vasculature may result in glomerulonephritis, interstitial nephritis, and potentially acute or chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが免疫介在性血管炎や腎尿細管・糸球体内皮細胞への直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、腎炎および腎機能障害をもたらす。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着やウイルス誘発性の腎血管血栓症により、糸球体腎炎、間質性腎炎、さらには急性または慢性腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus-1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral pathogens that have tropism for renal vasculature or parenchyma. Secondary causes include immune-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by persistent viral antigenemia and superimposed bacterial infections in immunocompromised kidneys.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common pathogens include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, leading to impaired renal function if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な起因菌は大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどで、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections, urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, and hematogenous bacterial spread from distant infection sites. Secondary factors include immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, urinary tract obstruction, anatomical abnormalities, and conditions predisposing to urine retention such as bladder paralysis or neoplasia.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can spread fungi to the kidneys, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質および/または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、閉塞、膿瘍形成、進行性の腎機能低下を招く可能性があります。血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行性感染により、特に免疫不全状態の馬で腎臓に真菌が到達します。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other fungi that invade the renal tissue. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (e.g., corticosteroid use, concurrent illness such as Cushing's disease), indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitated general condition.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属などの日和見真菌による腎組織への感染です。二次的原因および素因として、長期の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制（副腎皮質ステロイドの使用、クッシング病などの併発疾患）、留置尿道カテーテル、全身状態の衰弱などが挙げられます。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response leading to tissue damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal architecture. If bilateral or severe, it can lead to impaired renal function, azotemia, and potentially renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症反応が誘発され、組織損傷、膿瘍形成、腎構造の進行性破壊が起こります。両側性または重度の場合、腎機能障害、高窒素血症、さらには腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and other gram-negative bacteria ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common but possible route.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium, leading to impaired filtration, tubular dysfunction, and progressive loss of nephron function. Inflammatory cell infiltration causes edema, fibrosis, and vascular compromise, resulting in reduced glomerular filtration rate, proteinuria, electrolyte imbalances, and potential azotemia. Chronic inflammation can progress to irreversible renal fibrosis and renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、尿細管機能障害、ネフロンの進行性喪失を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤により浮腫、線維化、血管障害が生じ、糸球体濾過率の低下、蛋白尿、電解質異常、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性炎症は不可逆的な腎線維化および腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals. Secondary causes include systemic sepsis, endotoxemia, dehydration, hemolytic conditions, and immune complex deposition from chronic infections or neoplasia. Renal ischemia from shock or severe colic can also contribute to inflammatory kidney injury.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to other organs including lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Progressive tumor growth leads to compression of normal renal tissue, potential obstruction of urine flow, and eventual renal insufficiency if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂内の細胞の異常増殖を伴います。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、肺・肝臓・リンパ節などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の進行性増大により正常腎組織の圧迫、尿流の閉塞、そして両側性または対側腎が障害された場合には腎不全に至ります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown and is likely multifactorial, potentially involving genetic predisposition, spontaneous somatic mutations, and possible environmental carcinogen exposure. Nephroblastoma is more commonly seen in younger horses, suggesting a congenital or developmental origin, while renal cell carcinoma tends to occur in older horses. No specific infectious or hereditary cause has been definitively established.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves dysfunction of the kidneys' ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired tubular reabsorption or secretion leads to abnormal levels of calcium, phosphorus, and other metabolites, potentially resulting in renal tubular acidosis, hypercalcemia, or mineral imbalances. Chronic dysfunction can progress to nephrocalcinosis, renal fibrosis, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎臓による電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄の調節機能が障害される疾患である。尿細管の再吸収や分泌の障害により、カルシウム、リン、その他の代謝産物の異常が生じ、腎尿細管性アシドーシスや高カルシウム血症、ミネラル不均衡を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎石灰化症、腎線維化、最終的に腎不全へと進行しうる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants, and hereditary tubular defects. Secondary causes include dehydration, prolonged hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, and endocrine disorders such as hyperparathyroidism that alter renal mineral handling.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-containing plant ingestion, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or nephrosis in horses. Chronic imbalances cause mineral deposition within renal parenchyma, tubular degeneration, and progressive loss of renal concentrating and excretory ability. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop due to calcium-phosphorus imbalance, further exacerbating renal mineralization and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸含有植物の摂取により、腎尿細管機能が障害され、腎石灰化症や腎症が生じます。慢性的な栄養不均衡は腎実質内へのミネラル沈着、尿細管変性、および腎濃縮・排泄能の進行性喪失を引き起こします。カルシウム・リンの不均衡により二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発生し、腎の石灰化と線維化がさらに悪化する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiency or excess of calcium, phosphorus, vitamin A, or vitamin D, as well as chronic ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Oxalis, Rumex) that bind calcium and cause renal oxalate deposition. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of high-grain/low-forage diets causing calcium-phosphorus imbalance, poor-quality forage, and inadequate access to trace minerals and vitamins.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and eventual chronic renal failure. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal embryological development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional parenchyma result in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、最終的には慢性腎不全に至ります。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、胎生期の異常な発達や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化と機能的実質の喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting renal development or maintenance, such as genes involved in nephron differentiation or polycystin proteins. Breed predispositions have been noted, and consanguineous breeding increases the risk of homozygosity for deleterious alleles. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate progression of the underlying genetic defect.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial inflammation. This results in progressive glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, causing disruption of the glomerular basement membrane, proteinuria, and eventual loss of nephron function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate renal tissue damage, potentially leading to chronic kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着および/または尿細管間質の炎症を引き起こします。これにより進行性の糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じ、糸球体基底膜の破壊、蛋白尿、最終的にはネフロン機能の喪失につながります。補体活性化と炎症細胞の浸潤がさらに腎組織の障害を悪化させ、慢性腎臓病に進行する可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, which may be triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, or other systemic immune-mediated conditions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from persistent antigenic stimulation, molecular mimicry between infectious agents and renal tissue, and genetic predisposition to autoimmunity in certain individuals.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal tubular and/or glomerular structures, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and secretion functions. Chronic degeneration results in nephron loss, fibrosis, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure. Accumulation of uremic toxins such as BUN and creatinine occurs as functional renal mass declines below a critical threshold.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、腎尿細管および/または糸球体構造の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・再吸収・分泌機能の障害を引き起こします。慢性的な変性はネフロンの喪失、線維化、そして最終的には腎不全へと進行します。機能的腎組織が臨界閾値を下回ると、BUNやクレアチニンなどの尿毒症性毒素が蓄積します。
causes: Primary causes include nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemia, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include systemic diseases such as leptospirosis, equine infectious anemia, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, amyloidosis, and chronic dehydration or hemodynamic compromise leading to prolonged renal hypoperfusion.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney causes disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potentially urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular disruption may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage or eventual renal infarction and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性外傷により腎実質、腎被膜、または血管茎が損傷され、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。それに伴う炎症、虚血、および二次感染が腎機能を障害する可能性がある。重症例では血管損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞、線維化に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or accidents during transport. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from external objects, iatrogenic injury during surgical or percutaneous procedures, and rarely fractures of adjacent ribs or vertebrae causing direct renal laceration.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他の馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、輸送中の事故などによる腹部鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として、外部物体による穿通性損傷、外科的または経皮的処置中の医原性損傷、まれに隣接する肋骨や椎骨の骨折による直接的な腎裂傷がある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, nephritis, or renal neoplasia. Pain signals from the renal capsule or ureter stimulate visceral afferent pathways, leading to behavioral changes including flank-watching, stretching, posturing to urinate frequently, and reluctance to move. Chronic discomfort may also alter the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, contributing to anxiety-like behaviors and altered temperament.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓病変による慢性的な腎痛や不快感から生じる異常行動を伴います。腎被膜や尿管からの疼痛信号が内臓求心性経路を刺激し、脇腹を見る行動、伸展姿勢、頻繁な排尿姿勢、運動拒否などの行動変化を引き起こします。慢性的な不快感は視床下部-下垂体-副腎軸にも影響を及ぼし、不安様行動や気質の変化を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic interstitial nephritis, pyelonephritis, renal cysts, and renal neoplasia that produce persistent renal or ureteral pain. Secondary causes may involve urinary tract obstruction, renal ischemia, toxin-induced nephropathy (such as aminoglycoside or NSAID toxicity), and referred pain from adjacent structures. Metabolic imbalances including hypercalcemia and chronic dehydration may predispose horses to renal pathology and associated behavioral changes.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tubules and glomeruli, impairing filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic infection can result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。細菌感染により炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、腎尿細管および糸球体の進行性破壊が生じ、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能が障害されます。慢性感染は線維化、腎不全を引き起こし、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder paralysis, and catheterization-related contamination that predispose to bacterial colonization of the kidneys.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms, most commonly Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix) or migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae, invade the renal parenchyma. The parasites induce granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, and fibrosis within the kidneys, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Aberrant larval migration can also cause vasculitis and thrombosis of renal vasculature, resulting in ischemic damage and nephritis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、主にHalicephalobus gingivalis（ハリセファロバス）や普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫などの寄生虫が腎実質に侵入することで発生する。寄生虫は肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、線維化を引き起こし、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。異所性幼虫移行により腎血管の血管炎や血栓症が生じ、虚血性障害や腎炎を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode capable of opportunistic invasion), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Infection typically occurs through ingestion or wound contamination with larvae from contaminated soil or environment.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to immune-mediated glomerulonephritis and interstitial nephritis. Immune complex deposition within the renal vasculature and glomerular basement membrane results in progressive inflammation, impaired glomerular filtration, and potential renal insufficiency. In severe cases, vasculitis-induced ischemic damage further compromises renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎や間質性腎炎を誘発する。免疫複合体が腎血管や糸球体基底膜に沈着し、炎症の進行、糸球体濾過機能の低下、腎機能不全を招く。重症例では血管炎による虚血性障害がさらに腎機能を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that have renal tropism or cause secondary immune-mediated renal damage. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial superinfection that exacerbates viral-induced renal injury.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma (pyelonephritis) typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons, potentially leading to renal insufficiency or failure. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こし、腎機能不全や腎不全に至る可能性があります。一般的な起因菌には大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、コリネバクテリウム属、アクチノバチルス・エクーリなどが含まれます。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary or predisposing factors include immunosuppression, urinary tract obstruction, catheterization, bladder paralysis, and conditions that impair normal urine flow such as nephrolithiasis or ureteral strictures.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms (commonly Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or Mucor spp.) colonize the renal parenchyma, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. Hyphae may invade renal vasculature causing thrombosis and infarction, resulting in progressive destruction of renal tissue. In severe cases, fungal masses (fungal balls) can obstruct the renal pelvis or ureters, leading to hydronephrosis and renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 真菌（主にAspergillus属、Candida属、Mucor属など）が腎実質に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。菌糸が腎血管に侵入して血栓症や梗塞を引き起こし、腎組織の進行性破壊をもたらす。重症例では真菌塊（ファンガスボール）が腎盂や尿管を閉塞し、水腎症や腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections (Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., Cryptococcus spp.) that gain access via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (corticosteroid use, concurrent illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitated general condition. Secondary causes include disseminated systemic mycosis originating from respiratory or gastrointestinal sources.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and ultimately renal failure if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、水腎症を引き起こし、両側性の場合や対側腎が障害されている場合は最終的に腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infections.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if left untreated. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン機能を障害し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性物質や感染性因子による障害に起因することが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic diseases (e.g., purpura hemorrhagica), septicemia, endotoxemia, and hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury. Ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) can also contribute to renal inflammation.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can cause progressive destruction of normal renal tissue, obstruction of urine flow, and potential metastasis to lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. As the tumor enlarges, it compromises renal function, may invade surrounding structures, and can lead to paraneoplastic syndromes including weight loss and anemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常で制御不能な細胞増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎組織の進行性破壊、尿流の閉塞、肺・肝臓・リンパ節への転移を引き起こしうる。腫瘍が増大すると腎機能が低下し、周囲組織への浸潤や、体重減少・貧血などの傍腫瘍症候群を引き起こすことがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistently identified predisposing factors. Primary renal tumors such as renal cell carcinoma and nephroblastoma arise from malignant transformation of renal epithelial or embryonal cells, possibly due to spontaneous genetic mutations. Secondary renal involvement may occur through metastasis from other primary tumors or as part of multicentric lymphoma.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が障害される疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、または代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能障害は腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、および進行性のネフロン喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, and excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants that place metabolic stress on the kidneys.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium), can impair normal renal tubular function and glomerular integrity in horses. Imbalances in the calcium-phosphorus ratio or excessive dietary oxalates can lead to nephrocalcinosis, tubular degeneration, and progressive renal insufficiency. Chronic deficiency states may result in dystrophic mineralization of renal parenchyma and impaired electrolyte homeostasis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏は、馬の腎尿細管機能および糸球体の健全性を損なう可能性があります。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡や過剰なシュウ酸塩の摂取は、腎石灰化症、尿細管変性、進行性腎不全を引き起こします。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎実質の異栄養性石灰化および電解質恒常性の障害をもたらすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances in calcium and phosphorus (especially inverse Ca:P ratios), excessive oxalate-containing plants (e.g., tropical grasses such as Setaria or Panicum), and deficiencies in vitamin A or vitamin D. Secondary causes include chronic poor-quality forage, inadequate mineral supplementation, and prolonged grazing on nutrient-depleted pastures.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and electrolyte imbalances. Examples include renal tubular dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and inflammation ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異が関与し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、電解質異常を引き起こします。腎尿細管異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な発達や嚢胞形成が正常な腎構造を破壊します。進行性の線維化と炎症が最終的に慢性腎不全につながります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Specific conditions include renal tubular dysplasia (reported in certain breeds) and polycystic kidney disease. Environmental factors and secondary infections may accelerate disease progression but are not the primary cause.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、正常な腎発達と機能に関与する遺伝子の遺伝性変異であり、多くの場合常染色体劣性遺伝です。特定の疾患には腎尿細管異形成（特定の品種で報告）や多発性嚢胞腎が含まれます。環境要因や二次感染は疾患の進行を促進する可能性がありますが、主要な原因ではありません。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition within glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive damage to the glomerular basement membrane and tubular structures. The resulting chronic inflammation leads to glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, fibrosis, and progressive loss of renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の自己抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、糸球体基底膜および尿細管構造の進行性障害が引き起こされます。結果として慢性炎症が糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、線維化、および進行性の腎機能低下をもたらします。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by preceding infectious diseases (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), chronic antigenic stimulation, or drug reactions. Secondary factors include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune conditions, genetic predisposition, and chronic inflammatory states that promote molecular mimicry or epitope spreading.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephrons, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired renal filtration, concentration ability, and waste excretion. Chronic insult results in irreversible loss of functional renal tissue, culminating in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The compensatory hypertrophy of remaining nephrons may temporarily maintain function until a critical mass of tissue is lost.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロンの進行性劣化を伴い、腎濾過機能、濃縮能力、老廃物排泄の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害により機能的腎組織の不可逆的喪失が生じ、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的に腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンの代償性肥大により、組織の臨界量が失われるまで一時的に機能が維持されることがある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis. Secondary causes include chronic ischemia, recurrent pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related senile nephrosclerosis. Idiopathic renal degeneration is also recognized, particularly in older horses.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney results in parenchymal disruption, subcapsular or perirenal hemorrhage, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The injury may range from minor contusions with microhemorrhage to complete renal fracture or vascular pedicle avulsion, leading to significant hemorrhage, uroperitoneum, and secondary inflammation or infection. Compensatory mechanisms by the contralateral kidney may maintain renal function if the injury is unilateral.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的外傷または穿通性外傷により腎実質の損傷が生じ、被膜下出血や腎周囲出血、さらに後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こり得る。損傷は軽度の挫傷から腎の完全破裂や血管茎の断裂まで多岐にわたり、重篤な出血、尿腹症、二次的な炎症や感染を引き起こす可能性がある。一側性損傷の場合、対側腎の代償機能により腎機能は維持されることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collision with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes may include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる腹部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として、鋭利な物体による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、経皮的腎生検や外科手術中の医原性損傷が挙げられる。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or irritability) arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, nephritis, or renal neoplasia. Afferent pain signals from the renal capsule or parenchyma lead to visceral pain responses manifesting as behavioral changes. Chronic irritation of the renal system may also cause referred pain to the flank and lumbar regions, further altering the horse's demeanor and performance.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓病変による慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感から生じる異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を気にする行動、易刺激性など）を伴います。腎被膜や実質からの求心性疼痛信号が内臓痛反応を引き起こし、行動変化として現れます。慢性的な腎系の刺激は脇腹や腰部への関連痛を引き起こし、馬の気性やパフォーマンスをさらに変化させます。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic nephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and pyelonephritis causing persistent renal discomfort. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, hydronephrosis, renal toxicity from NSAIDs or aminoglycosides, and chronic urinary tract infections that contribute to ongoing renal pain and associated behavioral changes.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to nephritis or pyelonephritis, causing tubular damage, interstitial inflammation, and potentially abscess formation. Progressive infection can impair glomerular filtration and tubular function, leading to azotemia and renal insufficiency if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性伝播により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が誘発され、腎炎や腎盂腎炎を引き起こし、尿細管の損傷、間質性炎症、さらには膿瘍形成に至ることがあります。感染が進行すると糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害され、未治療の場合は高窒素血症や腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and concurrent systemic infections such as strangles or neonatal septicemia.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or lodge within the renal parenchyma, renal pelvis, or perirenal tissues. The parasites cause direct mechanical damage to nephrons, provoke granulomatous or eosinophilic inflammatory responses, and may lead to progressive renal fibrosis, obstruction of urine flow, and impaired renal function. Vascular damage from migrating larvae (particularly S. vulgaris) can also cause renal infarction and hemorrhage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質、腎盂、または腎周囲組織に移行・寄生することで発症する。寄生虫はネフロンへの直接的な機械的損傷を引き起こし、肉芽腫性または好酸球性炎症反応を誘発し、進行性の腎線維化、尿流閉塞、腎機能障害をもたらす。特にS. vulgarisの移行幼虫による血管障害は腎梗塞や出血を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through mesenteric and renal vasculature, infection with Halicephalobus gingivalis (a saprophytic nematode capable of invading the kidneys), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming programs, and contaminated environments that increase exposure to infective larval stages.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can target renal vasculature and tubular epithelium, causing immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, and interstitial nephritis. Viral replication within endothelial cells leads to vasculitis, impaired renal perfusion, and progressive loss of glomerular filtration. Immune complex deposition further exacerbates renal parenchymal damage and inflammation.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や尿細管上皮を標的とし、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、間質性腎炎を引き起こす。内皮細胞内でのウイルス増殖が血管炎を引き起こし、腎灌流障害と糸球体濾過率の低下をもたらす。免疫複合体の沈着がさらに腎実質の障害と炎症を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and other nephrotrophic viruses that directly infect renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and concurrent bacterial infections that compound viral-induced renal injury. Stress, immunosuppression, and co-infections may predispose horses to renal involvement.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobaculum suis, Corynebacterium spp., Streptococcus spp., and other gram-negative enteric bacteria, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染により発生し、まれに血行性に波及することもある。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こす。主な起因菌には大腸菌、Actinobaculum suis、Corynebacterium属、Streptococcus属などのグラム陰性腸内細菌が含まれ、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至る。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis, urethral obstruction, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, urinary stasis, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potentially formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) that can obstruct urine outflow. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract may contribute to renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害が生じ、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）が形成されて尿路閉塞を引き起こすことがある。原発巣からの血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行性感染が腎への波及経路となる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (e.g., corticosteroid use), indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitation from chronic illness. Pre-existing renal damage or urinary stasis may also facilitate fungal colonization.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and impaired renal function. Chronic infection can result in progressive nephron loss, fibrosis, and potentially renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、腎機能障害をもたらします。慢性感染は進行性のネフロン喪失や線維化を引き起こし、両側性の場合は腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is ascending bacterial infection, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, or Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common secondary cause.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
