pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive damage to the renal tubules, interstitium, and potentially the glomeruli. If untreated, chronic infection can result in renal fibrosis, impaired glomerular filtration, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発症します。感染により腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成が生じ、腎尿細管、間質、さらには糸球体に進行性の損傷をもたらします。未治療の場合、慢性感染は腎線維化、糸球体濾過率の低下、最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal or bladder conditions that promote bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or directly invade the renal parenchyma. The parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, and progressive nephritis, potentially leading to renal insufficiency. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also cause thrombosis, ischemia, and infarction of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質に移行・侵入することで発生する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、進行性腎炎が引き起こされ、腎不全に至る可能性がある。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、虚血、腎組織の梗塞を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasitic larvae such as Strongylus vulgaris through the mesenteric and renal vasculature, direct renal invasion by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic parasitic behavior), and rarely Dioctophyme renale infection. Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring the parasites.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause immune-mediated or direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelium and glomeruli, leading to impaired renal filtration and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in glomerular capillaries may result in glomerulonephritis, progressive renal insufficiency, and potentially acute kidney injury. Vasculitis associated with viral infection can further compromise renal blood flow and exacerbate tissue damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV-1）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが、免疫介在性または直接的な細胞障害により腎尿細管上皮や糸球体に損傷を引き起こし、腎濾過機能の低下や尿細管壊死をもたらす。糸球体毛細血管への免疫複合体沈着により糸球体腎炎が生じ、進行性の腎機能不全や急性腎障害に至ることがある。ウイルス感染に伴う血管炎が腎血流をさらに低下させ、組織障害を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include infection with equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), or other systemic viral infections that have renal tropism or cause secondary immune-mediated renal injury. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, viral-induced vasculitis, systemic inflammatory response, and concurrent dehydration or nephrotoxic drug administration that exacerbates viral renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common pathogens include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, which trigger neutrophilic infiltration and may lead to impaired renal function if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生する。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こす。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどが一般的な原因菌であり、好中球浸潤を誘発し、両側性の場合は腎機能障害に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urolithiasis), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and direct inoculation via contaminated catheters. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urinary stasis, urolithiasis, immunosuppression, anatomical abnormalities, and prolonged recumbency or hospitalization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. Fungal hyphae may invade renal vasculature causing thrombosis and ischemic necrosis, with progressive destruction of nephrons resulting in impaired renal function. Fungal balls (mycetomas) may form within the renal pelvis, causing obstruction and hydronephrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。真菌菌糸が腎血管に侵入して血栓症や虚血性壊死を生じ、ネフロンの進行性破壊により腎機能が障害される。腎盂内に真菌球（菌腫）が形成され、閉塞や水腎症を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary infection is caused by opportunistic fungi such as Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly other molds and yeasts that reach the kidney via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness. Secondary causes include pre-existing renal damage or urinary tract obstruction facilitating fungal colonization.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If bilateral or left untreated, it can lead to renal insufficiency or failure due to loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発症します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。両側性または未治療の場合、機能的ネフロンの喪失により腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Proteus spp., and Streptococcus spp., typically ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urinary catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is less common but possible.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. This leads to impaired filtration, proteinuria, azotemia, and electrolyte imbalances. Chronic inflammation can progress to fibrosis, nephron loss, and ultimately renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じる疾患である。これにより濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症、電解質異常が引き起こされる。慢性炎症は線維化やネフロンの喪失を招き、最終的に腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic sepsis, dehydration, and exposure to toxic plants or heavy metals.
causes_ja: 主な原因には細菌感染（レプトスピラ症、連鎖球菌感染症など）、ウイルス感染（馬伝染性貧血など）、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎がある。二次的原因としては腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系抗菌薬）、全身性敗血症、脱水、有毒植物や重金属への暴露が挙げられる。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass progressively replaces normal renal tissue, impairing kidney function and potentially metastasizing to lungs, liver, and other organs. Local invasion can obstruct the renal pelvis or ureter, leading to hydronephrosis, hematuria, and eventual renal failure if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍は、腎実質内の細胞が異常増殖するもので、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫が最も多い。腫瘍塊は正常な腎組織を徐々に置換し、腎機能を障害し、肺や肝臓などへ転移する可能性がある。局所浸潤により腎盂や尿管が閉塞し、水腎症、血尿、さらには両側性または対側腎が障害された場合は腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, and no specific risk factors have been clearly identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may affect the kidney as part of multicentric disease. Genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and exposure to environmental carcinogens have been hypothesized but remain unproven in equines.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves dysfunction of the kidneys' ability to properly regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, resulting in metabolic derangements such as hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction may lead to nephrocalcinosis, renal tubular acidosis, or secondary mineral imbalances affecting bone metabolism.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄を適切に調節する腎臓の機能障害を伴う。尿細管機能の障害によりカルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシスなどの代謝異常が引き起こされる。慢性的な機能障害は腎石灰化症、腎尿細管性アシドーシス、または骨代謝に影響を及ぼす二次的なミネラル不均衡を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, renal tubular acidosis, and excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants. Secondary causes include dehydration, nephrotoxic drug exposure (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic infections, and prolonged metabolic stress such as endurance exercise or prolonged anorexia.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium), can impair normal renal tubular function, glomerular integrity, and electrolyte homeostasis in horses. Chronic imbalances, especially excessive dietary phosphorus relative to calcium, can lead to calcium deposition in renal tissue (nephrocalcinosis), tubular degeneration, and progressive renal insufficiency. Prolonged deficiency or imbalance disrupts acid-base regulation and waste excretion, ultimately compromising overall renal architecture and function.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏は、馬の腎尿細管機能、糸球体の完全性、電解質恒常性を障害します。特にカルシウムに対するリンの過剰摂取は、腎組織へのカルシウム沈着（腎石灰化症）、尿細管変性、進行性腎不全を引き起こします。長期の欠乏や不均衡は酸塩基調節や老廃物排泄を妨げ、腎臓の構造と機能を損ないます。
causes: Primary causes include chronic dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus intake relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), vitamin A or D deficiency, and inadequate mineral supplementation. Secondary causes include poor-quality forage, prolonged feeding of bran-heavy or grain-heavy diets without appropriate calcium supplementation, and oxalate-rich pasture grasses that bind dietary calcium, reducing its bioavailability and leading to renal stress.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation disrupts normal kidney architecture. Progressive fibrosis and chronic kidney disease ensue as functional nephrons are lost over time.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造と機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能の障害、代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発育や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。機能的ネフロンの喪失に伴い、進行性の線維化と慢性腎臓病が発生します。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, and renal tubular acidosis, which may be breed-associated. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxin exposure, or concurrent infections can accelerate disease progression.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial regions. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive damage to the glomerular basement membrane, mesangium, and tubular structures. The resulting glomerulonephritis and/or interstitial nephritis leads to impaired renal filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質領域に免疫複合体が沈着する。これにより補体の活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、糸球体基底膜・メサンギウム・尿細管構造の進行性損傷が引き起こされる。結果として糸球体腎炎や間質性腎炎が生じ、腎濾過機能の障害、蛋白尿、腎機能の進行性低下をもたらす。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal tissue antigens, potentially triggered by preceding infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), chronic inflammatory conditions, or drug reactions. Secondary factors include genetic predisposition, molecular mimicry between microbial and renal antigens, and concurrent systemic autoimmune disorders such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndrome in horses.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic nephron loss triggers compensatory hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, which ultimately accelerates further damage. This progressive loss of functional renal tissue results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的なネフロン喪失は残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過を誘発し、最終的にさらなる損傷を加速させる。機能的腎組織の進行性喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and oxalate-containing plants like Oxalis or Halogeton), as well as age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, recurrent urinary tract infections, renal ischemia from prolonged hypotension, and systemic diseases such as equine metabolic syndrome or immune-mediated glomerulonephritis.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Direct blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney causes parenchymal disruption, subcapsular or perirenal hemorrhage, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, hematoma formation, and possible ischemia can lead to progressive renal damage, uroperitoneum, or secondary infection. In severe cases, renal vascular pedicle injury may cause life-threatening hemorrhage or complete renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎臓への直接的な鈍的外傷または穿通性外傷により、腎実質の損傷、被膜下または腎周囲の出血、そして後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じます。その結果、炎症、血腫形成、虚血が進行性の腎障害、尿腹症、または二次感染を引き起こす可能性があります。重度の場合、腎血管茎の損傷により致命的な出血や完全な腎梗塞が生じることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, and collisions with fixed objects. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from external objects, iatrogenic damage during percutaneous procedures, and rib fractures with fragments lacerating the kidney. Foals may sustain renal trauma during difficult births or from being stepped on.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or irritability) that arise secondary to renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic or acute renal disease, nephrolithiasis, or renal inflammation can stimulate visceral pain receptors, leading to behavioral changes that mimic colic or musculoskeletal discomfort. Uremia or electrolyte imbalances from impaired renal function may also contribute to altered mentation and abnormal behavior.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛みや機能障害に起因する異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、腹部を気にする行動、易刺激性など）を伴います。慢性または急性の腎疾患、腎結石、腎炎が内臓痛受容体を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系疾患に似た行動変化を引き起こします。腎機能障害による尿毒症や電解質異常も精神状態の変化や異常行動に寄与する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure leading to visceral pain and behavioral manifestations. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal cysts, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and severe dehydration causing renal ischemia. Referred pain from the renal capsule or urinary tract obstruction can also trigger behavioral abnormalities.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), tubular damage, interstitial edema, and abscess formation, which can progress to impaired glomerular filtration, renal insufficiency, and potentially sepsis if untreated. Chronic infections may result in fibrosis, renal scarring, and permanent loss of nephron function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。感染により炎症（腎盂腎炎）、尿細管障害、間質浮腫、膿瘍形成が生じ、糸球体濾過率の低下や腎不全、未治療の場合は敗血症に進行し得る。慢性感染は線維化、腎瘢痕化、ネフロン機能の永続的喪失を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage that predisposes to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms, most commonly Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix) or migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae, invade the renal parenchyma. The parasites cause granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, and fibrosis within the kidney, leading to progressive loss of renal function. Aberrant larval migration can also damage renal vasculature, causing thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、主にHalicephalobus gingivalis（Halicephalobus deletrix）や普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫などの寄生虫が腎実質に侵入することで発生します。寄生虫は肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、および腎臓内の線維化を引き起こし、腎機能の進行性低下をもたらします。異所性の幼虫移行は腎血管を損傷し、血栓症、梗塞、および二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすこともあります。
causes: Primary causes include infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a saprophytic nematode that can invade the kidneys), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can infect renal tissues, causing immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, tubular necrosis, and vasculitis within the kidneys. Viral replication in endothelial cells and renal parenchyma leads to inflammation, impaired glomerular filtration, and progressive renal dysfunction. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli further exacerbates tissue damage and compromises renal perfusion.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎組織に感染し、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、尿細管壊死、および腎血管炎を引き起こす。ウイルスが内皮細胞や腎実質で増殖することにより炎症が生じ、糸球体濾過機能が低下し、進行性の腎機能障害を招く。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着がさらに組織損傷を悪化させ、腎灌流を障害する。
causes: Primary causes include infection with equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), or other systemic viral infections that secondarily target the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and hemodynamic compromise associated with viremia. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, stress, and concurrent illness.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染により発生し、まれに血行性播種によっても起こる。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こす。主な原因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、連鎖球菌、コリネバクテリウム属などがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至る。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often associated with E. coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, immunosuppression, and catheterization. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites such as endocarditis or abscesses can also seed the kidneys.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma, pelvis, or ureters, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection results in progressive renal tissue destruction, potential formation of fungal granulomas (fungal balls), and impaired renal function. Immunosuppression, prolonged antibiotic use, or indwelling urinary catheters may predispose horses to fungal colonization of the urinary tract.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質、腎盂、または尿管に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。血行性播種または上行性感染により腎組織の進行性破壊、真菌球の形成、および腎機能障害が生じる。免疫抑制状態、長期の抗菌薬使用、または留置カテーテルが真菌の尿路定着を助長する。
causes: Primary causes include infection by opportunistic fungi such as Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly Cryptococcus spp. and Mucor spp. Secondary predisposing factors include prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (e.g., from corticosteroid use or systemic illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary tract obstruction.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly via hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Prolonged infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。長期化すると線維化、腎機能障害、さらには敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infections.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. This leads to impaired filtration, proteinuria, azotemia, and electrolyte imbalances. Prolonged inflammation can result in fibrosis, progressive nephron loss, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の機序により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が障害される疾患である。これにより濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症、電解質異常が生じる。炎症が持続すると線維化、ネフロンの進行性喪失、最終的に腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic sepsis, dehydration, heavy metal exposure, and pigment nephropathy from severe rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis.
causes_ja: 主な原因には細菌感染（レプトスピラ症、連鎖球菌感染など）、ウイルス感染（馬伝染性貧血など）、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎がある。二次的原因としては腎毒性薬剤（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系抗生物質）、全身性敗血症、脱水、重金属中毒、重度の横紋筋融解症や溶血による色素性腎症が挙げられる。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of abnormal cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair kidney function, and potentially metastasize to lungs, liver, and other organs. Tumor growth may cause progressive renal insufficiency, hematuria, and space-occupying effects within the retroperitoneal space.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常細胞の無制御な増殖を伴う。最も多く報告されるのは腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫であり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、腎機能を障害し、肺や肝臓などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の成長は進行性の腎不全、血尿、および後腹膜腔内の占拠性病変を引き起こす。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown. Potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation or irritation of renal tissue, and age-related cellular mutations. Nephroblastoma is more commonly seen in younger horses, suggesting a congenital or embryonal origin, while renal cell carcinoma tends to occur in older animals.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of normal kidney function affecting electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can progress to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary hyperparathyroidism with resultant mineral imbalances and soft tissue calcification.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄に影響を及ぼす腎機能の障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の低下により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の処理が異常となり、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能障害は腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または続発性副甲状腺機能亢進症に進行し、ミネラル不均衡や軟部組織の石灰化を招くことがある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic renal failure, renal tubular acidosis, and congenital or acquired nephropathies. Secondary causes encompass nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants, prolonged dehydration, and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or piroplasmosis that damage renal tubular cells.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratio or excessive oxalate intake from certain plants can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tubules, leading to progressive renal damage and impaired filtration capacity. Vitamin A deficiency may cause squamous metaplasia of renal tubular epithelium, predisposing to obstruction and secondary infection.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏やシュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料の摂取により、腎尿細管機能が障害され、腎石灰化症や腎尿細管変性が生じる。カルシウム-リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管にシュウ酸カルシウム結晶を沈着させ、進行性の腎障害と濾過能力の低下を引き起こす。ビタミンA欠乏は腎尿細管上皮の扁平上皮化生を引き起こし、閉塞や二次感染の素因となる。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of vitamin A, vitamin D, or imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios, as well as excessive ingestion of oxalate-containing plants (e.g., Oxalis, Rumex, Setaria). Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of high-grain/low-forage diets causing phosphorus excess, inadequate water intake, and chronic exposure to nephrotoxic plants that compound nutritional stress on the kidneys.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and inability to maintain fluid and electrolyte homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal embryological development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and inflammation ultimately lead to chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異を伴い、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、および体液・電解質恒常性の維持不能を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などでは、異常な胚発生や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化と炎症が最終的に慢性腎不全につながります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting renal development or function, such as genes involved in nephron differentiation or ciliary function. Secondary factors include environmental stressors, dehydration, nephrotoxic exposure, and concurrent infections that may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、ネフロン分化や繊毛機能に関与する遺伝子の変異（常染色体劣性または優性）による腎発達・機能の障害です。二次的要因として、環境ストレス、脱水、腎毒性物質への曝露、併発感染症などが遺伝性腎疾患の進行を加速させる可能性があります。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial regions. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, loss of functional nephrons, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質領域に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎を生じます。慢性炎症は線維化、機能的ネフロンの喪失、進行性腎不全へと至ります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal tissue antigens, potentially triggered by preceding infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), chronic inflammatory conditions, or drug reactions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune diseases such as equine systemic lupus-like syndrome, or cross-reactivity following exposure to infectious agents that share molecular mimicry with renal epitopes.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephrons, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired renal filtration, concentration ability, and waste excretion. Chronic loss of functional renal tissue results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may be initiated by toxic, ischemic, or immune-mediated injury that triggers irreversible structural changes in the renal parenchyma.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患はネフロンの進行性劣化を伴い、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症が生じ、腎濾過機能、濃縮能力、老廃物排泄の障害を引き起こす。機能的腎組織の慢性的な喪失は高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。毒性、虚血性、または免疫介在性の傷害が腎実質に不可逆的な構造変化を引き起こすことで発症する。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis or hemolysis. Secondary causes include chronic renal ischemia, recurrent pyelonephritis, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Idiopathic chronic renal degeneration is also recognized, particularly in older horses.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney results in parenchymal disruption, hemorrhage, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The injury may range from minor subcapsular hematomas and contusions to severe lacerations, vascular pedicle avulsion, or complete renal fracture. Secondary complications include perirenal abscess formation, uroperitoneum, sepsis, and progressive loss of renal function if the contralateral kidney is also compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性の外傷により腎実質の損傷、出血、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。損傷の程度は軽度の被膜下血腫や挫傷から、重度の裂傷、血管茎の断裂、腎臓の完全破裂まで多岐にわたる。二次的合併症として腎周囲膿瘍、尿腹症、敗血症、および対側腎も障害された場合の進行性腎機能低下がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures. Foals may sustain renal trauma during dystocia or rough handling.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, nephritis, or renal neoplasia. Persistent nociceptive input from the renal capsule or parenchyma can lead to behavioral changes including flank guarding, reluctance to move, postural abnormalities, and altered temperament. The disorder reflects a pain-mediated behavioral response rather than a primary neurological or psychological condition.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓病変による慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感から生じる異常行動を伴います。腎被膜や実質からの持続的な侵害受容刺激が、側腹部の防御反応、運動嫌悪、姿勢異常、気質の変化などの行動変化を引き起こします。この障害は原発性の神経学的・心理学的疾患ではなく、疼痛を介した行動反応を反映しています。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), chronic nephritis, renal abscessation, renal neoplasia, or hydronephrosis causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or perirenal adhesions that produce referred pain to the flank and lumbar regions. Chronic subclinical renal disease that intermittently produces discomfort can also contribute to behavioral changes.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to nephritis or pyelonephritis, resulting in progressive tubular damage, interstitial inflammation, and potential abscess formation. If untreated, chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が惹起され、腎炎や腎盂腎炎を引き起こし、尿細管障害、間質性炎症、膿瘍形成に至る。未治療の場合、慢性感染により線維化が進行し、腎機能障害や最終的には腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder dysfunction, and catheterization-related contamination.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasitic migration causes granulomatous inflammation, vascular damage, thrombosis, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infestation may result in fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and eventual renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の移行により肉芽腫性炎症、血管障害、血栓症、腎組織の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害される。慢性感染では線維化、水腎症が生じ、未治療の場合は最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic renal tropism), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources containing infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to the renal vasculature and glomeruli, leading to impaired renal filtration and tubular dysfunction. Viral replication within endothelial cells of renal vessels triggers inflammation, thrombosis, and ischemic injury to the nephrons, resulting in progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管系および糸球体に血管炎や免疫介在性障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能や尿細管機能の低下をもたらす。腎血管内皮細胞でのウイルス増殖が炎症、血栓形成、ネフロンの虚血性障害を誘発し、進行性の腎機能不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that target renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition in glomeruli, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections exacerbating renal damage.
causes_ja: 主な原因は馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV-1、EHV-4）、馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）など腎組織を標的とする全身性ウイルス感染である。二次的原因として、糸球体への免疫複合体沈着、全身性血管炎、脱水、および腎障害を悪化させる細菌の二次感染がある。

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This leads to impaired renal function, potentially resulting in renal failure if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。両側性または対側腎が障害されている場合、腎機能障害から腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Proteus spp., and Klebsiella spp. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Ascending infection from cystitis is the most frequent route of infection in horses.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, tissue necrosis, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary focus or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract may occur, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質および/または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、閉塞、組織壊死、進行性の腎機能低下を招く可能性があります。免疫抑制状態の馬では、原発巣からの血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行感染が生じることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade renal tissue. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, concurrent systemic illness, and prior renal damage. Secondary bacterial infections may complicate the fungal disease.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染です。長期間の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制、留置尿道カテーテル、併発する全身性疾患、既存の腎障害が素因となります。二次的な細菌感染が真菌性疾患を複雑化させることがあります。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, inciting an inflammatory response that leads to tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If bilateral or left untreated, it can result in renal insufficiency or failure due to loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして尿細管の損傷、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊をもたらします。両側性または未治療の場合、機能的ネフロンの喪失により腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and other gram-negative organisms. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis such as bladder paralysis or recumbency.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、大腸菌、レンサ球菌、Corynebacterium renaleなどのグラム陰性菌を中心とした上行性細菌感染です。素因として尿路結石、尿路閉塞、カテーテル挿入、免疫抑制、膀胱麻痺や長期臥位による尿停滞などが挙げられます。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and secretion. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow and nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. Glomerulonephritis often involves immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis may result from direct toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の損傷により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が障害され、濾過・再吸収・分泌機能が低下する。炎症細胞の浸潤や浮腫により腎血流とネフロン機能が損なわれ、線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着が関与し、尿細管間質性腎炎は直接的な毒性または感染性の障害によることが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated reactions. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic inflammatory conditions, toxin ingestion (e.g., heavy metals, certain plants), and extension of lower urinary tract infections.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma, collecting ducts, or surrounding tissues. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma. Tumor growth leads to progressive destruction of normal renal architecture, potential obstruction of urine flow, and in malignant cases, metastasis to lungs, liver, lymph nodes, and other organs via hematogenous or lymphatic spread.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質、集合管、または周囲組織の細胞が異常かつ無制御に増殖することで発生します。最も多く報告される腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫があります。腫瘍の増大により正常な腎構造が進行的に破壊され、尿路閉塞が生じる可能性があり、悪性の場合は血行性またはリンパ行性に肺、肝臓、リンパ節などへ転移します。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, and no specific genetic, environmental, or infectious causes have been consistently identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma tends to occur more frequently in younger horses. Predisposing factors may include chronic renal inflammation or unknown carcinogenic exposures, but these remain speculative.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormalities in calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic cases may progress to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary renal failure with accumulation of uremic toxins.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎臓の電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄の調節機能が障害される疾患である。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の代謝異常が生じ、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、または代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす。慢性例では腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または尿毒症性毒素の蓄積を伴う二次性腎不全に進行することがある。
causes: Primary causes include excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants (such as tropical grasses), chronic administration of nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), and primary renal tubular defects. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, heavy metal toxicity, vitamin D imbalances, and prolonged electrolyte disturbances from endocrine disorders such as hyperparathyroidism.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake interfere with mineral homeostasis, causing calcium deposition in renal tissue and progressive nephron damage. Chronic deficiency states lead to impaired renal concentrating ability, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取により、腎尿細管機能が障害され、腎石灰化症や尿細管変性が引き起こされます。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取はミネラルの恒常性を妨げ、腎組織へのカルシウム沈着と進行性のネフロン障害を引き起こします。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎濃縮能の低下、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全へと進行します。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus relative to calcium, vitamin A or D deficiency, and ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Oxalis, Halogeton, or tropical grasses high in oxalates). Secondary causes include chronic malnutrition, poor-quality forage, and prolonged feeding of grain-heavy diets without adequate mineral supplementation, leading to nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism and renal mineralization.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and inflammation ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化と炎症が最終的に慢性腎不全をもたらします。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting renal development or function, which may follow autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Certain breeds may have higher predisposition due to limited genetic diversity. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections can accelerate disease progression.
causes_ja: 主な原因は腎臓の発達や機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異であり、疾患の種類によって常染色体劣性または優性遺伝形式をとります。特定の品種では遺伝的多様性の制限により発症リスクが高い場合があります。脱水、腎毒性物質、併発感染症などの二次的要因が疾患の進行を加速させることがあります。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive damage to the glomerular basement membrane and renal parenchyma. The resulting glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis leads to impaired renal filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of kidney function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤が誘発され、糸球体基底膜と腎実質に進行性の損傷が生じます。その結果、糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が発生し、腎濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、進行性の腎機能喪失に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoimmune targeting of renal tissues, potentially triggered by preceding infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), viral infections, or drug exposure. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndromes, or cross-reactivity between microbial antigens and renal self-antigens. Genetic predisposition and chronic antigenic stimulation may also play contributing roles.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular necrosis, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired filtration, concentrating ability, and electrolyte regulation, ultimately resulting in azotemia and chronic renal failure. The progressive loss of functional renal tissue triggers compensatory hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, which further accelerates damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患はネフロンの構造と機能の進行性劣化を伴い、尿細管壊死、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む。これにより濾過能力、濃縮能力、電解質調節が障害され、最終的に高窒素血症および慢性腎不全に至る。機能的腎組織の進行性喪失は残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過を引き起こし、さらに損傷を加速させる。
causes: Primary causes include nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and chronic ischemia. Secondary causes include systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, prolonged dehydration, leptospirosis, and age-related degenerative changes. Idiopathic renal degeneration is also recognized, particularly in older horses.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney causes parenchymal disruption, hemorrhage, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, hematoma formation, and possible uroperitoneum can lead to systemic complications including azotemia, electrolyte imbalances (hyperkalemia, hyponatremia), and secondary infection. In severe cases, vascular pedicle injury may cause life-threatening hemorrhage or renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性の外傷により腎実質の損傷、出血、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。その結果生じる炎症、血腫形成、および尿腹症により、高窒素血症、電解質異常（高カリウム血症、低ナトリウム血症）、二次感染などの全身性合併症を引き起こす可能性がある。重症例では血管茎損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls (especially during jumping or racing), collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Penetrating injuries from sharp objects, impalement, or surgical complications are less common causes. Predisposing factors include pre-existing renal disease (enlarged kidneys), vigorous exercise, and inadequate housing or paddock management.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia. Persistent nociceptive input from the renal capsule or parenchyma leads to behavioral changes including flank guarding, reluctance to move, postural abnormalities, and altered temperament. The chronic pain stimulus may also cause secondary musculoskeletal tension and changes in gait or performance.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓病変による慢性的な腎臓痛や不快感から生じる異常行動を伴います。腎被膜や実質からの持続的な侵害受容入力により、側腹部の防御反応、運動嫌悪、姿勢異常、気性の変化などの行動変化が引き起こされます。慢性疼痛刺激は二次的な筋骨格系の緊張や歩様・パフォーマンスの変化も引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, or renal capsular distension leading to chronic pain and associated behavioral changes. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, chronic dehydration, hypercalcemia, or ascending urinary tract infections that compromise renal function and elicit discomfort-related behaviors.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. This leads to impaired renal function, azotemia, and potentially sepsis if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こす。これにより腎機能障害、高窒素血症が生じ、未治療では敗血症に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections from the lower urinary tract (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp.), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and nephrolithiasis predisposing to secondary infection. Contributing factors include urinary stasis, bladder dysfunction, immunosuppression, and urinary catheterization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasite migration causes direct tissue destruction, granulomatous inflammation, and fibrosis of the kidney, leading to impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also cause thrombosis, ischemia, and secondary bacterial infections.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgaris幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発生する。寄生虫の移行により直接的な組織破壊、肉芽腫性炎症、腎臓の線維化が引き起こされ、腎機能障害に至る。腎血管系を通じた幼虫の移行は血栓症、虚血、二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include infection by parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to immune-complex deposition, vasculitis, interstitial nephritis, and impaired renal function. Viral-induced endothelial injury in renal vasculature results in ischemia, inflammation, and progressive nephron loss. Secondary immune-mediated mechanisms may further exacerbate glomerulonephritis and tubular necrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、免疫複合体の沈着、血管炎、間質性腎炎、腎機能障害をもたらす。腎血管内皮の障害により虚血、炎症、ネフロンの進行性喪失が生じる。二次的な免疫介在性機序が糸球体腎炎や尿細管壊死をさらに悪化させることがある。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses that target renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from systemic viral infections, concurrent bacterial superinfection, dehydration, and nephrotoxic drug administration during viral illness.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, most commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., or Actinobacillus spp., ascend the urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the renal parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscessation, and impaired renal function. The infection triggers neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, and potentially pyelonephritis, leading to progressive nephron destruction and compromised urine concentrating ability. Chronic cases may result in fibrosis, renal scarring, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、アクチノバチルス属などの細菌が尿路上行性感染または血行性に腎実質に到達し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎機能障害を引き起こす。感染により好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、腎盂腎炎が生じ、ネフロンの進行性破壊と尿濃縮能の低下をもたらす。慢性例では線維化、腎瘢痕化が進行し、最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites (e.g., endocarditis, pneumonia, abscesses), and contamination during urinary catheterization. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis causing urinary obstruction and stasis, immunosuppression, anatomical abnormalities, and chronic debilitating conditions that predispose to bacterial colonization of the kidneys.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing tubular necrosis, obstruction of urine flow by fungal masses (fungal balls), and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to unilateral or bilateral renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質および/または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、尿細管壊死、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）による尿路閉塞、および進行性の腎機能低下が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染により片側性または両側性の腎障害が起こりうる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that gain access to the renal system. Secondary contributing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness that compromises immune defenses.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染である。二次的要因として、長期間の抗生物質投与、免疫抑制状態、留置尿道カテーテル、衰弱、および免疫防御を低下させる併発全身疾患が挙げられる。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response, leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If untreated, chronic infection can result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症反応が引き起こされ、好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊が生じます。未治療の場合、慢性感染は線維化、腎不全、さらには敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common but recognized route.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of renal function. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron architecture, resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially acute or chronic renal failure. Immune complex deposition, direct bacterial invasion, or toxin-mediated damage can trigger the inflammatory cascade.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の損傷が糸球体、尿細管、または間質に及ぶことで、濾過機能の障害、蛋白尿、腎機能の進行性低下を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン構造を破壊し、高窒素血症や電解質異常、急性または慢性腎不全に至る可能性がある。免疫複合体の沈着、細菌の直接侵入、または毒素による損傷が炎症カスケードを惹起する。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, and certain plants. Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from systemic diseases, septicemia, endotoxemia, dehydration, and hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass progressively replaces normal renal parenchyma, impairing renal function, and may invade local structures including the renal vein and caudal vena cava. Metastasis can occur via hematogenous or lymphatic routes to the lungs, liver, and other organs, leading to systemic disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍は、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫などが最も一般的であり、腎臓内の細胞が制御不能に増殖する疾患である。腫瘍塊は正常な腎実質を進行性に置換し、腎機能を障害し、腎静脈や後大静脈などの局所構造に浸潤することがある。血行性またはリンパ行性に肺、肝臓、その他の臓器に転移し、全身性疾患を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no well-established predisposing factors identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most frequently reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may affect the kidney as part of multicentric disease. Genetic mutations, chronic inflammation, and exposure to environmental carcinogens have been hypothesized but not confirmed in equines.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of normal kidney function affecting electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis and mineral imbalances. Progressive nephron loss reduces glomerular filtration rate, causing azotemia and accumulation of uremic toxins.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄に影響を与える腎機能の障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の処理が異常となり、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシスおよびミネラル不均衡が生じる。進行性のネフロン喪失により糸球体濾過率が低下し、高窒素血症および尿毒症性毒素の蓄積を引き起こす。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, and hypercalcemia secondary to excessive calcium intake or vitamin D toxicosis. Secondary causes include dehydration, nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), heavy metal exposure, and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or piroplasmosis that affect renal function. Dietary imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratio and oxalate-containing plant ingestion can also contribute.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function, promote nephrocalcinosis, or lead to calcium/phosphorus imbalances that cause renal mineralization and progressive nephron damage. Excessive dietary oxalates (e.g., from certain plants) bind calcium and deposit as calcium oxalate crystals in renal tubules, causing tubular necrosis and interstitial fibrosis. Chronic imbalances in the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio can lead to soft tissue mineralization including renal calcification, resulting in progressive loss of renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料の摂取により、腎尿細管機能の障害、腎石灰化、またはカルシウム・リンの不均衡が生じ、ネフロンの進行性障害を引き起こす。過剰なシュウ酸塩はカルシウムと結合してシュウ酸カルシウム結晶として腎尿細管に沈着し、尿細管壊死や間質線維化を引き起こす。慢性的なカルシウム・リン比の不均衡は腎臓を含む軟部組織の石灰化を引き起こし、腎機能が進行的に低下する。

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and inability to maintain fluid and electrolyte homeostasis. Specific conditions such as renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease result from aberrant renal development or cyst formation that progressively replaces functional renal parenchyma. This leads to chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual end-stage kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、体液・電解質恒常性の維持不全を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などの特定疾患では、腎臓の発生異常や嚢胞形成により機能的な腎実質が徐々に置換されます。これにより慢性腎不全、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には末期腎疾患に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations that affect renal development or function, often transmitted in an autosomal recessive or dominant pattern depending on the specific disorder. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, which have been identified in certain horse breeds. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体の活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じます。慢性炎症により線維化、ネフロンの喪失、進行性腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to production of autoantibodies against glomerular basement membrane or other renal antigens. Secondary causes may include chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), systemic autoimmune conditions, neoplasia, or chronic drug exposure that triggers immune-mediated renal injury through molecular mimicry or immune complex formation.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and concentrating ability. Chronic injury results in nephron loss, azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The disease may be unilateral or bilateral, with bilateral involvement carrying more severe systemic consequences.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・再吸収・濃縮能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害はネフロンの喪失、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全につながる。病変は片側性または両側性であり、両側性の場合はより重篤な全身症状を示す。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemia, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases (e.g., leptospirosis, equine infectious anemia), and prolonged hemodynamic compromise such as dehydration or hypotension.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular disruption may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage or renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管が直接損傷を受け、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。続発する炎症、虚血、二次感染により腎機能が障害される可能性がある。重症例では血管損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects or fractures of adjacent ribs or lumbar vertebrae that lacerate the kidney. Pre-existing renal enlargement due to hydronephrosis or neoplasia may predispose the kidney to traumatic injury.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、運動中や競技中の転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる腹部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として鋭利物による穿通創、隣接する肋骨や腰椎の骨折による腎臓の裂傷がある。水腎症や腫瘍による既存の腎腫大は外傷性損傷の素因となりうる。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction, such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal disease. Pain originating from the kidneys or ureters triggers visceral nociceptive pathways, leading to behavioral manifestations including flank guarding, stretching postures mimicking colic, and frequent posturing to urinate. Chronic renal irritation may also cause referred pain to the back and hindquarters, resulting in reluctance to work, altered gait, or behavioral changes under saddle.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、慢性腎疾患などの基礎的な腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連した異常行動を伴います。腎臓や尿管からの痛みが内臓侵害受容経路を刺激し、側腹部の防御、疝痛様の伸展姿勢、頻繁な排尿姿勢などの行動症状を引き起こします。慢性的な腎刺激は背部や後躯への関連痛を生じ、運動拒否や歩様異常、騎乗時の行動変化をもたらすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, ureteral obstruction, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure causing visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ischemic nephropathy from non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug toxicity, renal cysts, or perirenal abscessation. Behavioral changes may also be exacerbated by concurrent metabolic derangements such as uremia and electrolyte imbalances.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Pathogens such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive nephron destruction. This leads to impaired renal function, potentially resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and if bilateral, renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生する。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの病原体が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、進行性のネフロン破壊を引き起こす。これにより腎機能が障害され、高窒素血症や電解質異常を生じ、両側性の場合は腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from systemic infections. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder dysfunction (e.g., from cauda equina syndrome), and indwelling urinary catheter use that predisposes to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (formerly Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to and colonize the kidneys. The parasites cause direct mechanical damage to renal parenchyma, provoke granulomatous inflammation, and can lead to progressive nephritis, fibrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature may also cause thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎臓に移行・寄生することで発症する。寄生虫は腎実質に直接的な機械的損傷を与え、肉芽腫性炎症を引き起こし、進行性の腎炎、線維化、腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎血管内移行により血栓症、梗塞、二次的な細菌感染も生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic parasitic behavior), larval stages of Strongylus vulgaris through aberrant migration, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or concurrent illness that may predispose horses to opportunistic parasitic infections, as well as environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal vasculature and glomeruli, leading to impaired renal filtration and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and direct viral cytopathic effects result in progressive nephritis, proteinuria, and potential renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV-1）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や糸球体に血管炎および免疫介在性障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能の低下や尿細管壊死をもたらす。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着およびウイルスの直接的な細胞障害作用により、進行性の腎炎、蛋白尿、腎不全が生じる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that target or secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis, systemic vasculitis, and dehydration or hemodynamic compromise during severe viral illness.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, nephron loss, and ultimately renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、腎機能の進行性障害をもたらします。慢性感染は線維化、ネフロンの喪失を引き起こし、両側性の場合は最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Enterobacter spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Ascending infection from cystitis is the most frequent route of infection in horses.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal granulomas or mycetomas. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to renal involvement, often exacerbated by immunosuppression or prolonged antibiotic use.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、真菌性肉芽腫や菌腫の形成が生じます。血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行性感染が原因となり、免疫抑制や長期抗菌薬使用により悪化することがあります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly other environmental fungi. Secondary predisposing factors include prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (from corticosteroid use, systemic illness, or stress), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary tract obstruction.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla and pelvis, causing inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. In severe or chronic cases, fibrosis and impaired renal function may develop, potentially leading to renal failure if bilateral.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を通じて腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質および腎盂に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。重度または慢性の場合、線維化と腎機能障害が進行し、両側性であれば腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents are Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and other gram-negative bacteria ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Hematogenous spread from systemic infections is less common but possible.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. This leads to impaired filtration, tubular dysfunction, proteinuria, and accumulation of metabolic waste products (azotemia). Prolonged inflammation can result in fibrosis, chronic renal failure, and loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じる疾患です。これにより濾過機能の低下、尿細管機能障害、蛋白尿、および代謝老廃物の蓄積（高窒素血症）が起こります。炎症が長期化すると線維化、慢性腎不全、機能的ネフロンの喪失に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), toxin exposure (heavy metals, oxalate-containing plants), systemic sepsis, and hemodynamic insults such as severe dehydration or endotoxemia.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass disrupts normal renal architecture and function, potentially causing obstruction, hemorrhage, and progressive renal insufficiency. Metastasis may occur via hematogenous or lymphatic routes to lungs, liver, and other organs, leading to systemic disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は腎臓内の細胞の無制御な増殖を伴い、最も一般的なものは腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、または腎芽腫である。腫瘍塊は正常な腎構造と機能を破壊し、閉塞、出血、および進行性の腎機能不全を引き起こす可能性がある。血行性またはリンパ行性に肺、肝臓、その他の臓器へ転移し、全身性疾患を引き起こすことがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistently identified risk factors. Possible contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and exposure to environmental carcinogens. Renal cell carcinoma is the most frequently reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may represent systemic neoplastic involvement of the kidney.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Progressive nephron loss leads to inability to concentrate urine and maintain fluid-electrolyte equilibrium, contributing to secondary metabolic derangements including renal secondary hyperparathyroidism.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が障害される病態である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症または高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。進行性のネフロン喪失により尿濃縮能と体液電解質平衡の維持が不能となり、腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症などの二次的代謝異常を招く。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, and glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, prolonged hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, and dietary imbalances such as excessive calcium or oxalate-containing plant ingestion. Age-related degenerative changes and congenital renal anomalies may also predispose horses to renal metabolic dysfunction.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-containing plant ingestion, lead to renal tubular damage, nephrocalcinosis, or impaired renal function in horses. Chronic imbalances disrupt calcium-phosphorus homeostasis, causing mineralization of renal tissues, tubular degeneration, and progressive loss of nephron function. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further exacerbating renal mineral deposition and structural damage.
