Immunosuppression and concurrent bacterial infections may exacerbate renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This leads to impaired renal function, potentially resulting in septicemia, chronic renal failure, or perinephric abscess formation if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。未治療の場合、腎機能障害が進行し、敗血症、慢性腎不全、または腎周囲膿瘍に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, nephrolithiasis, and anatomical abnormalities that promote urinary stasis. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infections.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection may lead to progressive destruction of renal tissue, obstruction of the collecting system by fungal masses (fungal balls), and impaired renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can occur, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質および/または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。感染は腎組織の進行性破壊、真菌塊（ファンガルボール）による集合管系の閉塞、腎機能障害を引き起こす可能性がある。免疫不全状態の馬では血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行性感染が生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Secondary predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, concurrent systemic illness, and corticosteroid administration that disrupts normal microbial flora and immune defenses.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染である。二次的な素因として、長期抗生物質投与、免疫抑制、留置尿道カテーテル、併発する全身疾患、副腎皮質ステロイド投与による正常微生物叢および免疫防御の破綻が挙げられる。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale colonize the renal tissue, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma. Predisposing factors include urinary stasis, urolithiasis, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities that impair normal urine flow.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。大腸菌、プロテウス属、レンサ球菌属、コリネバクテリウム・レナーレなどの細菌が腎組織に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎実質の進行性破壊を引き起こします。尿の停滞、尿路結石、免疫抑制、正常な尿流を妨げる解剖学的異常が素因となります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus spp.) from the lower urinary tract. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and hematogenous spread from distant septic foci.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性があります。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性または感染性の損傷に続いて発生することが多いです。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, and certain plants (e.g., oak, red maple). Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi-associated purpura hemorrhagica), septicemia, endotoxemia, and severe dehydration or hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal proliferation of renal parenchymal or stromal cells, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, or nephroblastoma. Tumor growth leads to progressive destruction of normal renal architecture, compromising kidney function, and may metastasize to lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Local invasion can cause hematuria, hydronephrosis, and compression of adjacent structures, potentially leading to renal failure if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質細胞または間質細胞の異常増殖を伴い、腎細胞癌、扁平上皮癌、腎芽腫が最も多い。腫瘍の増殖により正常な腎構造が進行性に破壊され、腎機能が低下し、肺、肝臓、リンパ節への転移が起こり得る。局所浸潤により血尿、水腎症、隣接構造の圧迫が生じ、両側性または対側腎が障害された場合には腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no definitive genetic, infectious, or environmental causes identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most commonly reported primary renal tumor, while nephroblastoma is more frequently seen in younger horses. Chronic inflammation, toxin exposure, and age-related cellular mutations may play contributing roles, though these remain speculative.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, resulting in electrolyte imbalances, metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Chronic cases may progress to renal tubular acidosis, hypercalcemia, or secondary hyperparathyroidism with soft tissue mineralization.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎臓の電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄の調節機能が障害される疾患である。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、電解質異常、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が起こる。慢性例では腎尿細管性アシドーシス、高カルシウム血症、続発性上皮小体機能亢進症による軟部組織の石灰化に進行することがある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, prolonged high-calcium diets (excessive alfalfa hay), oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and systemic diseases such as sepsis or hemolytic conditions that impose metabolic burden on the kidneys.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can impair normal renal tubular function and structural integrity in horses. Chronic imbalances, especially calcium-phosphorus ratio disturbances (e.g., excess phosphorus from high-grain or oxalate-rich diets), lead to renal calcium deposition, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive tubular degeneration. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may further exacerbate renal mineral handling, resulting in impaired glomerular and tubular function.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡は、馬の腎尿細管機能および構造的完全性を損なう。特にカルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡（高穀物食やシュウ酸塩を多く含む飼料など）は、腎臓へのカルシウム沈着や腎石灰化症、進行性の尿細管変性を引き起こす。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症がさらに腎臓でのミネラル処理を悪化させ、糸球体および尿細管機能の障害をもたらす。
causes: Primary causes include dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (excessive phosphorus or inadequate calcium intake), vitamin A or D deficiency, and feeding of high-oxalate plants (such as tropical grasses) that bind dietary calcium. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of unbalanced grain-heavy diets without adequate forage or mineral supplementation, and chronic secondary hyperparathyroidism (nutritional secondary hyperparathyroidism).

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Specific conditions include renal tubular dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation disrupts normal kidney architecture. Progressive fibrosis and nephron destruction ultimately lead to chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異を伴い、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、および濃縮能の低下を引き起こします。具体的には腎尿細管異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などがあり、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化とネフロン破壊により、最終的に高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症を伴う慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes are inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting genes critical for normal renal development and function. Renal tubular dysplasia has been documented in certain horse breeds, and polycystic kidney disease may occur as a congenital hereditary condition. Consanguinity and selective breeding within closed populations increase the prevalence of these disorders.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components or tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated damage leads to glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, resulting in progressive inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of renal function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue destruction and impair glomerular filtration.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生します。免疫複合体の沈着や直接的な抗体介在性障害により糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が生じ、進行性の炎症、線維化、腎機能低下を引き起こします。補体活性化と炎症細胞浸潤がさらに組織破壊を悪化させ、糸球体濾過を障害します。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (such as Streptococcus equi), viral infections, or drug-induced hypersensitivity. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition associated with equine infectious anemia, chronic inflammatory conditions, or systemic autoimmune diseases. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease susceptibility.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal tubular and/or glomerular structures, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and excretion functions. Chronic injury results in fibrosis, nephron loss, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure. Accumulation of uremic toxins, electrolyte imbalances, and disrupted acid-base homeostasis ensue as functional nephron mass declines below a critical threshold.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、腎尿細管および/または糸球体構造の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・再吸収・排泄機能の障害を引き起こします。慢性的な障害により線維化、ネフロンの喪失が進行し、最終的に腎不全に至ります。機能的ネフロン量が臨界値を下回ると、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積、電解質異常、酸塩基平衡の破綻が生じます。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (such as aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and oxalate-containing plants like Oxalis or pigweed), chronic ischemia, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, prolonged dehydration, and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or equine infectious anemia that chronically affect renal perfusion and parenchyma.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or dorsal abdomen causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature. This results in hemorrhage (subcapsular hematoma or retroperitoneal bleeding), disruption of nephron architecture, and potential urine leakage into surrounding tissues. Secondary inflammation, ischemia, and possible infection can further compromise renal function and lead to systemic complications.
pathophysiology_ja: 側腹部や背側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下血腫や後腹膜出血）、ネフロン構造の破壊、および周囲組織への尿漏出が発生する。二次的な炎症、虚血、感染がさらに腎機能を悪化させ、全身性合併症を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs, or external wounds may also damage the kidney. Secondary causes include iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures or surgical interventions in the flank region.
causes_ja: 主な原因には、他の馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、または交通事故による鈍的外傷が含まれる。鋭利な物体、肋骨骨折、外部創傷による穿通性損傷も腎臓を損傷しうる。二次的原因として、経皮的処置や側腹部領域の外科的介入に伴う医原性損傷がある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that arise secondary to renal pain or discomfort caused by underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia. Chronic renal irritation or inflammation stimulates visceral pain pathways, leading to altered posture and behavioral changes that may mimic colic or musculoskeletal disorders. The behavioral manifestations reflect referred pain from the kidney and associated urinary structures.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓病変による腎臓の痛みや不快感に続発して、頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を見る行動、伸展行動などの異常行動が生じるものです。慢性的な腎臓の刺激や炎症が内臓痛経路を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系疾患に類似した姿勢や行動の変化を引き起こします。行動症状は腎臓および関連する泌尿器構造からの関連痛を反映しています。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), pyelonephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and ectopic ureters causing chronic renal pain. Secondary causes may include urinary tract infections ascending to the kidney, chronic dehydration leading to calculi formation, and renal trauma or perirenal abscessation.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli invade the renal tissue, causing inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, tubular dysfunction, and potentially acute or chronic renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。大腸菌、レンサ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が腎組織に侵入し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、およびネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こす。これにより糸球体濾過の障害、尿細管機能不全が生じ、未治療の場合は急性または慢性腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder catheterization, and pre-existing renal disease that predisposes to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and potentially vascular thrombosis, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through renal tissue disrupts normal filtration and concentrating mechanisms, and may result in hematuria, proteinuria, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発生する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、間質性腎炎、血管血栓症が引き起こされ、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎組織内移行により正常な濾過・濃縮機能が障害され、血尿、蛋白尿、二次的細菌感染を生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating larvae of Strongylus vulgaris through mesenteric and renal arteries, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary factors include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water facilitating infection.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause systemic infection with subsequent viral-mediated damage to renal vasculature and tubular epithelium. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli and direct viral cytopathic effects lead to glomerulonephritis, interstitial nephritis, and impaired renal function. Progressive inflammation may result in tubular necrosis, proteinuria, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが全身感染を引き起こし、腎血管や尿細管上皮にウイルス性障害をもたらす。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着やウイルスの直接的な細胞障害により、糸球体腎炎や間質性腎炎が生じ、腎機能が低下する。進行性の炎症により尿細管壊死、蛋白尿、腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses. Secondary factors include immunosuppression, concurrent bacterial infections, dehydration, and use of nephrotoxic drugs that exacerbate virus-induced renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な原因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、Streptococcus属、Corynebacterium属などがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often associated with urinary stasis, urolithiasis, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, and predisposing factors such as urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, or anatomical abnormalities that impair normal urine flow.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, inciting granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. This leads to progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potentially obstruction of the urinary tract by fungal masses (fungal balls). Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can occur, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質および/または腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害が生じ、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）による尿路閉塞を起こすこともある。免疫低下状態の馬では血行性播種や下部尿路からの上行感染が起こりうる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Secondary predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (e.g., corticosteroid use, systemic illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary stasis.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属などの環境中の日和見真菌による感染である。二次的な素因として、長期の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制（コルチコステロイド使用や全身性疾患）、尿道カテーテルの長期留置、既存の腎障害や尿うっ滞が挙げられる。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、およびネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、腎不全、さらに未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infection.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory infiltrates and edema disrupt normal nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if unresolved. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こします。炎症性浸潤と浮腫がネフロン機能を障害し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性があります。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は中毒性または感染性の侵襲により生じることが多いです。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from chronic infections such as strangles or equine infectious anemia, dehydration, and hemodynamic compromise. Toxin ingestion from plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria can also contribute.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal proliferation of renal parenchymal or stromal cells, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. Tumor growth disrupts normal renal architecture, leading to progressive loss of renal function, potential local invasion of surrounding tissues, and possible distant metastasis to lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Large tumors may cause hematuria, weight loss, and abdominal discomfort due to mass effect and paraneoplastic syndromes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または間質細胞の異常増殖を伴い、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫が最も一般的です。腫瘍の増殖により正常な腎構造が破壊され、腎機能の進行性喪失、周囲組織への局所浸潤、肺・肝臓・リンパ節への遠隔転移が起こり得ます。大きな腫瘍は腫瘤効果や腫瘍随伴症候群により血尿、体重減少、腹部不快感を引き起こすことがあります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic predisposition, chronic renal irritation, and age-related cellular mutations may play a role. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor, while lymphoma can affect the kidneys as part of multicentric disease. Nephroblastoma is occasionally reported in younger horses and is thought to arise from embryonal renal tissue.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Chronic dysfunction may lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary hyperparathyroidism with associated mineral derangements.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎臓の電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄の調節機能が障害される疾患である。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、電解質異常、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または続発性上皮小体機能亢進症とそれに伴うミネラル異常を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include congenital renal tubular defects, chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), and prolonged hypercalcemia or hypercalciuria related to diet. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, hemodynamic compromise, and excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants that burden renal metabolic pathways.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tubules, leading to progressive nephropathy. Chronic deficiency states may result in renal parenchymal damage, impaired glomerular filtration, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取により、腎尿細管機能が障害され、腎石灰化症や腎尿細管変性が馬に生じる。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取はシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の腎尿細管への沈着を引き起こし、進行性の腎症につながる。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎実質の損傷、糸球体濾過率の低下、最終的な腎不全をもたらす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, as well as calcium-phosphorus imbalance (e.g., high phosphorus/low calcium diets). Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of oxalate-rich plants (such as tropical grasses including Setaria, Cenchrus, or Panicum species), which bind dietary calcium and promote renal oxalate deposition. Poor-quality forage, inadequate mineral supplementation, and chronic malnutrition also contribute.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation results in progressive renal insufficiency. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, leading to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、電解質および体液恒常性の破綻を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などがあり、腎臓の発育異常や嚢胞形成により進行性の腎不全に至ります。代償機構が破綻すると、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的に腎不全へと進行します。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations transmitted in autosomal dominant or recessive patterns, depending on the specific disorder. Renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, and renal tubular acidosis have been documented in certain horse breeds. Secondary factors such as dehydration, concurrent infections, or nephrotoxic agents may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes that target renal structures such as the glomerular basement membrane, tubular epithelium, or interstitial tissue. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated cytotoxicity leads to glomerulonephritis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, and progressive renal parenchymal damage. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue injury, resulting in impaired renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜、尿細管上皮、または間質組織などの腎構造を標的とする自己抗体や自己反応性リンパ球を産生する。免疫複合体の沈着や抗体介在性の直接的な細胞傷害により、糸球体腎炎、尿細管間質性腎炎、および進行性の腎実質障害が生じる。補体活性化と炎症細胞浸潤がさらに組織障害を悪化させ、腎機能障害を引き起こす。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, EIA virus), drug reactions, or other systemic autoimmune conditions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from persistent antigenic stimulation and molecular mimicry between microbial and renal antigens. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease susceptibility.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and excretion functions. Chronic nephron loss triggers compensatory hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, which accelerates further damage and ultimately results in chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質性線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・再吸収・排泄機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的なネフロン喪失は残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過を誘発し、さらなる損傷を加速させ、最終的に高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症を伴う慢性腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (such as aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and oxalate-containing plants like Oxalis or Halogeton), chronic pyelonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, prolonged hypotension, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and systemic diseases such as equine infectious anemia or leptospirosis that compromise renal perfusion and structure.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature. This results in hemorrhage (subcapsular, perirenal, or retroperitoneal), possible urine leakage into surrounding tissues, and subsequent inflammation. Severe cases may lead to renal ischemia, nephron loss, and compromised renal function, particularly if both kidneys are affected or if secondary infection develops.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下、腎周囲、または後腹膜）や尿の周囲組織への漏出、その後の炎症が引き起こされる。重度の場合は腎虚血、ネフロンの喪失、腎機能障害を招き、特に両側腎が損傷した場合や二次感染が発生した場合に重篤化する。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or external impacts during transport. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects, iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy, and severe compression injuries. Foals may sustain renal trauma during difficult births (dystocia).
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、輸送中の外部衝撃による鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として鋭利物による穿通性損傷、経皮的腎生検時の医原性損傷、重度の圧迫損傷がある。子馬では難産時に腎外傷を負うことがある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors arising from chronic renal pain or discomfort due to underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia. Pain signals from the renal capsule and urinary tract stimulate visceral afferent nerves, leading to behavioral changes including flank guarding, stretching postures, reluctance to move, and altered urination patterns. Chronic renal insufficiency may also cause uremia-related central nervous system disturbances contributing to dullness, depression, or irritability.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎病変による慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感から生じる異常行動を伴います。腎被膜や尿路からの疼痛信号が内臓求心性神経を刺激し、側腹部の防御姿勢、伸展姿勢、運動嫌悪、排尿パターンの変化などの行動変化を引き起こします。慢性腎不全による尿毒症が中枢神経系に影響し、沈鬱や易刺激性を生じることもあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure causing visceral pain and discomfort. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, bladder pathology referring pain to the renal region, or toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or medications (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides).

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive nephron destruction. If untreated, it can result in renal fibrosis, impaired glomerular filtration, and potentially chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。感染により腎盂腎炎、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成、進行性のネフロン破壊が起こります。未治療の場合、腎線維化、糸球体濾過率の低下、慢性腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis or urinary stasis. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, and anatomical abnormalities that impede normal urine flow.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、大腸菌、レンサ球菌、コリネバクテリウム属、アクチノバチルス・エクーリなどによる下部尿路からの上行性細菌感染であり、尿路結石や尿停滞が関与することが多いです。二次的原因として、遠隔感染巣からの血行性播種、免疫抑制、尿道カテーテル留置、尿流を妨げる解剖学的異常が挙げられます。

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or lodge within the renal parenchyma, causing granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature can lead to thrombosis, infarction, and progressive nephritis. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, abscessation, and eventual renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質に移行・定着し、肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、腎機能障害を引き起こす疾患である。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、梗塞、進行性腎炎を引き起こす可能性がある。慢性感染は線維化、膿瘍形成を招き、両側性の場合は最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include migration of parasitic larvae such as Strongylus vulgaris (verminous arteritis affecting renal arteries), Halicephalobus gingivalis (aberrant nematode migration), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or heavy parasite burden facilitating aberrant larval migration. Contaminated feed, water, or soil exposure and inadequate deworming programs increase the risk of infection.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to immune-complex deposition, vasculitis, interstitial nephritis, and impaired renal function. Viremia results in endothelial damage within renal vasculature, causing ischemia, tubular necrosis, and progressive decline in glomerular filtration rate. Secondary inflammatory responses and fibrin deposition further compromise renal perfusion and function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、免疫複合体の沈着、血管炎、間質性腎炎、腎機能低下をもたらす。ウイルス血症により腎血管内皮が損傷され、虚血、尿細管壊死、糸球体濾過率の進行性低下が生じる。二次的な炎症反応とフィブリン沈着がさらに腎灌流と機能を障害する。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus-1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that target or secondarily affect renal tissues. Secondary causes include immune-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by persistent viral antigenemia, dehydration, and concurrent systemic illness exacerbating renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓における細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、連鎖球菌、コリネバクテリウム属などが一般的な原因菌であり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often associated with urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infections (e.g., endocarditis, abscesses), immunosuppression, anatomical abnormalities, and urinary stasis that predisposes to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. Fungal hyphae may invade renal vasculature causing thrombosis and ischemic necrosis, resulting in progressive loss of renal function. Fungal balls (mycetomas) can form within the renal pelvis, causing obstruction and hydronephrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こす。真菌菌糸が腎血管に侵入して血栓症や虚血性壊死を引き起こし、腎機能の進行性低下をもたらす。真菌塊（真菌腫）が腎盂内に形成され、閉塞や水腎症を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary infection is caused by opportunistic fungi such as Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly Mucor spp., often secondary to immunosuppression, prolonged antibiotic therapy, or indwelling urinary catheterization. Predisposing factors include systemic debilitation, corticosteroid administration, chronic illness, and disruption of normal mucosal barriers. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary pulmonary or gastrointestinal fungal infection may also seed the kidneys.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses occurs when bacteria ascend from the lower urinary tract via the ureters to colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, leading to inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Hematogenous spread from distant infections is also possible. Impaired urine flow due to urolithiasis, ureteral obstruction, or bladder dysfunction predisposes to bacterial colonization and biofilm formation within the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、細菌が下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質に上行性に感染し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こす疾患である。遠隔感染巣からの血行性播種も起こりうる。尿路結石、尿管閉塞、膀胱機能障害による尿流障害が細菌の定着およびバイオフィルム形成の素因となる。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending bacterial migration.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if untreated. Glomerulonephritis often results from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis may arise from ascending infections or toxic insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン機能を障害し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性があります。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着に起因することが多く、尿細管間質性腎炎は上行性感染や毒性物質による障害から生じることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic substances such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, and certain plants. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from chronic infections such as strangles or equine infectious anemia, as well as hemodynamic compromise from severe dehydration or sepsis.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma or associated structures. The most commonly reported primary renal tumors include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. Tumor growth may cause progressive renal insufficiency, hematuria, and space-occupying effects leading to abdominal pain and weight loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または関連構造における細胞の異常かつ制御不能な増殖を伴います。最も一般的に報告される原発性腎腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫が含まれ、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、局所リンパ節や肺などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の増大により進行性の腎不全、血尿、腹痛や体重減少をもたらす占拠性病変が生じます。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic predisposition, chronic irritation, and environmental carcinogens may play a role. Nephroblastoma is more frequently observed in younger horses, suggesting a congenital or developmental origin. Lymphoma involving the kidneys may be secondary to systemic multicentric lymphoma.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of normal kidney function affecting electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and other metabolites, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary hyperparathyroidism with progressive renal parenchymal damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄に影響を及ぼす正常な腎機能の障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、その他の代謝産物の異常な処理が生じ、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、または代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能障害は、腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または続発性副甲状腺機能亢進症を伴う進行性の腎実質損傷につながる。
causes: Primary causes include excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-rich plants (such as tropical grasses containing oxalates), leading to nephrocalcinosis and tubular damage. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, prolonged NSAID administration, heavy metal toxicity, and age-related renal degeneration. Metabolic disorders such as equine metabolic syndrome and pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID) may also predispose horses to renal metabolic derangements.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake causes calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tissue, resulting in progressive tubular damage, interstitial fibrosis, and impaired renal concentrating ability. Chronic deficiency states may also compromise renal blood flow and glomerular filtration, leading to azotemia and renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管機能を障害し、腎石灰化症や尿細管変性を引き起こす。カルシウムとリンの比率の不均衡やシュウ酸の過剰摂取は、腎組織へのシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の沈着を引き起こし、進行性の尿細管障害、間質線維化、腎濃縮能の低下をもたらす。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎血流量や糸球体濾過率を低下させ、高窒素血症や腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (especially inverted Ca:P ratio), excessive oxalate-containing plants (such as Setaria, Cenchrus, or tropical grasses), and vitamin A or D deficiency. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of high-grain/low-forage diets, chronic ingestion of nephrotoxic plants, and inadequate access to balanced mineral supplementation.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and eventual chronic renal failure. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional parenchyma result in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異により、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、最終的には慢性腎不全に至る。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などの疾患では、異常な発達や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊される。進行性の線維化と機能的実質の喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症が生じる。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease are among the recognized hereditary renal conditions in horses. Certain breeds may have higher predisposition due to limited gene pools and selective breeding practices.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components and tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated attack leads to glomerulonephritis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, and progressive renal tissue destruction. This results in impaired glomerular filtration, proteinuria, and eventual chronic kidney disease if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生する。免疫複合体の沈着や抗体介在性の直接的な攻撃により、糸球体腎炎、尿細管間質性腎炎、および進行性の腎組織破壊が生じる。その結果、糸球体濾過機能の障害、蛋白尿が起こり、未治療の場合は慢性腎臓病に進行する。
causes: Primary causes include dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoantibody production against renal antigens, potentially triggered by genetic predisposition. Secondary causes may include chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, systemic autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndrome, and persistent immune complex formation from other inflammatory conditions.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular necrosis, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic degeneration results in the gradual loss of functional nephrons, culminating in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The process may be initiated by toxic, ischemic, or immune-mediated insults that trigger irreversible structural damage to the kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管壊死、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な変性により機能的ネフロンが徐々に失われ、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的に腎不全に至る。毒性、虚血性、または免疫介在性の障害が不可逆的な腎構造損傷を引き起こすことで発症する。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and toxic plants like red maple or oak), ischemic injury from dehydration or hemodynamic compromise, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and prolonged hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia. Vitamin D toxicosis and oxalate-containing plant ingestion can also contribute to renal degeneration.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney results in disruption of renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, damage to the renal pedicle or major vessels can cause life-threatening hemorrhage or renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性の外傷により腎実質、被膜、または血管系が損傷を受け、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じます。それに伴う炎症、虚血、および二次感染の可能性により腎機能が障害されることがあります。重症例では腎茎部や主要血管の損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy. Severe exertion or crushing injuries during transport may also contribute.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他の馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる腹部鈍的外傷です。二次的原因には鋭利な物体による穿通性外傷、肋骨骨折による腎損傷、経皮的腎生検時の医原性損傷が含まれます。輸送中の激しい運動や圧挫損傷も原因となり得ます。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that arise secondary to renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or pyelonephritis can stimulate visceral nociceptors, leading to pain-related behavioral changes. The disorder reflects the horse's response to ongoing renal discomfort rather than a primary neurological or behavioral condition.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛みや機能障害に続発する異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、側腹部を見る、伸展姿勢など）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎などが内臓侵害受容器を刺激し、疼痛関連の行動変化を引き起こします。本疾患は原発性の神経・行動疾患ではなく、持続的な腎臓の不快感に対する馬の反応を反映しています。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal calculi, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic interstitial nephritis causing visceral pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, renal cysts, perirenal abscessation, or toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., red maple, oak). Idiopathic renal pain without identifiable structural lesions has also been reported.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli cause inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in pyelonephritis, interstitial nephritis, perirenal abscessation, and eventual renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能の障害をもたらします。慢性感染は腎盂腎炎、間質性腎炎、腎周囲膿瘍、さらには腎不全に進行する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urinary tract obstruction, bladder dysfunction, and catheterization-associated contamination. Predisposing factors include dehydration, concurrent systemic illness, and nephrolithiasis.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion leads to granulomatous nephritis, tubular destruction, interstitial fibrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries can also cause thrombosis, ischemia, and infarction of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性腎炎、尿細管の破壊、間質の線維化、腎機能障害が引き起こされる。幼虫の腎動脈への移行は血栓形成、虚血、腎組織の梗塞を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale infection. Secondary causes include immunosuppression or concurrent illness that facilitates opportunistic parasitic invasion, as well as environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water containing infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomerular endothelium, leading to acute interstitial nephritis and impaired renal function. Immune-mediated mechanisms including immune complex deposition in glomeruli may contribute to progressive renal injury. Vasculitis induced by viral infection can compromise renal blood flow, exacerbating tubular necrosis and nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体内皮に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、急性間質性腎炎や腎機能障害をもたらす。免疫複合体の糸球体への沈着など免疫介在性機序も腎障害の進行に寄与する。ウイルス感染による血管炎が腎血流を障害し、尿細管壊死やネフロン喪失を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that exhibit renal tropism. Secondary causes include immune complex-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by chronic viral antigenemia, as well as secondary bacterial infections in immunocompromised horses. Pre-existing renal compromise, stress, and concurrent illness may predispose horses to viral renal involvement.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This can lead to impaired renal function, septicemia, and in severe or bilateral cases, renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性伝播によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。重症例や両側性の場合、腎機能障害、敗血症、腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Nephrolithiasis and anatomical abnormalities may also facilitate bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, leading to progressive nephritis, fibrosis, and potential obstruction of the urinary tract. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can facilitate fungal colonization, particularly in immunocompromised horses.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎組織構造が破壊され、進行性の腎炎、線維化、および尿路閉塞を生じる可能性があります。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により、特に免疫低下状態の馬において真菌の定着が促進されます。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade renal tissue. Secondary causes include prolonged antibiotic therapy causing fungal overgrowth, immunosuppression (e.g., from corticosteroid use or concurrent illness such as Cushing's disease), indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitation or chronic stress.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobaculum suis, which damage the tubular epithelium and impair urine concentration ability.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、および進行性の腎機能低下をもたらします。主な原因菌には大腸菌、Corynebacterium renale、Streptococcus属、Actinobaculum suisなどがあり、尿細管上皮を障害し尿濃縮能を低下させます。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections from the lower urinary tract, often secondary to cystitis, urolithiasis, or urethral obstruction that causes urine stasis. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, anatomical abnormalities, pregnancy, and conditions causing incomplete bladder emptying. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is less common but possible.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal failure. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（ネフライティス）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により生じ、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性物質や感染に続発することが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, heavy metals, and toxic plants (e.g., red maple, oak). Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi-associated purpura hemorrhagica), severe dehydration, septicemia, and hemolytic conditions leading to pigment nephropathy.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or surrounding structures. The most commonly reported primary renal tumors include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair kidney function, and potentially metastasize to other organs including the lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Tumor growth may cause progressive renal insufficiency, hematuria, and space-occupying effects leading to abdominal discomfort.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または周囲の構造における異常かつ制御不能な細胞増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される原発性腎腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、腎機能を障害し、肺・肝臓・リンパ節などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の増大により進行性の腎不全、血尿、腹部不快感を伴う占拠性病変が生じる。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and environmental carcinogen exposure may play a role. Nephroblastoma is more commonly seen in younger horses, suggesting a congenital or developmental origin, while renal cell carcinoma tends to occur in older horses. Secondary renal involvement can occur via metastasis from other primary tumors or through multicentric lymphoma.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が障害される疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症または高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性ネフロン喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, and pyelonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants, and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Age-related degenerative changes and congenital renal abnormalities may also contribute.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake damage renal parenchyma by promoting mineral deposition within renal tissue, leading to progressive nephron loss and decreased glomerular filtration rate. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further exacerbating renal calcium handling abnormalities.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管機能を障害し、馬において腎石灰化症や腎尿細管変性を引き起こす。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取は、腎実質内へのミネラル沈着を促進し、進行性のネフロン喪失と糸球体濾過率の低下をもたらす。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発生し、腎臓のカルシウム処理異常をさらに悪化させることがある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus relative to calcium, vitamin A or D deficiency, and chronic ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Oxalis, Halogeton, or tropical grasses high in oxalates). Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of grain-heavy diets without adequate forage, poor-quality hay, and lack of mineral supplementation leading to chronic metabolic derangements affecting renal function.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and compromised electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal embryonic development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and nephron destruction ultimately result in chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能の低下、電解質および水分バランスの障害を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な胎生期発育や嚢胞形成により正常な腎構造が破壊されます。進行性の線維化とネフロン破壊により最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting renal development or function, such as those seen in renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease in certain horse breeds. Secondary contributing factors include consanguineous breeding practices that increase the prevalence of homozygous deleterious alleles. Environmental stressors and concurrent infections may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissues. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Over time, chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、および腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じます。慢性炎症により線維化、ネフロンの喪失、進行性腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant immune responses generating autoantibodies against glomerular basement membrane or other renal antigens, potentially triggered by genetic predisposition. Secondary causes include chronic infections (such as equine infectious anemia or streptococcal infections), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions that result in immune complex formation and subsequent renal deposition.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and concentrating ability. Chronic insult results in nephron loss, azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The remaining nephrons undergo compensatory hypertrophy but ultimately fail as the disease progresses beyond a critical threshold.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過能、再吸収能および濃縮能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害によりネフロンが喪失し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンは代償性肥大を起こすが、疾患が臨界閾値を超えると最終的に機能不全に陥る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemia, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases such as equine infectious anemia, and prolonged hemodynamic compromise. Ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple, oxalate-containing plants) can also contribute to renal degeneration.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar or flank region causes disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle. This leads to hemorrhage (perirenal, subcapsular, or intra-abdominal), potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum), inflammation, and if severe, compromised renal perfusion resulting in ischemic necrosis. Secondary complications include hematuria, retroperitoneal abscessation, adhesion formation, and in bilateral or severe unilateral cases, acute renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部または脇腹への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または血管茎の損傷が生じる。これにより出血（腎周囲、被膜下、または腹腔内）、尿漏出（尿腹症）、炎症が引き起こされ、重度の場合は腎灌流障害による虚血性壊死が生じる。二次的合併症として血尿、後腹膜膿瘍、癒着形成、および両側性または重度片側性の場合には急性腎不全が起こりうる。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collision with fixed objects, or traffic accidents. Penetrating injuries from fence posts, stakes, or other sharp objects can also directly damage the kidney. Iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures is a less common cause.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that arise secondary to renal pain or discomfort caused by underlying kidney pathology such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia. Chronic renal irritation or inflammation stimulates visceral afferent nerves, leading to pain-associated behavioral changes that may be misinterpreted as colic or musculoskeletal issues. The disorder reflects the horse's behavioral response to ongoing renal dysfunction or discomfort rather than a primary behavioral condition.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの基礎的な腎臓疾患に起因する腎臓の痛みや不快感に伴う異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、腹部を見る行動、伸展姿勢など）を含みます。慢性的な腎臓の刺激や炎症が内臓求心性神経を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系の問題と誤認される可能性のある疼痛関連行動変化を引き起こします。本疾患は原発性行動障害ではなく、持続的な腎機能障害や不快感に対する馬の行動反応を反映しています。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), pyelonephritis, renal cysts, renal neoplasia, and chronic interstitial nephritis that produce persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, hydronephrosis, perirenal abscessation, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Predisposing factors include chronic dehydration, high-calcium diets, recurrent urinary tract infections, and age-related renal degeneration.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, impairing glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症します。細菌感染により腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が生じ、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害されます。慢性感染は線維化、腎不全、さらに未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, anatomical abnormalities, and pre-existing bladder dysfunction that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and potentially vascular thrombosis, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Aberrant larval migration from the gastrointestinal tract via the mesenteric vasculature or direct hematogenous spread can result in both unilateral and bilateral kidney damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や腎血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、間質性腎炎、および血管血栓症が引き起こされ、進行性の腎機能障害に至る。消化管からの異所性幼虫移行や血行性播種により片側または両側の腎臓が障害される。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the renal vasculature, infection with Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode that can invade the kidneys), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary factors include immunosuppression, heavy parasitic burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring free-living nematodes.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to immune-complex deposition, vasculitis, interstitial nephritis, and progressive renal dysfunction. Viremia results in endothelial damage within renal vasculature, causing ischemia and secondary tubular necrosis. Inflammatory infiltrates and edema compromise renal filtration and concentrating ability.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害を引き起こし、免疫複合体の沈着、血管炎、間質性腎炎、進行性腎機能障害をもたらす。ウイルス血症により腎血管内皮が障害され、虚血および続発性尿細管壊死が生じる。炎症性浸潤と浮腫が腎濾過機能および濃縮能を低下させる。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other systemic viral infections that target or secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by viral antigen-antibody complex deposition, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that exacerbate renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma (pyelonephritis) typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This leads to impaired renal function, including decreased concentrating ability, azotemia, and potential septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎実質の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常下部尿路からの上行性感染、まれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。これにより濃縮能低下、高窒素血症、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る腎機能障害が生じます。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Proteus spp., and Klebsiella spp., often ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra and proximity to fecal contamination.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to fungal nephritis and pyelonephritis.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、閉塞、膿瘍形成、進行性の腎機能低下を招く可能性がある。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により真菌性腎炎および腎盂腎炎が発生する。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade the kidneys. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness that compromises immune defenses. Secondary bacterial infections may complicate the condition.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境中の真菌による日和見感染である。長期間の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制状態、尿道カテーテルの留置、衰弱、免疫機能を低下させる併発疾患が素因となる。二次的な細菌感染が病態を複雑化させることがある。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If untreated, chronic infection can result in fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症反応が誘発され、好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が生じます。未治療の場合、慢性感染により線維化、腎機能障害、さらには敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urinary catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities that promote urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common but recognized route.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and secretion functions. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. This results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and impaired waste elimination.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過・再吸収・分泌機能が障害される疾患です。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、線維化や慢性腎不全へ進行する可能性があります。その結果、高窒素血症、電解質異常、老廃物排泄障害が生じます。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira spp., Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), toxin exposure (e.g., heavy metals, toxic plants such as oak or red maple), and systemic diseases such as septicemia or endotoxemia.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair glomerular filtration and tubular function, and potentially metastasize to regional lymph nodes, lungs, and other organs. As the tumor expands, it may cause compression of adjacent renal tissue leading to progressive renal insufficiency and hematuria.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常かつ無制御な細胞増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能を障害し、所属リンパ節や肺などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の拡大に伴い、隣接する腎組織が圧迫され、進行性の腎機能不全や血尿を引き起こす。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no clearly identified genetic, infectious, or environmental risk factors consistently documented. Renal cell carcinoma is the most frequently reported primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma tends to occur in younger animals. Chronic inflammation or unknown carcinogenic exposures may play a contributing role, but definitive causative agents have not been established.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to secondary hyperparathyroidism, renal osteodystrophy, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎機能の障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物の排泄が乱れる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、腎性骨異栄養症、進行性のネフロン喪失につながる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease, nephrotoxin exposure (such as aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, or vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, hemodynamic compromise, oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and age-related renal degeneration. Dietary imbalances with excessive calcium or phosphorus intake can also contribute to renal metabolic dysfunction.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can impair normal renal tubular function and structural integrity in horses. Chronic imbalances, especially excessive phosphorus relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), lead to calcium deposition in renal tissues (nephrocalcinosis), tubular degeneration, and progressive loss of renal function. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may also contribute to renal mineralization and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡は、馬の腎尿細管機能および構造的完全性を損なう。特にカルシウムに対するリンの過剰（Ca:P比の逆転）は腎組織へのカルシウム沈着（腎石灰化症）、尿細管変性、進行性の腎機能低下を引き起こす。二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症も腎臓の石灰化および線維化に寄与する。
causes: Primary causes include dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (especially excessive phosphorus from high-grain or bran-heavy diets), vitamin A deficiency, and vitamin D deficiency or excess. Secondary causes include oxalate-rich pastures (e.g., tropical grasses) that bind dietary calcium, leading to chronic calcium deficiency and compensatory renal mineral disturbances.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal kidney development or cyst formation results in progressive renal insufficiency. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, leading to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能および濃縮能の低下を引き起こします。腎形成不全や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の発育異常や嚢胞形成により進行性の腎機能不全が生じます。代償機構が破綻すると、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的に腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting kidney development or function, often transmitted in an autosomal recessive or dominant pattern depending on the specific disorder. Specific examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease observed in certain horse breeds. Secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate disease progression.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
