pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Chronic inflammation leads to fibrosis, loss of functional nephrons, and eventual renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、腎実質の進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎を発症します。慢性炎症は線維化、機能ネフロンの喪失、最終的な腎不全を引き起こします。
causes: Primary causes include idiopathic autoimmune dysregulation targeting renal glomerular or tubular basement membrane antigens. Secondary causes may involve chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, or systemic immune-mediated diseases that result in immune complex deposition in the kidneys. Genetic predisposition and environmental triggers may also contribute to disease onset.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive loss of functional nephrons due to chronic tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, reduced concentrating ability, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, resulting in chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and metabolic derangements.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、慢性的な尿細管変性、間質線維化、および糸球体硬化症による機能的ネフロンの進行性喪失を伴います。これにより糸球体濾過率の低下、濃縮能の低下、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が生じます。やがて代償機構が破綻し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、代謝障害を伴う慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic pyelonephritis, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, hemodynamic compromise from prolonged hypotension, and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. In some cases, the etiology remains idiopathic.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, vasculature, or collecting system. This can result in subcapsular hematoma, parenchymal laceration, renal pedicle injury, or urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. Subsequent hemorrhage, inflammation, and potential uroperitoneum can lead to systemic compromise including hypovolemia, azotemia, and sepsis.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、血管系、または集合系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより被膜下血腫、実質裂傷、腎茎損傷、または後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こりうる。続発する出血、炎症、および尿腹症は循環血液量減少、高窒素血症、敗血症などの全身的な障害を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include external blunt force trauma such as kicks from other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures. Violent athletic activities such as racing or jumping may also predispose to renal trauma.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などの外部からの鈍的外力である。二次的原因として鋭利な物体による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、経皮的処置中の医原性損傷がある。競馬や障害飛越などの激しい運動活動も腎外傷の素因となりうる。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as excessive flank watching, stretching, posturing to urinate, or intermittent colic-like signs) that are associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal neoplasia can stimulate visceral afferent nerves, leading to referred pain and characteristic behavioral changes. The disorder may also involve altered electrolyte balance and uremic toxin accumulation affecting the central nervous system.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連する異常行動（過度の腹部注視、伸展姿勢、排尿姿勢、間欠的な疝痛様症状など）を伴います。慢性腎炎症、腎結石、または腎腫瘍が内臓求心性神経を刺激し、関連痛や特徴的な行動変化を引き起こします。電解質バランスの異常や尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が中枢神経系に影響を与えることもあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal neoplasia (such as renal cell carcinoma), chronic pyelonephritis, and renal cysts causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, chronic interstitial nephritis, renal abscessation, or toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) or medications (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides).

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), tubular damage, interstitial edema, and abscess formation, which can progressively impair glomerular filtration and concentrating ability. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, nephron loss, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。感染により腎盂腎炎、尿細管障害、間質性浮腫および膿瘍形成が生じ、糸球体濾過率や濃縮能が進行性に低下する。慢性感染は線維化やネフロンの喪失を引き起こし、最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary contributing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and pre-existing lower urinary tract disease that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, fibrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries can also lead to thrombosis, infarction, and secondary bacterial infection of the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、大型円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や腎血管系に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫の侵入は肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管の破壊、線維化、腎機能障害を引き起こす。幼虫の腎動脈内移行は血栓症、梗塞、二次的な細菌感染を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae (large strongyles), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor hygiene, and exposure to contaminated soil or water facilitating parasitic entry. Aberrant larval migration from intestinal parasites may also target the kidneys.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubules, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive renal dysfunction. Viral-induced endothelial injury and immune complex deposition in renal vasculature result in ischemia, tubular necrosis, and interstitial nephritis. In severe cases, widespread renal parenchymal damage leads to acute or chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが血管炎や免疫介在性の糸球体・尿細管障害を引き起こし、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。ウイルスによる内皮損傷と免疫複合体の腎血管への沈着が虚血、尿細管壊死、間質性腎炎を引き起こす。重症例では広範な腎実質障害により急性または慢性腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses that target renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that exacerbate viral-induced renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This can lead to impaired renal function, septicemia, and potentially chronic renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。未治療の場合、腎機能障害、敗血症、さらには慢性腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and pre-existing lower urinary tract infections. Nephrolithiasis and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract may also facilitate bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, impairing glomerular filtration and tubular function, and may result in fungal ball (mycetoma) formation causing urinary obstruction. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to progressive renal insufficiency and potential systemic mycosis.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、糸球体濾過や尿細管機能が障害され、真菌球（菌腫）の形成により尿路閉塞を引き起こすことがあります。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染により、進行性の腎不全や全身性真菌症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or less commonly Cryptococcus spp., often secondary to immunosuppression from prolonged antibiotic therapy, corticosteroid use, or debilitating systemic illness. Predisposing factors include indwelling urinary catheters, urinary stasis, diabetes mellitus, and chronic renal disease that compromises local immune defenses. Hematogenous spread from pulmonary or gastrointestinal fungal infections may also seed the kidneys.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal medulla, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites is a less common route. Predisposing factors include urinary stasis, urolithiasis, and immunosuppression.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌が腎髄質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、および腎機能の進行性障害をもたらします。血行性の感染経路はまれですが起こり得ます。尿停滞、尿路結石、免疫抑制が素因となります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, catheterization, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from systemic infections, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities of the urinary tract.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious insult to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of renal function. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema damage the nephron architecture, potentially resulting in fibrosis and chronic kidney disease if unresolved. Immune complex deposition, direct bacterial infection, or toxin-mediated injury can trigger the inflammatory cascade affecting one or both kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン構造を損傷し、未解決の場合は線維化や慢性腎臓病に進行する可能性があります。免疫複合体の沈着、細菌の直接感染、または毒素性障害が炎症カスケードを誘発します。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (e.g., Streptococcus, E. coli), immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals. Secondary causes include systemic infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia, leptospirosis), dehydration, septicemia, and endotoxemia. Ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple) and pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria can also contribute.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of abnormal cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to other organs such as the lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Progressive tumor growth leads to renal insufficiency, compression of adjacent structures, and systemic paraneoplastic effects.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常細胞の無制御な増殖を伴う。最も多く報告される腫瘍は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫であり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、肺、肝臓、リンパ節などへ転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の進行により腎不全、隣接臓器の圧迫、全身性の腫瘍随伴症候群が生じる。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though genetic mutations, chronic inflammation, and possible environmental carcinogen exposure may contribute. Nephroblastoma tends to occur more frequently in younger horses, suggesting a congenital or developmental origin, while renal cell carcinoma is more common in older horses.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive nephron loss with subsequent azotemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄を調節する腎臓の機能障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の低下により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、または代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能障害は腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、進行性のネフロン喪失および高窒素血症につながる。
causes: Primary causes include excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants (such as tropical grasses), chronic vitamin D toxicosis, and inherited or acquired renal tubular defects. Secondary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), prolonged dehydration, septicemia, and conditions causing chronic hypercalcemia such as hyperparathyroidism. Nutritional imbalances with high calcium-to-phosphorus ratios or excessive protein intake can also contribute.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamins (such as vitamin A, D, or E) and minerals (such as calcium, phosphorus, or magnesium), can impair normal renal tubular function, glomerular integrity, and electrolyte homeostasis in horses. Imbalances in the calcium-to-phosphorus ratio or excessive oxalate-containing forages can lead to calcium deposition in renal tissues (nephrocalcinosis), tubular degeneration, and progressive renal dysfunction. Chronic deficiency states may result in secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and eventual renal fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミン（A、D、Eなど）やミネラル（カルシウム、リン、マグネシウムなど）の栄養欠乏は、馬の腎尿細管機能、糸球体の完全性、および電解質恒常性を障害する。カルシウムとリンの比率の不均衡やシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の過剰摂取は、腎組織へのカルシウム沈着（腎石灰化症）、尿細管変性、進行性腎機能障害を引き起こす。慢性的な欠乏状態は二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、最終的には腎線維症に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary imbalances such as excessive phosphorus relative to calcium (inverted Ca:P ratio), feeding of high-oxalate grasses (e.g., tropical pastures such as buffel grass or setaria), and deficiencies in vitamin A or D. Secondary causes include prolonged grazing on nutrient-poor pastures, inadequate mineral supplementation, and chronic ingestion of nephrotoxic plants that exacerbate underlying nutritional imbalances.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and concentrating ability. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation results in progressive destruction of functional renal parenchyma. Over time, compensatory mechanisms fail, leading to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過能力および濃縮能力の低下を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成により機能的な腎実質が進行性に破壊されます。やがて代償機構が破綻し、高窒素血症、電解質異常、慢性腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive or dominant, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia (commonly reported in certain horse breeds) and polycystic kidney disease. Consanguinity or inbreeding within certain bloodlines increases the prevalence of these disorders.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、正常な腎発達および機能に関与する遺伝子の常染色体劣性または優性の遺伝子変異です。腎異形成（特定の馬品種で報告が多い）や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれます。特定の血統内での近親交配が、これらの疾患の発生率を高めます。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components or tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated injury leads to glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, resulting in progressive inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of renal function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue damage and impair glomerular filtration.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎臓抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生します。免疫複合体の沈着や直接的な抗体介在性障害により糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が引き起こされ、進行性の炎症・線維化・腎機能低下をもたらします。補体活性化や炎症細胞浸潤がさらに組織損傷を悪化させ、糸球体濾過機能を障害します。
causes: Primary causes include dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoantibody production against renal self-antigens, possibly triggered by molecular mimicry following infectious diseases (e.g., Streptococcus equi, EIA virus). Secondary causes may include chronic infections, drug reactions, neoplasia, or systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndromes that result in immune complex-mediated renal injury.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to a gradual decline in glomerular filtration rate and impaired renal function. Chronic nephrotoxic insults, ischemia, or immune-mediated damage result in irreversible nephron loss, eventually progressing to chronic renal failure with azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and impaired waste excretion.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、糸球体濾過率の低下と腎機能障害を引き起こす。慢性的な腎毒性障害、虚血、または免疫介在性損傷により不可逆的なネフロン喪失が生じ、最終的に高窒素血症、電解質異常、老廃物排泄障害を伴う慢性腎不全に進行する。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (such as aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and oxalate-containing plants), chronic ischemia, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include systemic diseases such as leptospirosis, equine infectious anemia, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and chronic urinary obstruction or recurrent pyelonephritis.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or renal vasculature, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular pedicle injury may cause life-threatening hemorrhage or complete renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じ、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が起こる。続発する炎症、虚血、および二次感染の可能性により腎機能が障害される。重症例では血管茎損傷により致命的な出血や完全な腎梗塞を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal or lumbar trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating renal tissue, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous procedures such as renal biopsy. Extreme physical exertion or violent struggling during recumbency may also contribute.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、または交通事故による腹部・腰部への鈍的外傷である。二次的原因として、鋭利な物体による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎組織の裂傷、腎生検などの経皮的処置中の医原性損傷がある。過度の運動や横臥時の激しい暴れも原因となりうる。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves chronic renal pain or discomfort arising from kidney pathology (such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal failure) that manifests as abnormal behavioral patterns. The persistent nociceptive input from the renal system leads to altered posture, reluctance to move, flank guarding, and changes in urination behavior. Secondary hormonal and metabolic imbalances from impaired renal function may further contribute to neurological and behavioral changes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、慢性腎不全などの腎臓病変に起因する慢性的な腎臓の疼痛や不快感が異常な行動パターンとして発現するものです。腎臓からの持続的な侵害受容入力により、姿勢の変化、運動拒否、側腹部の防御反応、排尿行動の変化が生じます。腎機能低下に伴うホルモンおよび代謝異常が、神経学的・行動学的変化をさらに悪化させる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal neoplasia, pyelonephritis, chronic interstitial nephritis, and renal cysts causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, hydronephrosis, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and ischemic renal injury leading to chronic discomfort and behavioral manifestations.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to nephritis or pyelonephritis, resulting in tubular damage, interstitial inflammation, and potentially abscess formation. Progressive infection can impair glomerular filtration and tubular function, leading to renal insufficiency or failure if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が誘発され、腎炎や腎盂腎炎を引き起こし、尿細管障害、間質性炎症、さらには膿瘍形成に至ることがあります。感染が進行すると糸球体濾過機能および尿細管機能が障害され、未治療では腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder dysfunction, and catheterization-related contamination that predispose to renal colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, fibrosis, and potentially vascular thrombosis, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through renal tissue disrupts normal filtration and may result in hematuria, proteinuria, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発生する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、線維化、血管血栓症が引き起こされ、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎組織内移行は正常な濾過機能を障害し、血尿、蛋白尿、二次的細菌感染を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with aberrant migration to the kidneys), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae via the mesenteric vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause immune-mediated or direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelium and glomeruli, leading to interstitial nephritis, glomerulonephritis, and impaired renal function. Immune complex deposition in the glomerular basement membrane and vasculitis of renal vessels further compromise filtration and tubular reabsorption, potentially progressing to acute or chronic renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害または免疫介在性の損傷を引き起こし、間質性腎炎や糸球体腎炎、腎機能障害を生じる。免疫複合体の糸球体基底膜への沈着や腎血管の血管炎がさらに濾過機能や尿細管再吸収を障害し、急性または慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally other systemic viral infections that have renal tropism or cause secondary immune-mediated renal injury. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, concurrent illness, stress, and inadequate vaccination history.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な原因菌には大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、コリネバクテリウム・レナーレなどがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often facilitated by urinary stasis, urolithiasis, or anatomical abnormalities. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, catheterization-related contamination, and predisposing factors such as bladder paralysis or recurrent urinary tract infections.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, causing progressive nephritis, obstruction of urine flow, and potentially systemic dissemination. Immunosuppression, prolonged antibiotic use, or indwelling urinary catheters may predispose horses to opportunistic fungal colonization of the urinary tract.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、進行性の腎炎、尿流の閉塞、さらには全身への播種が生じる可能性がある。免疫抑制状態、長期間の抗菌薬使用、または留置カテーテルが日和見性真菌感染の素因となる。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that gain access to the urinary tract. Secondary contributing factors include prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression (from corticosteroid use or systemic illness), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary stasis.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染である。二次的要因として、長期の広域抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制（コルチコステロイド使用や全身性疾患）、留置尿道カテーテル、既存の腎障害や尿うっ滞が挙げられる。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, interstitial edema, and potentially abscess formation. Chronic infection can result in progressive fibrosis, renal scarring, and impaired renal function, potentially leading to renal failure if bilateral.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経て腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症反応が引き起こされ、好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、間質浮腫、さらには膿瘍形成に至ることがあります。慢性感染は進行性の線維化や腎瘢痕化を引き起こし、両側性の場合は腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale, which typically ascend from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urinary catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infections is a less common but possible route of renal infection.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency if untreated. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often follows toxic or infectious insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こします。炎症性細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、未治療の場合は線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性があります。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は毒性物質や感染性の障害に続いて発生することが多いです。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, and heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition from chronic infections or systemic diseases, dehydration, hemolytic episodes, and ascending urinary tract infections. Plant toxins (e.g., oak, red maple) and myoglobinuria from severe rhabdomyolysis can also contribute.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis, leading to progressive destruction of normal renal tissue, impaired kidney function, and potential metastasis to distant organs. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma. Tumor expansion may cause compression of adjacent structures, hematuria, and eventually renal failure if bilateral or if the contralateral kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂内の細胞が異常増殖し、正常な腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、および遠隔臓器への転移を引き起こす。最も多く報告される腫瘍型は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫である。腫瘍の拡大により隣接構造の圧迫、血尿が生じ、両側性または対側腎が障害された場合には腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, and no specific genetic, environmental, or infectious causes have been definitively identified. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary renal tumor in adult horses, while nephroblastoma tends to occur more frequently in younger horses. Lymphoma may involve the kidneys as part of a multicentric neoplastic process.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Chronic cases may progress to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary hyperparathyroidism with associated soft tissue mineralization.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎臓の電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄の調節機能の障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の低下により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸の異常な処理が生じ、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、電解質異常、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積を引き起こす。慢性例では腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症に進行し、軟部組織の石灰化を伴うことがある。
causes: Primary causes include congenital or acquired renal tubular defects, chronic kidney disease, and toxic nephropathy from ingestion of nephrotoxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple), aminoglycosides, or NSAIDs. Secondary causes include severe dehydration, prolonged electrolyte imbalances, hypercalcemia from excessive calcium intake or vitamin D toxicosis, and systemic diseases such as sepsis or hemolytic conditions that impose excessive metabolic burden on the kidneys.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratio (especially excess phosphorus relative to calcium) promote dystrophic mineralization of renal tissues, disrupting normal filtration and concentrating ability. Prolonged deficiency states can result in progressive renal parenchymal damage and secondary renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡は、馬の腎尿細管機能を障害し、腎石灰沈着症や腎尿細管変性を引き起こします。特にカルシウムとリンの比率の慢性的な不均衡（リン過剰）は腎組織の異栄養性石灰化を促進し、正常な濾過・濃縮機能を障害します。長期的な欠乏状態は進行性の腎実質障害と二次的な腎不全につながる可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or excessive phosphorus intake leading to inverted calcium-phosphorus ratio, often seen with high-grain, low-forage diets or oxalate-rich pastures (e.g., tropical grasses). Secondary causes include poor-quality feed, inadequate mineral supplementation, and chronic grazing on pastures with high oxalate content that binds dietary calcium, creating functional calcium deficiency.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, and renal tubular acidosis, where abnormal kidney development or cystic degeneration results in chronic renal insufficiency. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional renal parenchyma ultimately leads to end-stage renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能の障害、代謝老廃物の蓄積を引き起こします。具体的には腎異形成、多発性嚢胞腎、尿細管性アシドーシスなどがあり、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞性変性が慢性腎不全に至ります。進行性の線維化と機能的腎実質の喪失により、最終的に末期腎不全に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive or dominant, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Specific examples include renal dysplasia reported in certain horse breeds and polycystic kidney disease. Inbreeding and limited genetic diversity within certain bloodlines increase the prevalence of these disorders.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive destruction of nephrons, resulting in glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Chronic immune-mediated inflammation leads to fibrosis, loss of functional renal tissue, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着する。これにより補体の活性化、炎症細胞の浸潤、ネフロンの進行性破壊が引き起こされ、糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎を生じる。慢性的な免疫介在性炎症は線維化と機能的腎組織の喪失を招き、最終的に腎不全に至る。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia, streptococcal infections), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from persistent antigenic stimulation, equine purpura hemorrhagica, and systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndromes. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to susceptibility.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Progressive degeneration of renal tubular epithelium and glomerular structures leads to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and concentration of urine. Chronic nephron loss triggers compensatory hypertrophy of remaining nephrons, eventually resulting in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Fibrosis and mineralization of renal tissue further compromise kidney function over time.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎尿細管上皮および糸球体構造の進行性変性により、濾過・再吸収・尿濃縮機能が障害される。慢性的なネフロン喪失により残存ネフロンの代償性肥大が起こり、最終的に高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積をもたらす。腎組織の線維化および石灰化がさらに腎機能を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemia, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases such as equine infectious anemia, and prolonged hemodynamic compromise leading to progressive renal injury.
causes_ja: 主な原因として、慢性的な腎毒性物質への曝露（アミノグリコシド系薬剤、NSAIDs、重金属、ビタミンD中毒）、慢性虚血、加齢性変性変化が挙げられる。二次的原因には慢性腎盂腎炎、腎結石症、馬伝染性貧血などの全身性疾患、および長期的な血行動態障害による進行性腎障害がある。

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney causes parenchymal disruption, hemorrhage, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting hematoma, inflammation, and possible uroperitoneum can lead to systemic complications including azotemia, electrolyte imbalances (hyperkalemia, hyponatremia), and secondary infection. In severe cases, vascular pedicle injury may cause life-threatening hemorrhage or renal ischemia and infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性外傷により腎実質の損傷、出血、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。血腫、炎症、尿腹症により高窒素血症、電解質異常（高カリウム血症、低ナトリウム血症）、二次感染などの全身性合併症を引き起こす可能性がある。重症例では腎血管茎の損傷により致命的な出血や腎虚血・梗塞を生じることがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Penetrating injuries from fence posts, stakes, or other sharp objects can also damage the kidney. Secondary causes include iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures in the retroperitoneal area.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他の馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、交通事故などによる腹部鈍的外傷である。柵の支柱や杭などの鋭利な物体による穿通性外傷も腎臓を損傷し得る。二次的原因として経皮的腎生検や後腹膜領域の外科手術中の医原性損傷がある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as stretching, posturing to urinate frequently, or flank watching) associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal insufficiency can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to behavioral changes that mimic colic or musculoskeletal pain. Uremia or electrolyte imbalances secondary to renal compromise may also contribute to altered mentation and behavioral abnormalities.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、体を伸ばす動作、脇腹を気にする行動など）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石症、または腎機能不全が内臓痛経路を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系疼痛に類似した行動変化を引き起こします。腎障害に続発する尿毒症や電解質異常も精神状態の変化や行動異常に寄与する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic renal failure, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and renal cysts causing visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, bladder dysfunction, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and chronic dehydration leading to renal compromise.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial colonization leads to inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive nephritis, which can impair glomerular filtration and tubular function. If untreated, infection may progress to pyelonephritis, perinephric abscess, or septicemia with subsequent renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症、膿瘍形成、進行性の腎炎が生じ、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が障害されます。未治療の場合、腎盂腎炎、腎周囲膿瘍、または敗血症に進行し、腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, originating from the lower urinary tract. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, immunosuppression, and catheterization-associated infections. Predisposing factors include chronic bladder dysfunction, nephrolithiasis, and concurrent systemic illness.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasitic organisms (such as Halicephalobus gingivalis, Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale) within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasite migration causes direct mechanical damage, inflammatory granuloma formation, vascular thrombosis, and progressive destruction of nephrons, leading to impaired renal function. Chronic infection can result in interstitial nephritis, fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and potentially renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、寄生虫（Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫の幼虫、腎虫など）が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の移行により機械的損傷、肉芽腫形成、血管血栓症、およびネフロンの進行性破壊が起こり、腎機能障害を引き起こす。慢性感染では間質性腎炎、線維化、水腎症、さらには腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with aberrant migration to kidneys), larval migration of Strongylus vulgaris through renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming programs, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to interstitial nephritis, vasculitis, and immune-complex deposition. The resulting inflammation impairs glomerular filtration and tubular reabsorption, potentially progressing to acute or chronic renal insufficiency. Viral-induced endothelial damage in renal vasculature may also contribute to ischemic injury and further nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞変性障害を引き起こし、間質性腎炎、血管炎、免疫複合体の沈着をもたらす。これにより糸球体濾過および尿細管再吸収が障害され、急性または慢性の腎不全に進行する可能性がある。腎血管内皮の損傷により虚血性障害やネフロンの喪失がさらに促進される。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that target or secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune-complex mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by chronic viral infections and viral-induced vasculitis leading to renal ischemia. Concurrent dehydration, NSAID use, or bacterial co-infections may exacerbate renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、および腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な起因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、Streptococcus属、Corynebacterium属などがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), particularly in mares due to their shorter urethra, and hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and nephrolithiasis that damages mucosal barriers and facilitates bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, leading to progressive nephritis, possible obstruction of urine flow by fungal masses (fungal balls), and impaired renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending urinary tract infection may facilitate fungal colonization, particularly in immunocompromised or debilitated horses.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、真菌塊（ファンガスボール）による尿路閉塞や腎機能障害を生じる。血行性播種または上行性尿路感染により、特に免疫不全や衰弱した馬において真菌の定着が促進される。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal pathogens such as Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., and occasionally other environmental fungi. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness that compromise the horse's immune defenses.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属などの日和見真菌病原体である。長期の抗生物質投与、免疫抑制状態、留置尿道カテーテルの使用、衰弱、および全身性疾患による免疫防御の低下が素因となる。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization leads to inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If left untreated, it can result in septicemia, chronic renal failure, or perinephric abscess formation.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が引き起こされます。未治療の場合、敗血症、慢性腎不全、または腎周囲膿瘍に進行する可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, prolonged catheterization, and immunosuppression. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites and anatomical abnormalities of the urinary tract.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and secretion functions. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise renal blood flow and tubular integrity, resulting in azotemia, proteinuria, and electrolyte imbalances. Chronic inflammation may progress to fibrosis and irreversible loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の機序により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が障害され、濾過・再吸収・分泌機能が低下する疾患である。炎症細胞の浸潤や浮腫が腎血流と尿細管の健全性を損ない、高窒素血症、蛋白尿、電解質異常を引き起こす。慢性炎症は線維化に進行し、機能的ネフロンの不可逆的な喪失をもたらす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), heavy metals, systemic diseases such as equine purpura hemorrhagica, and ascending urinary tract infections.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis, leading to progressive destruction of normal renal tissue. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma. As the tumor enlarges, it can obstruct urine flow, invade surrounding structures, compromise renal function, and potentially metastasize to the lungs, liver, and other organs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂内の細胞が制御不能に増殖し、正常な腎組織が進行性に破壊される疾患である。最も多く報告される腫瘍型は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫である。腫瘍の増大に伴い、尿路閉塞、周囲組織への浸潤、腎機能の低下が起こり、肺や肝臓など他臓器への転移の可能性がある。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses remains largely unknown. Potential contributing factors may include genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation or irritation of renal tissue, and age-related cellular mutations. No specific environmental or infectious agents have been definitively linked to equine renal tumors.
causes_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍の正確な原因は大部分が不明である。遺伝的素因、腎組織の慢性炎症や刺激、加齢に伴う細胞変異などが関与する可能性がある。馬の腎腫瘍に明確に関連する特定の環境因子や感染性病原体は確認されていない。

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of the kidney's ability to regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. This can lead to accumulation of uremic toxins, imbalances in calcium, phosphorus, and potassium metabolism, and impaired vitamin D activation. Progressive nephron loss results in compensatory hyperfiltration of remaining nephrons, eventually leading to chronic renal failure and secondary metabolic derangements including metabolic acidosis and renal secondary hyperparathyroidism.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎臓の電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄の調節能力の障害を伴う。これにより尿毒症性毒素の蓄積、カルシウム・リン・カリウム代謝の不均衡、およびビタミンD活性化の障害が生じる。進行性のネフロン喪失により残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過が起こり、最終的に慢性腎不全および代謝性アシドーシスや腎性二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症などの二次的代謝異常に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), nephrolithiasis, and chronic pyelonephritis. Secondary causes include dehydration, hypercalcemia, oxalate nephropathy from ingestion of oxalate-containing plants (e.g., Oxalis spp., Rumex spp.), and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or equine infectious anemia that secondarily affect renal function.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or renal tubular degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake from certain plants can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tubules, leading to progressive renal damage and impaired filtration capacity. Vitamin A deficiency may result in squamous metaplasia of renal tubular epithelium, further compromising renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏やシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の摂取は、馬の腎尿細管機能を障害し、腎石灰化症や腎尿細管変性を引き起こす。カルシウム・リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸の過剰摂取は、腎尿細管にシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の沈着を引き起こし、進行性の腎障害と濾過能力の低下をもたらす。ビタミンA欠乏は腎尿細管上皮の扁平上皮化生を引き起こし、腎機能をさらに損なう可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, as well as calcium-phosphorus imbalance (especially excessive phosphorus relative to calcium). Secondary causes include chronic ingestion of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Setaria, Cenchrus, Oxalis species), which bind calcium and deposit oxalate crystals in the kidneys, and prolonged feeding of grain-heavy diets without adequate mineral supplementation.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Conditions such as renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease result from abnormal kidney development or cyst formation, causing progressive renal parenchymal destruction and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異により、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、電解質・水分バランスの乱れを引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などの疾患は、腎臓の発育異常や嚢胞形成により腎実質が進行性に破壊され、最終的に腎不全に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting kidney development or function, such as renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease. Certain breed predispositions have been identified, and secondary factors such as dehydration, nephrotoxic agents, or concurrent infections may accelerate disease progression.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、腎臓の発育や機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異（常染色体劣性または優性遺伝）であり、腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎が含まれます。特定の品種に素因が認められ、脱水、腎毒性物質、併発感染症などの二次的要因が病態の進行を加速させる可能性があります。

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or immune complexes directed against renal glomerular or tubular antigens, leading to complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis. Immune complex deposition in the glomerular basement membrane causes thickening, proteinuria, and progressive loss of nephron function. Chronic inflammation ultimately results in fibrosis, reduced glomerular filtration rate, and renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎糸球体または尿細管抗原に対する自己抗体や免疫複合体を産生し、補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、進行性の糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎を引き起こす。糸球体基底膜への免疫複合体沈着により基底膜の肥厚、蛋白尿、ネフロン機能の進行性喪失が生じる。慢性炎症は最終的に線維化、糸球体濾過率の低下、腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include idiopathic autoimmune dysregulation targeting renal antigens, potentially triggered by molecular mimicry following systemic infections such as Streptococcus equi or equine infectious anemia virus. Secondary causes may include chronic immune-mediated conditions (e.g., systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndromes), drug reactions, neoplasia-associated paraneoplastic immune responses, or persistent antigenic stimulation from chronic infections leading to immune complex formation and renal deposition.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to a gradual decline in glomerular filtration rate, impaired concentrating ability, and accumulation of metabolic waste products (azotemia). Chronic loss of functional renal tissue eventually results in end-stage renal failure with electrolyte imbalances, metabolic acidosis, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性悪化を伴う。これにより糸球体濾過率の低下、濃縮能の障害、代謝老廃物の蓄積（高窒素血症）が生じる。機能的腎組織の慢性的喪失は最終的に電解質異常、代謝性アシドーシス、尿毒症を伴う末期腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic ischemic injury, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases (e.g., equine infectious anemia, leptospirosis), and prolonged hemodynamic compromise from dehydration or endotoxemia. Idiopathic chronic interstitial nephritis is also a recognized cause in horses.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or dorsal abdomen causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or renal vasculature. This results in hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), parenchymal contusion or laceration, and potential disruption of the collecting system leading to uroperitoneum. Secondary inflammation, ischemia, and possible infection may further compromise renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 側腹部または背側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下または腎周囲血腫）、実質挫傷や裂傷が起こり、集合系の破綻により尿腹症を引き起こす可能性がある。二次的な炎症、虚血、および感染がさらに腎機能を悪化させることがある。
causes: Primary causes include kicks from other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collisions with fixed objects, and penetrating wounds (e.g., fence posts, sharp objects). Secondary causes include iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or abdominal surgery, and rarely, fractured ribs or lumbar transverse processes damaging the kidney.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、運動中や競技中の転倒、固定物への衝突、および穿通性外傷（柵の支柱や鋭利な物体など）である。二次的原因として、経皮的腎生検や腹部手術中の医原性損傷、まれに肋骨や腰椎横突起の骨折による腎臓への損傷がある。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that are associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or subclinical renal disease can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to stereotypic or pain-related behavioral changes. The altered nociceptive signaling from the kidneys may manifest as behavioral abnormalities even when overt clinical signs of renal failure are not yet apparent.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛みや機能障害に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を見る行動、伸びをする動作など）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石、または無症候性の腎疾患が内臓痛経路を刺激し、常同行動や疼痛関連の行動変化を引き起こします。腎臓からの侵害受容シグナルの変化により、明らかな腎不全の臨床徴候が現れる前に行動異常として発現することがあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic interstitial nephritis, renal neoplasia, and pyelonephritis leading to visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal cysts, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or nephrotoxic plants), or referred pain from other urogenital structures.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to pyelonephritis, abscess formation, or interstitial nephritis, which can progressively impair glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が誘発され、腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成、間質性腎炎を引き起こし、糸球体濾過および尿細管機能が進行的に障害される。慢性感染は線維化、腎不全、さらに未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, or hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tissue necrosis, and progressive destruction of renal architecture, leading to impaired kidney function. Larval migration through renal vessels may also cause thrombosis, ischemia, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、組織壊死、腎構造の進行性破壊が生じ、腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の腎血管内移行は血栓症、虚血、二次的細菌感染を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic invasive potential), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae, and rarely Dioctophyme renale. Secondary factors include immunosuppression, poor sanitation, and exposure to contaminated soil or water that harbors infective larvae or eggs.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubules, leading to impaired renal filtration and function. Viral replication within renal endothelial and epithelial cells triggers inflammatory infiltration and necrosis, resulting in acute or chronic renal insufficiency. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli may further exacerbate glomerulonephritis and progressive renal damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎臓の糸球体や尿細管に血管炎および免疫介在性障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能の低下をもたらす。ウイルスが腎内皮細胞や上皮細胞で増殖し、炎症性浸潤と壊死を誘発して急性または慢性の腎機能不全を引き起こす。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着が糸球体腎炎をさらに悪化させる可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include viral infections such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that target or secondarily affect renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, and hemodynamic compromise resulting from viral-induced sepsis or multi-organ dysfunction. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, stress, and concurrent infections.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, commonly Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., or Corynebacterium spp., ascend via the urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the renal parenchyma. This leads to inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue (pyelonephritis), impairing glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、アクチノバチルス属、連鎖球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属などの細菌が尿路上行性感染または血行性に腎実質に到達し、炎症・膿瘍形成・組織破壊（腎盂腎炎）を引き起こします。これにより糸球体濾過や尿細管機能が障害されます。慢性感染では線維化、腎不全、さらには敗血症に進行する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections (most common), often secondary to urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, or catheterization, with common pathogens being E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, urinary stasis, and anatomical abnormalities that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, causing progressive nephritis, tubular damage, and potentially obstructive fungal masses (fungal balls) within the renal pelvis or ureters. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to impaired renal function and systemic illness.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こす。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、進行性の腎炎、尿細管障害、さらに腎盂や尿管内に真菌塊（ファンガルボール）が形成され閉塞を生じることがある。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により腎機能障害および全身性疾患に至る。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that gain access to the kidneys via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Secondary contributing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and debilitating concurrent diseases that compromise host immune defenses.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, though hematogenous spread is also possible. Bacterial colonization of the renal pelvis and parenchyma triggers an inflammatory response, leading to tissue damage, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Chronic infection can result in fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and eventual renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染によって発生しますが、血行性の播種も起こり得ます。腎盂および腎実質への細菌定着が炎症反応を引き起こし、組織損傷、膿瘍形成、および腎機能の進行性障害をもたらします。慢性感染は線維化、水腎症、そして未治療の場合は最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, typically ascending from lower urinary tract infections. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, immunosuppression, catheterization, and anatomical abnormalities that impair normal urine flow. Nephroliths and chronic cystitis are significant risk factors for the development of ascending renal infection.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of renal function. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema compromise the renal parenchyma, resulting in reduced glomerular filtration rate, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of metabolic waste products. Chronic inflammation may lead to fibrosis and irreversible structural damage to the nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、進行性の腎機能喪失を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が腎実質を障害し、糸球体濾過率の低下、電解質異常、代謝老廃物の蓄積をもたらす。慢性炎症は線維化を引き起こし、ネフロンの不可逆的な構造的損傷に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (such as leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic diseases, septicemia, dehydration, and exposure to toxic plants or heavy metals. Ascending urinary tract infections and embolic showering from endocarditis can also lead to renal inflammation.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass progressively replaces normal renal parenchyma, impairing kidney function and potentially metastasizing to lungs, liver, and other organs via hematogenous or lymphatic routes. Local invasion can cause obstruction of the ureter or renal vasculature, leading to hydronephrosis, hematuria, and secondary renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎臓内の細胞が異常かつ無制御に増殖するもので、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫が最も一般的です。腫瘍塊は正常な腎実質を徐々に置換し、腎機能を障害するとともに、血行性またはリンパ行性に肺や肝臓などへ転移する可能性があります。局所浸潤により尿管や腎血管の閉塞が生じ、水腎症、血尿、続発性腎不全を引き起こすことがあります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, with no consistently identified predisposing factors. Renal cell carcinoma is the most commonly reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma can involve the kidney as part of multicentric disease. Genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and environmental carcinogen exposure have been speculated but not definitively proven in equines.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves dysfunction of the kidneys' ability to properly regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired tubular reabsorption and secretion lead to electrolyte imbalances (calcium, phosphorus, potassium), metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Chronic cases may progress to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, osteodystrophy (rubber jaw), and soft tissue mineralization.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎臓の電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄の調節機能障害を伴う。尿細管の再吸収・分泌障害により、電解質異常（カルシウム、リン、カリウム）、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が生じる。慢性例では腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、骨異栄養症（ラバージョー）、軟部組織の石灰化に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease (CKD), acute kidney injury from nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), and renal tubular acidosis. Secondary causes include dehydration, urolithiasis, pyelonephritis, oxalate-containing plant ingestion, and prolonged hemodynamic compromise leading to renal ischemia.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can lead to renal dysfunction in horses through nephrocalcinosis, tubular degeneration, or impaired renal cellular metabolism. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios (especially excess phosphorus from high-grain or oxalate-rich diets) can cause calcium deposition in renal tissues, leading to progressive nephropathy. Vitamin A deficiency may result in metaplastic changes in renal tubular epithelium, impairing normal renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏は、腎石灰沈着症、尿細管変性、または腎細胞代謝の障害を通じて馬の腎機能障害を引き起こす。カルシウムとリンの比率の慢性的な不均衡（特に高穀物飼料やシュウ酸塩の多い飼料による過剰リン）は、腎組織へのカルシウム沈着を引き起こし、進行性腎症をもたらす。ビタミンA欠乏は腎尿細管上皮の化生変化を引き起こし、正常な腎機能を損なう可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of vitamin A, vitamin D, or imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios, often from feeding high-oxalate tropical grasses or excessive grain without adequate calcium supplementation. Secondary causes include chronic ingestion of nephrotoxic plants, prolonged poor-quality forage, and inadequate access to balanced mineral supplements. Concurrent dehydration or other metabolic stressors may exacerbate nutritional renal damage.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and water homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation progressively replaces functional parenchyma, ultimately resulting in chronic renal failure. The accumulation of uremic toxins and metabolic derangements leads to systemic clinical signs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を及ぼす遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過機能障害、電解質および水分恒常性の破綻を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、異常な腎発生や嚢胞形成により機能的実質が徐々に置換され、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。尿毒症性毒素の蓄積と代謝異常により全身性の臨床症状が発現します。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, which may follow autosomal recessive, autosomal dominant, or other inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Specific examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease caused by defects in genes regulating renal organogenesis or tubular cell proliferation. Secondary factors such as concurrent infections, dehydration, or nephrotoxic exposure may accelerate disease progression.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissue. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive damage to the glomerular basement membrane and renal parenchyma. The resulting glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis leads to impaired renal filtration, proteinuria, and progressive loss of kidney function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の自己抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生し、糸球体および/または尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着する。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤が誘発され、糸球体基底膜および腎実質の進行性障害が生じる。結果として糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が発症し、腎濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、進行性の腎機能喪失に至る。
causes: Primary causes include idiopathic autoimmune dysregulation targeting renal antigens, potentially triggered by molecular mimicry following infectious diseases such as Streptococcus equi or equine infectious anemia virus. Secondary causes may include chronic infections, drug reactions, systemic autoimmune conditions, and neoplasia that provoke immune complex formation and subsequent renal deposition.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, loss of concentrating ability, and accumulation of uremic toxins. Over time, compensatory mechanisms in remaining nephrons fail, resulting in chronic renal failure and azotemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性悪化を伴う。これにより糸球体濾過能の低下、濃縮能の喪失、尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が生じる。最終的に残存ネフロンの代償機構が破綻し、慢性腎不全と高窒素血症に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), chronic hypoperfusion, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, systemic diseases such as immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and ingestion of toxic plants (e.g., oak, red maple, oxalate-containing plants). Idiopathic renal degeneration is also recognized in older horses.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney causes disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature, leading to hemorrhage, hematoma formation, and potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space. The resulting inflammation, ischemia, and possible secondary infection can compromise renal function. In severe cases, vascular pedicle injury may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage or renal infarction.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性の外傷により腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管が損傷し、出血、血腫形成、および後腹膜腔への尿漏出が生じる。それに伴う炎症、虚血、および二次感染の可能性により腎機能が障害される。重症例では腎血管茎の損傷により致命的な出血や腎梗塞を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy. Extreme exertion or crushing injuries during transport may also contribute.
causes_ja: 主な原因は他馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、または車両事故による鈍的腹部外傷である。二次的原因には鋭利物による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、または経皮的腎生検時の医原性損傷が含まれる。輸送中の過度の負荷や圧挫損傷も原因となりうる。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that are associated with underlying renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal cysts can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to characteristic behavioral changes. The discomfort originating from the kidneys or ureters manifests as alterations in posture, gait, and temperament rather than overt clinical signs of renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を気にする行動、体を伸ばす動作など）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石、または腎嚢胞が内臓痛経路を刺激し、特徴的な行動変化を引き起こします。腎臓や尿管からの不快感が、明らかな腎不全の臨床徴候ではなく、姿勢・歩様・気質の変化として現れます。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, pyelonephritis, and chronic interstitial nephritis that produce visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, renal neoplasia, renal trauma, or referred pain from adjacent structures. Predisposing factors include chronic dehydration, high-calcium diets, and recurrent urinary tract infections.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Bacterial infection triggers an inflammatory response leading to pyelonephritis, abscess formation, or interstitial nephritis, resulting in progressive damage to nephrons, impaired renal function, and potential sepsis. Chronic cases may lead to renal fibrosis, hydronephrosis, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓感染症は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症する。細菌感染により炎症反応が誘発され、腎盂腎炎、膿瘍形成、または間質性腎炎を引き起こし、ネフロンの進行性障害、腎機能低下、敗血症の可能性がある。慢性例では腎線維化、水腎症、最終的に腎不全に至ることがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus equuli, and Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, and conditions predisposing to urinary stasis such as recumbency or neurological disorders.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale migrate to or lodge within the renal parenchyma, renal pelvis, or perirenal tissues. The parasites cause direct mechanical damage, granulomatous inflammation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue, potentially leading to nephritis, abscess formation, hydronephrosis, and impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal vasculature can also induce thrombosis and ischemic necrosis of kidney tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質、腎盂、または腎周囲組織に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫は直接的な機械的損傷、肉芽腫性炎症、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こし、腎炎、膿瘍形成、水腎症、および腎機能障害を招く可能性がある。幼虫が腎血管を移行することで血栓症や虚血性壊死を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant migration of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode that can become an opportunistic parasite), migrating larvae of Strongylus vulgaris, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water harboring infective larvae or parasitic stages.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause immune-mediated or direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular and glomerular structures. Viral replication in endothelial cells leads to vasculitis, thrombosis, and ischemic injury to the kidneys, resulting in impaired glomerular filtration and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli may further contribute to progressive renal dysfunction.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管および糸球体構造に免疫介在性または直接的な細胞障害を引き起こします。血管内皮細胞でのウイルス増殖により血管炎、血栓症、腎虚血性障害が生じ、糸球体濾過機能の低下と尿細管壊死をもたらします。糸球体への免疫複合体の沈着がさらに進行性の腎機能障害に寄与する場合があります。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus type 1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially other nephrotrophic viruses that secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune-mediated glomerulonephritis triggered by viral antigen-antibody complex deposition, as well as hemodynamic compromise from systemic viral illness leading to renal hypoperfusion.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial pathogens, commonly Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus spp., Streptococcus spp., or Corynebacterium spp., ascend from the lower urinary tract or spread hematogenously to the kidneys, causing inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma. The resulting pyelonephritis impairs tubular and glomerular function, leading to impaired urine concentration, electrolyte imbalances, and potentially renal failure if left untreated. Chronic infection may lead to fibrosis, nephrolithiasis, and irreversible loss of functional nephrons.
pathophysiology_ja: 大腸菌、アクチノバチルス属、連鎖球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属などの細菌が下部尿路からの上行感染または血行性に腎臓に到達し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎実質の進行性破壊を引き起こす。結果として生じる腎盂腎炎は尿細管および糸球体機能を障害し、尿濃縮能の低下、電解質異常、未治療の場合は腎不全に至る。慢性感染は線維化、腎結石、不可逆的なネフロン喪失を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections (most commonly E. coli), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and urolithiasis causing urinary stasis and secondary infection. Predisposing factors include bladder paralysis, urethral obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and anatomical abnormalities that impair normal urine flow.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, causing granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, leading to progressive nephritis, fungal ball (mycetoma) formation, and impaired renal function.
