causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy. Foaling accidents and riding-related incidents may also contribute to renal trauma.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他の馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、または交通事故による鈍的外傷である。二次的原因には、鋭利な物体による穿通性損傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、または経皮的腎生検時の医原性損傷が含まれる。分娩時の事故や騎乗中の事故も腎外傷の原因となりうる。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as stretching, posturing to urinate frequently, or flank-watching) associated with renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal neoplasia can stimulate visceral pain pathways, leading to behavioral manifestations that mimic colic or musculoskeletal discomfort. Altered electrolyte balance and uremic toxin accumulation may also contribute to neurological and behavioral changes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に関連した異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、側腹部を気にする行動、伸展姿勢など）を伴います。慢性腎炎、腎結石、または腎腫瘍が内臓痛経路を刺激し、疝痛や筋骨格系の不快感に類似した行動症状を引き起こします。電解質バランスの乱れや尿毒素の蓄積も神経学的および行動的変化に寄与する可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure leading to visceral pain. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, renal cysts, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and electrolyte imbalances causing discomfort and behavioral changes.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacterial invasion triggers an inflammatory response leading to nephritis or pyelonephritis, resulting in progressive tubular damage, interstitial inflammation, and impaired renal function. If untreated, chronic infection can lead to abscess formation, fibrosis, and ultimately renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。細菌の侵入により炎症反応が惹起され、腎炎や腎盂腎炎を引き起こし、尿細管障害、間質性炎症、腎機能低下が進行します。未治療の場合、慢性感染により膿瘍形成、線維化、最終的には腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, as well as hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, bladder dysfunction, and catheterization-related contamination that predispose to bacterial colonization of the kidneys.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic invasion causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and potentially vascular thrombosis, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through renal tissue disrupts normal filtration and concentrating ability, and may result in hematuria, proteinuria, and secondary bacterial infection.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管の破壊、間質性腎炎、血管血栓症が生じ、進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こす。幼虫の腎組織内移行により正常な濾過機能および濃縮機能が障害され、血尿、蛋白尿、二次的な細菌感染が生じうる。
causes: Primary causes include infection by parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (a rhabditid nematode), aberrant migration of Strongylus vulgaris larvae through renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Infection occurs through ingestion of larvae from contaminated soil or water, or through wound contamination. Immunosuppression, poor hygiene, and exposure to contaminated environments are predisposing factors.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubules, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and progressive renal dysfunction. Viral replication within endothelial cells of renal vasculature triggers inflammatory infiltration, thrombosis, and ischemic necrosis of renal parenchyma. In severe cases, immune complex deposition in glomeruli contributes to glomerulonephritis and declining renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管内皮細胞で増殖し、血管炎や免疫介在性の糸球体・尿細管障害を引き起こす。ウイルス感染により炎症性細胞浸潤、血栓形成、腎実質の虚血性壊死が生じる。重症例では免疫複合体の糸球体沈着により糸球体腎炎が進行し、腎機能が低下する。
causes: Primary causes include infection with equine herpesvirus (particularly EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally other systemic viral infections that target renal vasculature. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, viral-induced vasculitis leading to ischemic renal injury, and concurrent bacterial superinfection exacerbating renal damage. Predisposing factors include immunosuppression, stress, and co-infections.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or, less commonly, through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. This leads to impaired renal function, potentially resulting in renal failure if bilateral involvement occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 腎臓の細菌感染（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種によって発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。両側性の場合、腎機能障害が進行し腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Proteus spp., Klebsiella spp., Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, urinary catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infection.
causes_ja: 一般的な原因菌には大腸菌、プロテウス属、クレブシエラ属、レンサ球菌属、コリネバクテリウム・レナーレなどがあります。素因として尿路結石、膀胱麻痺、尿道カテーテル留置、免疫抑制、尿停滞を引き起こす疾患があります。雌馬は尿道が短いため上行性感染を起こしやすい傾向があります。

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, tissue destruction, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract allows fungal invasion, often facilitated by immunosuppression or prolonged antibiotic use.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、閉塞や組織壊死、進行性の腎機能低下をもたらします。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染により真菌が侵入し、免疫抑制や長期抗菌薬使用が発症を助長します。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi that invade the kidneys via hematogenous spread or ascending urinary tract infection. Secondary contributing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy disrupting normal flora, immunosuppression (from corticosteroid use, systemic illness, or stress), indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal damage or urinary stasis.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, though hematogenous spread is also possible. Bacterial colonization of the renal pelvis and parenchyma leads to inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Chronic infection can result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染によって発生しますが、血行性の伝播も起こり得ます。腎盂および腎実質への細菌定着により、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が引き起こされます。慢性感染は線維化、腎不全、さらに未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Streptococcus spp., and Klebsiella spp., typically ascending from the lower urinary tract. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and anatomical abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infection.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal nephron function, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often arises from direct toxic or infectious injury.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎（腎臓の炎症）は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫がネフロン機能を障害し、線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は直接的な毒性または感染性障害により発生することが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic drugs such as NSAIDs and aminoglycosides. Secondary causes include immune-mediated diseases, systemic sepsis, dehydration, and exposure to toxic plants or heavy metals. Ascending urinary tract infections and equine purpura hemorrhagica can also contribute to renal inflammation.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported primary renal tumors include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to other organs including lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Tumor growth may cause progressive renal insufficiency, hematuria, and space-occupying effects leading to abdominal discomfort.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂における異常な細胞増殖を伴います。最も一般的に報告される原発性腎腫瘍には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、およびリンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、肺・肝臓・リンパ節などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の増大により進行性の腎機能不全、血尿、および腹部不快感を引き起こすことがあります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown; potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation, and environmental carcinogen exposure. Renal cell carcinoma is the most common primary malignant renal tumor, while nephroblastoma is more frequently reported in younger horses, suggesting possible congenital or developmental origins. Secondary renal involvement may occur via metastasis from lymphoma or other systemic neoplastic diseases.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves dysfunction of the kidneys' ability to properly regulate electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, resulting in metabolic derangements such as hypercalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, or metabolic acidosis. Chronic cases may progress to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary renal failure due to mineral deposition and tubular damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、腎臓による電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄の適切な調節機能の障害を伴う。尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、高カルシウム血症、高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシスなどの代謝異常が引き起こされる。慢性例ではミネラル沈着や尿細管障害により、腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または二次性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include congenital or acquired renal tubular dysfunction, excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants (e.g., oxalate-rich grasses), and vitamin D toxicity. Secondary causes include chronic kidney disease from nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), prolonged dehydration, and systemic conditions such as endotoxemia or leptospirosis that impair renal metabolic function.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, or phosphorus, can impair normal renal tubular function and structural integrity in horses. Chronic imbalances, especially excessive dietary phosphorus relative to calcium, can lead to calcium deposition in renal tissues (nephrocalcinosis) and progressive tubular degeneration. Secondary hyperparathyroidism from calcium-phosphorus imbalance may further exacerbate renal mineralization and impair glomerular and tubular function.
pathophysiology_ja: 特にビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏や不均衡は、馬の腎尿細管機能および構造的完全性を損なう可能性があります。特にカルシウムに対するリンの過剰摂取は、腎組織へのカルシウム沈着（腎石灰化症）および進行性の尿細管変性を引き起こします。カルシウム・リン不均衡による二次性上皮小体機能亢進症が腎臓の石灰化をさらに悪化させ、糸球体および尿細管機能を障害します。
causes: Primary causes include dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (particularly high phosphorus/low calcium diets such as all-grain diets without adequate forage), vitamin A deficiency, and vitamin D deficiency or excess. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., tropical grasses) that bind dietary calcium, and chronic consumption of poor-quality feed lacking essential minerals and vitamins.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and inability to concentrate urine. Specific conditions such as renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease result from abnormal renal development or cyst formation, ultimately causing chronic renal failure. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional renal parenchyma lead to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and accumulation of uremic toxins.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異を伴い、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、および尿濃縮能の低下を引き起こします。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などの特定の疾患は、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成に起因し、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。進行性の線維化と機能的腎実質の喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、および尿毒症性毒素の蓄積が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting renal development or function, which may follow autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns depending on the specific disorder. Specific examples include renal dysplasia reported in certain horse breeds and ectopic cilia-associated renal malformations. Secondary factors such as concurrent infections, dehydration, or nephrotoxic exposures may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane or tubular components. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated attack leads to glomerulonephritis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, and progressive renal tissue destruction. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate renal damage, leading to impaired glomerular filtration and tubular function.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜や尿細管成分を含む腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生します。免疫複合体の沈着や直接的な抗体介在性攻撃により糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が引き起こされ、腎組織の進行性破壊が生じます。補体活性化と炎症細胞浸潤がさらに腎障害を悪化させ、糸球体濾過機能および尿細管機能の低下をもたらします。
causes: The primary cause involves a dysregulated immune response targeting renal self-antigens, potentially triggered by molecular mimicry following infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), chronic inflammatory conditions, or drug reactions. Secondary causes include persistent systemic infections such as equine infectious anemia or Leptospira, which may generate cross-reactive antibodies. Genetic predisposition and concurrent autoimmune disorders may also contribute to disease development.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, reabsorption, and excretion functions. Chronic loss of functional nephrons results in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The condition may be accompanied by renal tubular necrosis and mineralization of renal tissues.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質性線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・再吸収・排泄機能の障害を引き起こす。機能的ネフロンの慢性的な喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、最終的には腎不全に至る。腎尿細管壊死や腎組織の石灰化を伴うこともある。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (such as aminoglycoside antibiotics, NSAIDs, heavy metals, and vitamin D toxicosis), ischemic injury, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, systemic infections, immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, and oxalate-containing plant ingestion (e.g., Oxalis species). Pigment nephropathy from myoglobinuria or hemoglobinuria may also contribute.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the abdomen or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle. This leads to hemorrhage (subcapsular, perirenal, or intra-abdominal), potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum), inflammation, and if severe, compromised renal perfusion resulting in ischemic necrosis. Secondary complications include retroperitoneal abscessation, adhesion formation, and in bilateral or severe unilateral cases, acute renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 腹部または腰部への鈍的もしくは穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管茎に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下、腎周囲、または腹腔内）、尿漏出（尿腹症）、炎症が引き起こされ、重度の場合は腎灌流低下による虚血性壊死が生じる。二次的合併症として後腹膜膿瘍、癒着形成、両側性または重度の片側性損傷では急性腎不全が発生しうる。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collision with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects or surgical complications, and rarely, severe exertion causing renal vascular rupture. Foals may sustain renal injury during dystocia or rough handling.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves chronic renal pain or discomfort stemming from underlying kidney pathology (such as nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or chronic renal failure) that manifests as abnormal behavioral patterns. The persistent nociceptive input from the affected kidney(s) leads to changes in posture, gait, temperament, and performance, as the horse attempts to compensate for or respond to visceral pain. Altered electrolyte balance and uremic toxin accumulation may also contribute to neurological and behavioral changes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、慢性腎不全などの基礎的な腎臓病変に起因する慢性的な腎臓の痛みや不快感が異常な行動パターンとして発現するものである。罹患した腎臓からの持続的な侵害受容入力により、姿勢、歩様、気性、パフォーマンスに変化が生じる。電解質バランスの異常や尿毒症性毒素の蓄積も神経学的・行動学的変化に寄与する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, pyelonephritis, chronic interstitial nephritis, and renal neoplasia causing persistent renal pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, hydronephrosis, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and systemic diseases leading to renal compromise and associated discomfort.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically ascending from the lower urinary tract or via hematogenous spread. Infection leads to inflammation (pyelonephritis), tubular damage, interstitial edema, and abscess formation, which progressively impairs glomerular filtration and tubular function. Chronic cases may result in fibrosis, renal insufficiency, and potential septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生します。感染により炎症（腎盂腎炎）、尿細管障害、間質性浮腫、膿瘍形成が起こり、糸球体濾過機能および尿細管機能が進行性に障害されます。慢性例では線維化、腎不全、さらには敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (commonly Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus equuli) from the lower urinary tract, or hematogenous spread from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, immunosuppression, catheterization, and pre-existing renal damage that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses occurs when parasitic organisms, most commonly Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix) or migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae, invade the renal parenchyma. The parasites cause granulomatous inflammation, tissue destruction, and progressive nephritis, leading to impaired renal function. Vascular damage from larval migration can also result in thrombosis, ischemia, and infarction of renal tissue.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫症は、主にHalicephalobus gingivalis（Halicephalobus deletrix）や普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫などの寄生虫が腎実質に侵入することで発生する。寄生虫は肉芽腫性炎症、組織破壊、進行性腎炎を引き起こし、腎機能障害をもたらす。幼虫の移行による血管損傷は血栓症、虚血、腎組織の梗塞を引き起こすこともある。
causes: Primary causes include infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode capable of opportunistic parasitism), migrating larvae of Strongylus vulgaris through the mesenteric and renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression or compromised health status that facilitates parasitic invasion and establishment in renal tissue.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause systemic vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubules. Viral replication within renal endothelial cells leads to inflammation, thrombosis of renal vasculature, and subsequent ischemic injury resulting in impaired renal filtration and tubular necrosis. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli may further exacerbate renal dysfunction.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが全身性血管炎を引き起こし、腎糸球体および尿細管に免疫介在性障害をもたらします。腎血管内皮細胞でのウイルス増殖により炎症や血栓形成が生じ、虚血性障害による腎濾過機能の低下および尿細管壊死が起こります。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着がさらに腎機能障害を悪化させることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus-1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and potentially equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that compound viral-induced renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common pathogens include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染により発生し、まれに血行性播種によって生じます。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。主な病原菌には大腸菌、レンサ球菌、ブドウ球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urolithiasis), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and contamination during urinary catheterization. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urinary stasis, nephrolithiasis, immunosuppression, bladder dysfunction, and anatomical abnormalities that impair normal urine flow.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or necrotizing inflammation. The infection disrupts normal renal architecture, potentially causing obstruction, abscessation, and progressive loss of renal function. Hematogenous spread from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to fungal nephritis, pyelonephritis, or fungal ball (mycetoma) formation within the renal pelvis.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または壊死性の炎症を引き起こします。感染により正常な腎構造が破壊され、閉塞、膿瘍形成、および進行性の腎機能低下を招く可能性があります。原発巣からの血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により、真菌性腎炎、腎盂腎炎、または腎盂内の真菌球（菌腫）形成に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi, often following immunosuppression due to prolonged antibiotic therapy, corticosteroid use, or debilitating systemic illness. Secondary causes include ascending urinary tract infections, contaminated urinary catheters, and hematogenous dissemination from pulmonary or gastrointestinal fungal infections. Predisposing factors include chronic illness, immunocompromise, and disruption of normal mucosal barriers.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium renale colonize the renal tissue, causing inflammation, abscessation, and progressive destruction of renal parenchyma. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites can also seed the kidneys, leading to suppurative nephritis and impaired renal function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、コリネバクテリウム・レナーレなどの細菌が腎組織に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎実質の進行性破壊を引き起こします。遠隔感染巣からの血行性播種によっても化膿性腎炎が生じ、腎機能障害をきたすことがあります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Actinobacillus spp., Corynebacterium renale) from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis, bladder dysfunction, or urethral obstruction. Secondary causes include hematogenous bacterial spread from systemic infections, immunosuppression, catheterization-related contamination, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that impair urine flow.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious injury to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium, leading to impaired filtration, tubular dysfunction, and progressive loss of nephron function. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, resulting in proteinuria, azotemia, and electrolyte imbalances. Chronic inflammation can progress to fibrosis and irreversible renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の障害により糸球体、尿細管、または間質に炎症が生じ、濾過機能障害や尿細管機能不全、ネフロンの進行性喪失を引き起こします。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、蛋白尿、高窒素血症、電解質異常をもたらします。慢性炎症は線維化に進行し、不可逆的な腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic sepsis, heavy metal exposure, and complications from conditions such as purpura hemorrhagica or endotoxemia.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the uncontrolled proliferation of cells within the kidney, most commonly renal cell carcinoma, lymphoma, or nephroblastoma. The tumor mass disrupts normal renal architecture, impairing filtration, concentrating ability, and endocrine functions of the kidney. Locally invasive tumors may obstruct the ureter or renal vasculature, and metastatic spread can occur to the lungs, liver, and lymph nodes.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎臓内の細胞が無秩序に増殖する疾患であり、腎細胞癌、リンパ腫、腎芽腫が最も多い。腫瘍塊は正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過機能、濃縮能、および内分泌機能を障害する。局所浸潤性腫瘍は尿管や腎血管を閉塞させることがあり、肺、肝臓、リンパ節への転移が起こり得る。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown. Potential contributing factors include genetic predisposition, chronic inflammation or irritation of renal tissue, and exposure to environmental carcinogens. Renal cell carcinoma is the most commonly reported primary renal tumor, while lymphoma may affect the kidney as part of multicentric disease.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves disruption of normal kidney function affecting electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. Impaired renal tubular function leads to abnormal handling of calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate, potentially resulting in metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, hypercalcemia or hypocalcemia, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal tubular acidosis, nephrocalcinosis, or secondary hyperparathyroidism with progressive renal parenchymal damage.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝疾患は、電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、老廃物排泄に影響を及ぼす正常な腎機能の障害を伴う。腎尿細管機能の障害により、カルシウム、リン、重炭酸塩の異常な処理が生じ、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、高カルシウム血症または低カルシウム血症、高窒素血症を引き起こす可能性がある。慢性的な機能障害は、腎尿細管性アシドーシス、腎石灰化症、または続発性副甲状腺機能亢進症を伴う進行性の腎実質障害につながりうる。
causes: Primary causes include excessive dietary calcium or phosphorus imbalances, oxalate-containing plant ingestion (e.g., tropical grasses high in oxalates), and prolonged administration of nephrotoxic drugs such as NSAIDs or aminoglycosides. Secondary causes include chronic dehydration, heavy metal exposure, vitamin D toxicosis, and pre-existing chronic kidney disease leading to disrupted mineral metabolism.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis, tubular degeneration, and progressive renal insufficiency in horses. Imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios (especially excess phosphorus or oxalate ingestion) promote calcium deposition in renal parenchyma, disrupting normal filtration and reabsorption mechanisms. Chronic deficiency states lead to secondary hyperparathyroidism, further exacerbating renal mineralization and fibrosis.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養素の欠乏やシュウ酸を多く含む飼料の摂取は、腎尿細管機能を障害し、腎石灰化症、尿細管変性、進行性腎不全を引き起こします。カルシウムとリンの不均衡（特にリン過剰やシュウ酸摂取）は腎実質へのカルシウム沈着を促進し、正常な濾過・再吸収機能を障害します。慢性的な欠乏状態は二次性副甲状腺機能亢進症を引き起こし、腎の石灰化と線維化をさらに悪化させます。
causes: Primary causes include dietary calcium-phosphorus imbalance (high phosphorus/low calcium diets), excessive consumption of oxalate-containing plants (such as tropical grasses or sorrel), and deficiencies in vitamin A or vitamin D. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of bran-heavy or grain-heavy diets without adequate calcium supplementation, and chronic grazing on oxalate-rich pastures that bind dietary calcium and reduce its bioavailability.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and disrupted electrolyte and fluid homeostasis. Examples include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal renal development or cyst formation results in progressive renal insufficiency and eventual renal failure. Chronic compensatory mechanisms in remaining nephrons ultimately lead to hyperfiltration injury and further deterioration of kidney function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管または糸球体の構造と機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、進行性のネフロン喪失、濾過障害、電解質および体液の恒常性の破綻を引き起こす。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などが含まれ、腎臓の異常発達や嚢胞形成により進行性の腎機能不全から最終的に腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過が二次的な障害を引き起こし、腎機能のさらなる悪化をもたらす。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations (autosomal recessive or dominant) affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function, such as those involved in renal dysplasia or polycystic kidney disease. Secondary factors include consanguineous breeding practices that increase the prevalence of homozygous deleterious alleles within certain horse breeds. Environmental stressors, concurrent infections, or nephrotoxic exposures may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive T-cells directed against renal antigens, leading to immune complex deposition in the glomeruli and/or tubulointerstitial tissues. This triggers complement activation, inflammatory cell infiltration, and progressive glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, resulting in impaired renal function. Chronic immune-mediated damage leads to fibrosis, nephron loss, and eventual renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が腎臓の自己抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性T細胞を産生し、糸球体や尿細管間質組織に免疫複合体が沈着します。これにより補体活性化、炎症細胞浸潤、進行性の糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が引き起こされ、腎機能が障害されます。慢性的な免疫介在性障害は線維化、ネフロンの喪失、最終的に腎不全へと進行します。
causes: Primary causes include dysregulation of immune tolerance leading to autoantibody production against glomerular basement membrane or tubular antigens. Secondary causes may include chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi, equine infectious anemia), drug reactions, or systemic autoimmune conditions that trigger immune complex formation and renal deposition. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to immune dysregulation.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of nephron structure and function, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis. This leads to impaired glomerular filtration, loss of concentrating ability, and accumulation of metabolic waste products (azotemia). Chronic progressive loss of functional renal tissue eventually results in renal insufficiency or failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含むネフロン構造と機能の進行性悪化を伴う。これにより糸球体濾過率の低下、濃縮能の喪失、代謝老廃物の蓄積（高窒素血症）が生じる。機能的腎組織の慢性進行性喪失により、最終的に腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), oxalate-containing plants, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic renal ischemia, recurrent or chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, and systemic diseases such as equine infectious anemia or immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Idiopathic chronic interstitial nephritis is also commonly identified.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or renal vasculature. This results in hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), disruption of normal renal architecture, potential urine leakage (uroperitoneum or retroperitoneal urine accumulation), and inflammatory response. Severe cases may lead to renal ischemia, thrombosis of renal vessels, or secondary infection progressing to abscessation.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性外傷により、腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管系に直接的な損傷が生じる。これにより出血（被膜下血腫または腎周囲血腫）、正常な腎構造の破壊、尿漏出（尿腹症または後腹膜尿貯留）、および炎症反応が引き起こされる。重症例では腎虚血、腎血管血栓症、または二次感染による膿瘍形成に進行する場合がある。
causes: Primary causes include blunt trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating injuries from sharp objects (fencing, stakes), iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy, and fractures of the lumbar transverse processes impinging on the kidney.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that arise secondary to renal pain, inflammation, or dysfunction. Chronic renal disease, nephrolithiasis, or pyelonephritis can cause visceral pain that manifests as behavioral changes including irritability, decreased performance, and altered posture. The pain signals originating from the kidneys are transmitted via splanchnic nerves, leading to referred pain and characteristic behavioral responses.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の痛み、炎症、または機能不全に続発する異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を気にする行動、伸びをする動作など）を伴います。慢性腎疾患、腎結石症、または腎盂腎炎が内臓痛を引き起こし、易刺激性、パフォーマンス低下、姿勢の変化などの行動変化として現れます。腎臓からの痛み信号は内臓神経を介して伝達され、関連痛や特徴的な行動反応を引き起こします。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, pyelonephritis, renal neoplasia, and chronic renal failure causing discomfort. Secondary causes may include ureterolithiasis, renal abscessation, toxic nephropathy (from NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, or heavy metals), and ischemic renal injury. Idiopathic renal pain without identifiable structural lesions has also been reported.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus spp. induce inflammation (pyelonephritis), leading to tubular damage, interstitial edema, abscess formation, and progressive loss of renal function. Chronic infection may result in fibrosis, renal scarring, and eventual renal insufficiency if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発症します。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、アクチノバチルス属などの細菌が炎症（腎盂腎炎）を引き起こし、尿細管障害、間質性浮腫、膿瘍形成、および進行性の腎機能低下をもたらします。慢性感染は線維化、腎瘢痕化を引き起こし、未治療の場合は最終的に腎不全に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp., and Actinobacillus spp.) from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis, bladder dysfunction, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, immunosuppression, and predisposing factors such as urinary stasis, nephrolithiasis, and anatomical abnormalities.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses primarily involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasitic migration causes direct mechanical damage to renal tissue, granulomatous inflammation, fibrosis, and obstruction of renal tubules or vessels, leading to progressive renal dysfunction. Larval migration through the renal arterial supply (particularly with S. vulgaris) can cause thrombosis, infarction, and secondary nephritis.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、主にHalicephalobus gingivalis、普通円虫（Strongylus vulgaris）の幼虫、または腎虫（Dioctophyme renale）などの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・寄生することで発生する。寄生虫の移行により腎組織への直接的な機械的損傷、肉芽腫性炎症、線維化、腎尿細管や血管の閉塞が生じ、進行性の腎機能障害を引き起こす。特にS. vulgarisでは腎動脈への幼虫移行により血栓症、梗塞、二次性腎炎が発生しうる。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infections by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating larvae of Strongylus vulgaris through mesenteric and renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burdens due to inadequate deworming programs, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can target renal vasculature and tubular epithelium, causing immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, vasculitis, and tubular necrosis. Viral replication within renal endothelial cells leads to inflammation, microthrombosis, and impaired glomerular filtration, resulting in progressive renal dysfunction. Immune complex deposition in glomeruli further exacerbates tissue damage and compromises kidney function.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV-1）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎血管や尿細管上皮を標的とし、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎、血管炎、尿細管壊死を引き起こす。腎内皮細胞でのウイルス増殖により炎症、微小血栓形成、糸球体濾過障害が生じ、進行性の腎機能障害をもたらす。糸球体への免疫複合体沈着がさらに組織損傷を悪化させる。
causes: Primary causes include infection with equine herpesvirus-1 (EHV-1), equine arteritis virus (EAV), or other nephrotrophic viruses that directly damage renal tissue. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, systemic vasculitis, dehydration, and concurrent bacterial infections that compound viral-induced renal injury. Immunosuppression and stress may predispose horses to more severe renal involvement.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli, leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染によって発生し、まれに血行性播種によっても起こる。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こす。主な原因菌には大腸菌、連鎖球菌、ブドウ球菌、Corynebacterium renale、Actinobacillus equuliなどがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至る。
causes: Primary causes include ascending urinary tract infections, urolithiasis causing urinary stasis, and hematogenous bacterial dissemination from distant infection sites. Secondary causes include immunosuppression, urinary catheterization, bladder paralysis, anatomical abnormalities, and conditions predisposing to urinary stasis such as recumbency or neurological disease.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or pyogranulomatous inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal mycetomas or fungal concretions within the collecting system. Hematogenous dissemination or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to unilateral or bilateral renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または化膿性肉芽腫性炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、集合系内での真菌腫や真菌性結石の形成が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行性感染により、片側性または両側性の腎障害を引き起こし得る。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi, often secondary to prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, or indwelling urinary catheters. Predisposing factors include chronic debilitation, concurrent systemic illness, corticosteroid use, and disruption of normal urinary tract flora. Environmental exposure to high fungal spore loads may also contribute.

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacteria colonize the renal tissue, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. If bilateral or left untreated, it can lead to chronic renal failure, septicemia, and toxemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発症します。細菌が腎組織に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こします。両側性または未治療の場合、慢性腎不全や敗血症、毒血症に至ることがあります。
causes: The primary cause is ascending bacterial infection, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Corynebacterium renale, Proteus spp., and Streptococcus spp. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, bladder paralysis, catheterization trauma, and immunosuppression. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites can also occur but is less common.
causes_ja: 主な原因は大腸菌、コリネバクテリウム・レナーレ、プロテウス属、レンサ球菌属などによる上行性細菌感染です。素因として尿路結石、尿停滞、膀胱麻痺、カテーテル挿入による外傷、免疫抑制などがあります。遠隔感染巣からの血行性伝播も起こり得ますが、頻度は低いです。

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitial tissue of the kidneys. This leads to impaired filtration, proteinuria, azotemia, and electrolyte imbalances. Chronic inflammation can result in progressive fibrosis, nephron loss, and ultimately renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質組織が損傷される疾患である。これにより濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症、電解質異常が生じる。慢性炎症は進行性の線維化、ネフロン喪失、最終的に腎不全を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), systemic sepsis, dehydration, pigment nephropathy from rhabdomyolysis, and immune complex deposition from chronic infections.
causes_ja: 主な原因には細菌感染（レプトスピラ、連鎖球菌など）、ウイルス感染（馬伝染性貧血など）、免疫介在性糸球体腎炎がある。二次的原因には腎毒性薬物（NSAIDs、アミノグリコシド系）、全身性敗血症、脱水、横紋筋融解症による色素性腎症、慢性感染による免疫複合体沈着が含まれる。

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves the abnormal proliferation of cells within the kidney parenchyma or renal pelvis. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory functions, and potentially metastasize to distant organs such as lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Progressive tumor growth leads to renal dysfunction, paraneoplastic syndromes, and compression or invasion of adjacent structures.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎腫瘍は、腎実質または腎盂内の細胞の異常増殖を伴う。最も一般的に報告される腫瘍は腎細胞癌、腎芽腫（ネフロブラストーマ）、リンパ腫であり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過および排泄機能を障害し、肺・肝臓・リンパ節などの遠隔臓器に転移する可能性がある。腫瘍の進行により腎機能不全、腫瘍随伴症候群、隣接構造の圧迫や浸潤が生じる。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, though spontaneous neoplastic transformation of renal epithelial or embryonal cells is suspected. Genetic predisposition, chronic irritation, and age-related cellular changes may contribute as potential risk factors. No specific infectious, toxic, or environmental cause has been definitively identified in equine species.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and bicarbonate metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, metabolic acidosis or alkalosis, and azotemia. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が障害される病態である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、重炭酸の代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、代謝性アシドーシスまたはアルカローシス、高窒素血症を引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性のネフロン喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic renal failure, nephrotoxin exposure (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, hemodynamic compromise, systemic infections, high-calcium or high-oxalate diets, and age-related renal degeneration. Concurrent conditions such as endotoxemia, rhabdomyolysis, and prolonged NSAID use can predispose horses to renal metabolic dysfunction.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-rich diets, lead to impaired renal tubular function, nephrocalcinosis, or renal tissue degeneration in horses. Chronic imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake can cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tubules, leading to tubular necrosis and progressive renal insufficiency. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may develop, further exacerbating mineral imbalances and renal damage.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取により、腎尿細管機能障害、腎石灰化症、または腎組織の変性が馬に生じる。カルシウム-リン比の慢性的な不均衡やシュウ酸塩の過剰摂取はシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の腎尿細管への沈着を引き起こし、尿細管壊死と進行性の腎不全をもたらす。続発性副甲状腺機能亢進症が発生し、ミネラル不均衡と腎障害がさらに悪化する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include diets deficient in vitamin A, vitamin D, or with imbalanced calcium-phosphorus ratios, as well as excessive consumption of oxalate-containing plants (e.g., Halogeton, Oxalis, tropical grasses high in oxalates). Secondary causes include chronic feeding of high-grain/low-forage diets leading to phosphorus excess, inadequate water intake, and prolonged grazing on nutrient-poor pastures.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and eventual chronic renal failure. Examples include renal dysplasia, polycystic kidney disease, and renal tubular acidosis, where abnormal kidney development or function results from autosomal recessive or dominant gene defects. Progressive fibrosis, tubular degeneration, and loss of concentrating ability lead to azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and uremia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響する遺伝子変異に起因し、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能障害、最終的には慢性腎不全に至ります。腎異形成、多発性嚢胞腎、腎尿細管性アシドーシスなどが含まれ、常染色体劣性または優性の遺伝子異常により腎臓の発達や機能が障害されます。進行性の線維化、尿細管変性、濃縮能の喪失により高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿毒症が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations affecting kidney development or function, which may follow autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance patterns. Specific examples include renal dysplasia (abnormal renal development), polycystic kidney disease, and hereditary nephritis. Breed predisposition has been reported, and consanguineous breeding increases the risk of expression of recessive alleles.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system erroneously targets renal tissues, leading to immune-complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated attack on glomerular and/or tubular structures. This results in progressive glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis with inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of nephron function. Complement activation and infiltration of inflammatory cells further exacerbate renal damage, ultimately leading to chronic kidney disease.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が誤って腎組織を標的とし、免疫複合体の沈着や糸球体・尿細管構造への直接的な抗体介在性攻撃を引き起こします。これにより進行性の糸球体腎炎または尿細管間質性腎炎が生じ、炎症、線維化、ネフロン機能の喪失をもたらします。補体の活性化と炎症細胞の浸潤が腎障害をさらに悪化させ、最終的に慢性腎臓病に至ります。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to autoantibody production against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), viral infections, or drug reactions. Secondary causes include immune-complex deposition associated with equine infectious anemia, systemic lupus-like syndromes, or other chronic inflammatory conditions. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease development.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentrating ability, and electrolyte regulation. Chronic nephron loss triggers compensatory hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons, which paradoxically accelerates further glomerular damage. End-stage disease results in azotemia, uremia, and multi-organ consequences of renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過機能、濃縮能力、電解質調節が障害される。慢性的なネフロン喪失は残存ネフロンの代償性過剰濾過を引き起こし、逆説的にさらなる糸球体障害を促進する。末期には高窒素血症、尿毒症および多臓器障害に至る。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis), ischemic injury, and age-related degenerative changes. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, oxalate-containing plant ingestion (e.g., Oxalis, Halogeton), and systemic diseases such as leptospirosis or equine infectious anemia that impose chronic renal stress.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the kidney results in disruption of the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vascular pedicle, leading to hemorrhage, urine leakage, and subsequent inflammation. The retroperitoneal location of equine kidneys provides some protection, but severe external force (kicks, falls, crush injuries) can cause contusion, laceration, or complete rupture. Secondary complications include perirenal hematoma formation, uroperitoneum if urine leaks into the peritoneal cavity, and potential progression to renal failure if bilateral or if the remaining kidney is compromised.
pathophysiology_ja: 鈍的または穿通性の外傷により腎実質、被膜、または血管茎が損傷し、出血、尿漏出、および続発する炎症が生じます。馬の腎臓は後腹膜に位置するためある程度保護されていますが、蹴り、転倒、圧挫損傷などの強い外力により挫傷、裂傷、または完全破裂が起こり得ます。二次的合併症として腎周囲血腫、尿が腹腔内に漏出した場合の尿腹症、および対側腎の機能不全時の腎不全への進行が挙げられます。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls during exercise or competition, collision with fixed objects, and vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds (e.g., stake injuries, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney) and iatrogenic injury during surgical or percutaneous renal procedures. Predisposing factors include pre-existing renal enlargement (hydronephrosis, neoplasia) which makes the kidney more susceptible to traumatic rupture.

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors (such as frequent posturing to urinate, flank watching, or stretching) that arise secondary to renal pain or dysfunction. Chronic or acute renal pathology—including nephrolithiasis, pyelonephritis, or renal neoplasia—stimulates visceral pain receptors, leading to altered behavior patterns. The resultant discomfort may also cause changes in appetite, performance decline, and intermittent colic-like signs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、腎臓の疼痛や機能障害に続発して異常行動（頻繁な排尿姿勢、脇腹を気にする行動、伸展姿勢など）が生じるものです。腎結石症、腎盂腎炎、腎腫瘍などの急性または慢性の腎病変が内臓痛受容器を刺激し、行動パターンの変化を引き起こします。その結果、食欲低下、パフォーマンスの低下、間欠的な疝痛様症状が認められることがあります。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, renal cysts, pyelonephritis, and renal neoplasia that produce chronic visceral pain. Secondary causes may involve ureterolithiasis, chronic renal failure, or referred pain from adjacent structures causing persistent behavioral changes mimicking other conditions.
causes_ja: 主な原因には、慢性的な内臓痛を引き起こす腎結石症、腎嚢胞、腎盂腎炎、および腎腫瘍が含まれます。二次的原因として、尿管結石、慢性腎不全、または隣接臓器からの関連痛により持続的な行動変化が生じることがあります。

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial invasion of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. This leads to impaired renal function, azotemia, and potential sepsis if untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に侵入することで発生します。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が腎盂および実質に定着し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こします。これにより腎機能障害、高窒素血症、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis, bladder dysfunction, or catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infections, immunosuppression, nephrolithiasis causing urinary stasis, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that predispose to bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma and vasculature. Parasitic infiltration causes granulomatous inflammation, tubular destruction, interstitial nephritis, and progressive renal fibrosis. Larval migration through renal arterial supply can also lead to thrombosis, ischemic injury, and secondary bacterial infections of the kidney.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・寄生することで発症する。寄生虫の侵入により肉芽腫性炎症、尿細管破壊、間質性腎炎、進行性の腎線維化が引き起こされる。幼虫の腎動脈系への移行により血栓症、虚血性障害、および二次的な細菌感染が生じることもある。
causes: Primary causes include parasitic infection by Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode with opportunistic pathogenicity), migrating Strongylus vulgaris larvae through the mesenteric and renal vasculature, and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, poor deworming management, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water sources harboring infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause immune-mediated or direct cytopathic damage to renal tubular epithelial cells and glomeruli, leading to interstitial nephritis, glomerulonephritis, and vasculitis. Immune complex deposition within the renal vasculature and glomerular basement membrane further compromises renal filtration and function. Progressive inflammation may result in acute kidney injury or chronic renal insufficiency if unresolved.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが腎尿細管上皮細胞や糸球体に直接的な細胞障害または免疫介在性の損傷を引き起こし、間質性腎炎、糸球体腎炎、血管炎を生じる。腎血管や糸球体基底膜への免疫複合体の沈着により、腎濾過機能がさらに障害される。炎症が遷延すると急性腎障害や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition, viral-induced vasculitis, and hemodynamic compromise from systemic illness leading to renal ischemia.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, causing inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp., leading to impaired renal function if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、主に下部尿路からの上行性感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊を引き起こします。一般的な原因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、レンサ球菌属、コリネバクテリウム属などがあり、未治療の場合は腎機能障害に至ります。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), often associated with urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, or urinary catheterization. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from distant infection sites (e.g., respiratory infections, endocarditis, umbilical infections in foals), immunosuppression, and structural abnormalities of the urinary tract that promote bacterial colonization.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma, pelvis, or ureters, leading to granulomatous or pyogranulomatous inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) that may obstruct urine flow. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can initiate the disease process.
pathophysiology_ja: Aspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質、腎盂、または尿管に定着し、肉芽腫性または化膿肉芽腫性炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、および尿流を閉塞する真菌塊（ファンガルボール）の形成が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染により発症する。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other pathogenic fungi that invade the renal tissue. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, corticosteroid use, indwelling urinary catheters, and pre-existing renal disease. Secondary bacterial infections often complicate the condition.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属などの日和見真菌による腎組織への感染である。長期抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制状態、コルチコステロイド使用、留置カテーテル、既存の腎疾患が素因となる。二次的な細菌感染がしばしば合併する。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract through the ureters to the renal pelvis and parenchyma. Bacterial colonization triggers an inflammatory response leading to neutrophilic infiltration, tubular damage, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of renal tissue. If untreated, chronic infection can result in fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由して腎盂および腎実質へ細菌が上行性に感染することで発生します。細菌の定着により炎症反応が誘発され、好中球浸潤、尿細管障害、膿瘍形成、腎組織の進行性破壊が生じます。未治療の場合、慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害、さらには敗血症を引き起こす可能性があります。
causes: The primary cause is ascending bacterial infection, most commonly by Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and conditions causing urinary stasis. Hematogenous spread from distant infection sites can also occur, though less commonly.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious processes that damage the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys, leading to impaired filtration, proteinuria, and azotemia. Inflammatory cell infiltration and edema disrupt normal renal architecture, potentially progressing to fibrosis and chronic renal insufficiency. Glomerulonephritis may result from immune complex deposition, while tubulointerstitial nephritis often arises from ascending infections or toxic insults.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の過程により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が損傷を受け、濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症を引き起こす。炎症細胞の浸潤と浮腫が正常な腎構造を破壊し、線維化や慢性腎不全に進行する可能性がある。糸球体腎炎は免疫複合体の沈着により、尿細管間質性腎炎は上行性感染や毒性物質により生じることが多い。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., Leptospira, Streptococcus equi), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and nephrotoxic agents such as NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, and heavy metals. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from chronic infections, equine purpura hemorrhagica, and systemic inflammatory conditions. Ascending urinary tract infections and hemodynamic compromise due to dehydration or endotoxemia may also contribute.

name: Renal Neoplasia (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal neoplasia in horses involves abnormal, uncontrolled cellular proliferation within the kidney parenchyma or surrounding tissues. The most commonly reported types include renal cell carcinoma, nephroblastoma, and lymphoma, which can disrupt normal renal architecture, impair filtration and excretory function, and potentially metastasize to other organs such as lungs, liver, and lymph nodes. Progressive tumor growth leads to compression of normal renal tissue, hematuria, and eventually renal insufficiency if bilateral or sufficiently advanced.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓腫瘍は、腎実質または周囲組織における異常な細胞増殖を伴います。最も一般的に報告される種類には腎細胞癌、腎芽腫、リンパ腫があり、正常な腎構造を破壊し、濾過・排泄機能を障害し、肺、肝臓、リンパ節などへ転移する可能性があります。腫瘍の進行性増大により正常腎組織の圧迫、血尿、そして最終的には腎不全に至ることがあります。
causes: The exact etiology of renal neoplasia in horses is largely unknown, and no specific genetic, infectious, or environmental risk factors have been definitively established. Sporadic mutations in renal tubular or embryonal cells are presumed to underlie tumor development. Age-related cellular changes may predispose older horses, although nephroblastoma is more commonly seen in younger animals.

name: Renal Metabolic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal metabolic disease in horses involves impaired kidney function leading to disrupted electrolyte balance, acid-base homeostasis, and waste product excretion. The kidneys fail to adequately regulate calcium, phosphorus, and other mineral metabolism, potentially resulting in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia, azotemia, and metabolic acidosis. Chronic dysfunction can lead to renal secondary hyperparathyroidism, soft tissue mineralization, and progressive nephron loss.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎代謝性疾患は、腎機能障害により電解質バランス、酸塩基平衡、および老廃物排泄が損なわれる疾患である。腎臓がカルシウム、リン、その他のミネラル代謝を適切に調節できなくなり、高カルシウム血症や高リン血症、高窒素血症、代謝性アシドーシスを引き起こす。慢性的な機能障害は腎性二次性上皮小体機能亢進症、軟部組織の石灰化、進行性のネフロン喪失につながる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic kidney disease (CKD), nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals), and nephrolithiasis. Secondary causes include dehydration, systemic infections, leptospirosis, excessive dietary calcium or oxalate-containing plants, and prolonged hemodynamic compromise leading to ischemic renal injury.

name: Renal Nutritional Deficiency (Horse)
pathophysiology: Nutritional deficiencies, particularly of vitamin A, vitamin D, calcium, phosphorus, or oxalate-containing plant ingestion, can impair renal tubular function and lead to nephrocalcinosis or tubular degeneration in horses. Imbalances in calcium-phosphorus ratios or excessive oxalate intake cause calcium oxalate crystal deposition in renal tubules, leading to progressive tubular necrosis and interstitial fibrosis. Chronic deficiency states may also impair renal blood flow and glomerular filtration, resulting in progressive renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: ビタミンA、ビタミンD、カルシウム、リンなどの栄養欠乏やシュウ酸含有植物の摂取により、腎尿細管機能が障害され、腎石灰化症や尿細管変性が生じる。カルシウム・リン比の不均衡や過剰なシュウ酸摂取はシュウ酸カルシウム結晶の腎尿細管への沈着を引き起こし、進行性の尿細管壊死および間質線維化をもたらす。慢性的な欠乏状態は腎血流量および糸球体濾過率を低下させ、進行性の腎不全を引き起こす可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include dietary deficiencies of calcium, phosphorus, vitamin A, or vitamin D, as well as excessive intake of oxalate-rich plants (e.g., Oxalis, Halogeton, sorrel) that bind calcium and deposit oxalate crystals in the kidneys. Secondary causes include prolonged feeding of high-grain, low-forage diets causing calcium-phosphorus imbalance, or chronic selenium or potassium deficiency affecting renal cellular integrity.

name: Renal Genetic Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal genetic disorders in horses involve inherited mutations affecting renal tubular or glomerular structure and function, leading to progressive nephron loss, impaired filtration, and eventual chronic renal failure. Specific conditions include renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease, where abnormal development or cyst formation disrupts normal renal architecture. Progressive fibrosis and loss of functional nephrons result in azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and impaired urine concentrating ability.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓遺伝性疾患は、腎尿細管や糸球体の構造・機能に影響を与える遺伝子変異に起因し、ネフロンの進行性喪失、濾過機能障害、最終的に慢性腎不全に至ります。腎異形成や多発性嚢胞腎などの特定の疾患では、異常な発達や嚢胞形成が正常な腎構造を破壊します。進行性の線維化と機能的ネフロンの喪失により、高窒素血症、電解質異常、尿濃縮能の低下が生じます。
causes: The primary cause is inherited genetic mutations, often autosomal recessive, affecting genes responsible for normal renal development and function. Renal dysplasia and polycystic kidney disease are among the recognized hereditary renal conditions in horses. Secondary factors such as dehydration, concurrent infections, or nephrotoxic exposure may accelerate the progression of underlying genetic renal disease.

name: Renal Autoimmune Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: The immune system produces autoantibodies or autoreactive lymphocytes directed against renal antigens, including glomerular basement membrane components or tubular epithelial cells. Immune complex deposition or direct antibody-mediated injury leads to glomerulonephritis or tubulointerstitial nephritis, causing progressive inflammation, fibrosis, and loss of renal function. Complement activation and inflammatory cell infiltration further exacerbate tissue damage and impair glomerular filtration.
pathophysiology_ja: 免疫系が糸球体基底膜成分や尿細管上皮細胞などの腎抗原に対する自己抗体または自己反応性リンパ球を産生します。免疫複合体の沈着や抗体を介した直接的な障害により糸球体腎炎や尿細管間質性腎炎が生じ、進行性の炎症、線維化、腎機能低下を引き起こします。補体活性化および炎症性細胞浸潤がさらに組織障害を悪化させ、糸球体濾過を障害します。
causes: The primary cause is immune dysregulation leading to loss of self-tolerance against renal antigens, potentially triggered by chronic infections (e.g., Streptococcus equi), viral infections, or drug reactions. Secondary causes include immune complex deposition from systemic autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus-like syndromes, equine infectious anemia, or other chronic inflammatory diseases. Genetic predisposition and environmental factors may also contribute to disease development.

name: Renal Degenerative Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal degenerative disease in horses involves progressive deterioration of renal parenchyma, including tubular degeneration, interstitial fibrosis, and glomerulosclerosis, leading to impaired filtration, concentration, and excretion functions. Chronic insult results in nephron loss, azotemia, electrolyte imbalances, and eventual renal failure. The progressive nature leads to irreversible structural damage with compensatory hypertrophy of remaining nephrons until decompensation occurs.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎変性疾患は、尿細管変性、間質線維化、糸球体硬化症を含む腎実質の進行性劣化を伴い、濾過・濃縮・排泄機能の障害を引き起こす。慢性的な障害によりネフロンの喪失、高窒素血症、電解質異常が生じ、最終的に腎不全に至る。残存ネフロンの代償性肥大が起こるが、進行すると代償不全となる。
causes: Primary causes include chronic exposure to nephrotoxins (aminoglycosides, NSAIDs, heavy metals, vitamin D toxicosis, oak or acorn ingestion), chronic ischemia, and age-related degeneration. Secondary causes include chronic pyelonephritis, nephrolithiasis, prolonged dehydration, systemic diseases such as leptospirosis, and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Idiopathic renal degeneration is also recognized in older horses.

name: Renal Traumatic Injury (Horse)
pathophysiology: Blunt or penetrating trauma to the flank or lumbar region causes direct damage to the renal parenchyma, capsule, or vasculature. This results in hemorrhage (subcapsular or perirenal hematoma), potential urine leakage into the retroperitoneal space, and subsequent inflammation. Severe cases may lead to renal ischemia, nephron loss, or life-threatening hemorrhage if major renal vessels are disrupted.
pathophysiology_ja: 腰部や側腹部への鈍的または穿通性の外傷が腎実質、腎被膜、または腎血管に直接的な損傷を引き起こします。これにより出血（被膜下または腎周囲血腫）、後腹膜腔への尿漏出、およびそれに続く炎症が生じます。重症例では腎虚血、ネフロンの喪失、または主要腎血管の損傷による致命的な出血に至る可能性があります。
causes: Primary causes include blunt abdominal trauma from kicks by other horses, falls, collisions with fixed objects, or vehicular accidents. Secondary causes include penetrating wounds from sharp objects, fractured ribs lacerating the kidney, or iatrogenic injury during percutaneous renal biopsy or surgical procedures.
causes_ja: 主な原因は、他の馬からの蹴り、転倒、固定物への衝突、または車両事故による腹部への鈍的外傷です。二次的原因には、鋭利物による穿通傷、肋骨骨折による腎臓の裂傷、経皮的腎生検や外科的処置中の医原性損傷が含まれます。

name: Renal Behavioral Disorder (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal behavioral disorder in horses involves abnormal behaviors associated with chronic renal pain or dysfunction, where persistent nociceptive signals from diseased kidneys alter the horse's normal behavioral patterns. Chronic renal inflammation, nephrolithiasis, or renal insufficiency can cause visceral pain that manifests as flank sensitivity, postural changes, altered urination patterns, and behavioral abnormalities such as irritability or reluctance to work. The disorder reflects the interplay between progressive renal pathology and the horse's behavioral response to chronic discomfort.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎行動障害は、慢性的な腎臓の疼痛や機能不全に関連する異常行動を伴い、病変のある腎臓からの持続的な侵害受容信号が馬の正常な行動パターンを変化させます。慢性腎炎、腎結石症、または腎不全による内臓痛が、側腹部の過敏性、姿勢の変化、排尿パターンの異常、易刺激性や運動拒否などの行動異常として現れます。この障害は、進行性の腎病変と慢性的な不快感に対する馬の行動反応の相互作用を反映しています。
causes: Primary causes include nephrolithiasis, chronic nephritis, renal neoplasia, pyelonephritis, and renal cysts that produce persistent visceral pain. Secondary causes may include urinary tract obstruction, chronic dehydration, nephrotoxic drug exposure (e.g., NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), and metabolic imbalances leading to progressive renal damage and associated behavioral changes.

name: Renal Infectious Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infectious disease in horses involves bacterial colonization of the renal parenchyma, typically via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract or hematogenous spread. Bacteria such as Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and Actinobacillus equuli invade the renal tissue, causing inflammation (pyelonephritis), abscessation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. This leads to impaired renal filtration, tubular dysfunction, and potentially acute or chronic renal failure if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症は、下部尿路からの上行性感染または血行性播種により細菌が腎実質に定着することで発生する。大腸菌、連鎖球菌、Actinobacillus equuliなどの細菌が腎組織に侵入し、炎症（腎盂腎炎）、膿瘍形成、ネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こす。これにより腎濾過機能障害、尿細管機能不全が生じ、未治療の場合は急性または慢性腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infections (most commonly E. coli, Streptococcus spp., Corynebacterium spp.) from the lower urinary tract, often associated with urolithiasis, bladder paralysis, or urethral obstruction. Secondary causes include hematogenous spread from systemic infections (e.g., strangles, neonatal septicemia with Actinobacillus equuli), immunosuppression, and predisposing anatomical abnormalities or catheterization.

name: Renal Parasitic Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal parasitic disease in horses involves migration and colonization of parasites such as Halicephalobus gingivalis (Halicephalobus deletrix), Strongylus vulgaris larvae, or Dioctophyme renale within the renal parenchyma or vasculature. Parasite migration causes direct tissue destruction, granulomatous inflammation, vasculitis, and progressive nephritis, leading to impaired renal function. Larval migration through renal arteries (particularly S. vulgaris) can cause thromboembolic infarction and ischemic damage to the kidneys.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎寄生虫疾患は、Halicephalobus gingivalis、Strongylus vulgarisの幼虫、またはDioctophyme renaleなどの寄生虫が腎実質や血管系に移行・定着することで発症する。寄生虫の移行により直接的な組織破壊、肉芽腫性炎症、血管炎、進行性の腎炎が引き起こされ、腎機能障害に至る。特にS. vulgarisの幼虫が腎動脈を通過する際に血栓塞栓性梗塞や虚血性腎障害を引き起こすことがある。
causes: Primary causes include aberrant larval migration of Strongylus vulgaris through mesenteric and renal vasculature, infection with Halicephalobus gingivalis (a free-living nematode capable of opportunistic tissue invasion), and rarely Dioctophyme renale (giant kidney worm). Secondary causes include immunosuppression, heavy parasite burden due to inadequate deworming, and environmental exposure to contaminated soil or water containing infective larvae.

name: Renal Viral Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Viral agents such as equine herpesvirus (EHV) or equine arteritis virus (EAV) can cause vasculitis and immune-mediated damage to renal glomeruli and tubules, leading to impaired renal filtration, tubular necrosis, and progressive nephritis. Immune complex deposition in renal vasculature and direct viral cytopathic effects contribute to inflammation, edema, and compromised renal perfusion, potentially resulting in acute or chronic renal insufficiency.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬ヘルペスウイルス（EHV）や馬動脈炎ウイルス（EAV）などのウイルスが血管炎や免疫介在性の糸球体・尿細管障害を引き起こし、腎濾過機能の低下、尿細管壊死、進行性腎炎をもたらす。腎血管への免疫複合体の沈着やウイルスの直接的な細胞障害効果により、炎症・浮腫・腎灌流障害が生じ、急性または慢性の腎不全に至る可能性がある。
causes: Primary causes include systemic viral infections such as equine herpesvirus (EHV-1, EHV-4), equine arteritis virus (EAV), and occasionally equine infectious anemia virus (EIAV) that secondarily affect the kidneys. Secondary factors include immunosuppression, concurrent bacterial infections, dehydration, and pre-existing renal compromise that exacerbate viral-induced renal damage.

name: Renal Bacterial Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Bacterial infection of the kidneys (pyelonephritis) in horses typically occurs via ascending infection from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly through hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, triggering an inflammatory response that leads to tissue destruction, abscess formation, and progressive impairment of renal function. Common causative organisms include Escherichia coli, Actinobacillus equuli, Streptococcus spp., and Corynebacterium spp.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎臓細菌感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路からの上行性感染により発生し、まれに血行性に波及する。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症反応を引き起こして組織破壊、膿瘍形成、腎機能の進行性障害をもたらす。主な起因菌には大腸菌、Actinobacillus equuli、Streptococcus属、Corynebacterium属などがある。
causes: Primary causes include ascending bacterial infection from the lower urinary tract (cystitis, urethritis), hematogenous spread from distant infection sites, and direct contamination following urinary tract catheterization or obstruction. Secondary causes and predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary stasis, immunosuppression, nephrolithiasis, and anatomical abnormalities that impair normal urine flow.

name: Renal Fungal Disease (Horse)
pathophysiology: Fungal organisms, most commonly Aspergillus spp. or Candida spp., colonize the renal parenchyma and/or renal pelvis, leading to granulomatous or pyogranulomatous inflammation. This results in progressive destruction of renal tissue, impaired renal function, and potential formation of fungal masses (fungal balls) that may obstruct urine flow. Hematogenous dissemination from a primary site or ascending infection from the lower urinary tract can lead to renal involvement.
pathophysiology_ja: 主にAspergillus属やCandida属などの真菌が腎実質や腎盂に定着し、肉芽腫性または化膿性肉芽腫性炎症を引き起こす。これにより腎組織の進行性破壊、腎機能障害、および尿流を閉塞しうる真菌塊（ファンガルボール）の形成が生じる。血行性播種または下部尿路からの上行感染により腎臓が侵される。
causes: Primary causes include opportunistic fungal infections by Aspergillus spp., Candida spp., or other environmental fungi. Predisposing factors include prolonged antibiotic therapy, immunosuppression, indwelling urinary catheters, debilitation, and concurrent systemic illness that compromises immune defenses.
causes_ja: 主な原因はAspergillus属、Candida属、その他の環境真菌による日和見感染である。長期間の抗菌薬投与、免疫抑制状態、留置尿道カテーテル、衰弱、および免疫防御を低下させる併発疾患が素因となる。

name: Renal Infection (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal infection (pyelonephritis) in horses typically results from ascending bacterial infection via the ureters from the lower urinary tract, or less commonly from hematogenous spread. Bacteria colonize the renal pelvis and parenchyma, triggering inflammation, abscess formation, and progressive destruction of nephrons. Chronic infection can lead to fibrosis, impaired renal function, and potentially septicemia if left untreated.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎感染症（腎盂腎炎）は、通常、下部尿路から尿管を経由した上行性細菌感染、またはまれに血行性播種により発生します。細菌が腎盂および腎実質に定着し、炎症、膿瘍形成、およびネフロンの進行性破壊を引き起こします。慢性感染は線維化、腎機能障害を招き、未治療の場合は敗血症に至る可能性があります。
causes: The most common causative agents include Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., Staphylococcus spp., Corynebacterium renale, and Actinobacillus equuli. Predisposing factors include urolithiasis, urinary tract obstruction, bladder paralysis, catheterization, immunosuppression, and congenital urinary tract abnormalities. Mares may be more susceptible due to their shorter urethra facilitating ascending infections.

name: Renal Inflammation (Horse)
pathophysiology: Renal inflammation (nephritis) in horses involves immune-mediated or infectious damage to the glomeruli, tubules, or interstitium of the kidneys. This leads to impaired filtration, proteinuria, azotemia, and electrolyte imbalances. Prolonged inflammation can result in fibrosis, progressive nephron loss, and eventual renal failure.
pathophysiology_ja: 馬の腎炎は、免疫介在性または感染性の機序により糸球体、尿細管、または間質が障害される疾患である。これにより濾過機能の低下、蛋白尿、高窒素血症、電解質異常が生じる。炎症が持続すると線維化やネフロンの進行性喪失を引き起こし、最終的に腎不全に至る。
causes: Primary causes include bacterial infections (e.g., leptospirosis, streptococcal infections), viral infections (e.g., equine infectious anemia), and immune-mediated glomerulonephritis. Secondary causes include nephrotoxic drugs (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides), heavy metals, systemic sepsis, and dehydration leading to ischemic renal injury.
